documents.t: A balance adjustment adds coins to, or removes coins from, a viewer's wallet: a goodwill credit after an outage, or a correction. Every adjustment is a new ledger row with a reason the viewer sees in their coin history. Large ones need a second member to approve. Permission area: Balance adjustments View See requests Edit Make, approve and decline adjustments

Open the viewer on Admin Panel›Audience›Users and choose Adjust balance. Choose Paid or Bonus coins, Add or Remove, and the Amount (whole coins). For bonus coins, an optional Bonus expiry. Empty uses the region's bonus expiry (7 days by default). Write the Reason the viewer sees, such as Goodwill credit for the playback outage on 24 October. It becomes the label in their coin history. Optionally add an Internal note that never leaves the panel. Choose Adjust balance. Removing coins can never take the balance below zero. Up to the approval limit (1,000 coins by default, in Admin Panel›Settings›Payments›Balance adjustments), the change is applied at once. Above it, the request waits as Pending until another member approves it.

your-domain.com/admin/balance-adjustments 123456 1Requests by statusAll, Pending (waiting for a second member), Applied and Declined. 2UserWho the coins are for. 3ChangeThe coins added or removed, and when bonus coins expire. 4Reason the user seesShown in their coin history. 5Requested byWho asked for it, and when. 6StatusA second member with Balance adjustments (Edit) approves or declines it. Balance adjustments filtered to Pending: a request over the approval limit waiting for a second member. Members with Balance adjustments (Edit) get a bell notification when a request waits for them. Four eyes Nobody can approve their own request, the Owner included. A member also can't approve a request from the person who added them to the team. This keeps one person from moving large amounts of coins alone. Every request, approval and decline is in the audit log.

Push sends a notification to viewers' phones: to all viewers, or to the followers of one title. Every push also lands in the app's notification inbox. Automatic pushes (new episode drops, replies, VIP renewal reminders) are sent by eDrama itself; this screen is for the messages your team writes. Permission area: Push View See sent and scheduled pushes Edit Compose, send, schedule, test and cancel your-domain.com/admin/push 123456789 1AudienceAll viewers, or a title’s followers (then pick the title). 2KindNews & drops, or Offer. Viewers choose which kinds they receive. 3TitleUp to 65 characters. 4BodyUp to 178 characters. 5Other languagesOptional translations; empty uses your default text. 6OpensA title, an episode, the Wallet or VIP. 7Lock-screen previewHow the push looks on a phone. 8Send pushGoes out within minutes, or schedule it for a time. 9Test sendTo the devices of the app account signed in with your email. The New push composer open over the Push list, with the lock-screen preview.

Choose New push. Audience: All viewers or A title's followers (then pick a live title; the reach updates). Kind: News & drops: pushed to viewers with Drop alerts on. Offer: pushed only to viewers with Offers on. Everyone in the audience also finds it in their inbox. Title (up to 65 characters), such as E24 drops tonight at 8, and Body (up to 178), such as Ava faces the board. You asked to be reminded. Optional translations per app language; empty uses your default text. Opens: a title, an episode of it, the Wallet or VIP. Send: Now, or At a time (in the default region's time zone). Check the lock-screen preview, then choose Test send (optional) and Send push or Schedule push.

Test send goes to the devices of the app account signed in with your email. Sign in to the app on your phone with the same email as your Studio account and allow notifications first. If your devices refuse the test, open the app once so it registers again.

At most 3 pushes per viewer per day (default), counting automatic ones. Pushes above the cap wait for the next day; the inbox still gets every message. Quiet hours 23:00–08:00 in each viewer's own time (default). Pushes wait until quiet hours end. Money notices are never marketing. Change these in Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications. Pushes need the Firebase keys there too; without them the panel says pushes aren't set up.

The list shows every push, newest first, with status cards for Scheduled, Sent, Canceled and Failed. Reach reads "sent of targeted", then how many are waiting (quiet hours or the cap) and how many failed. Results refresh every minute for two days. A scheduled push can be cancelled until it starts going out.

Viewers send requests from App›Me›Help & refunds. Each one arrives here as a ticket. You reply by email (from your own mailbox), then record where the ticket stands. Permission area: Support tickets View See tickets Edit Change status and notes your-domain.com/admin/support-tickets 12345 1Tickets by statusAll tickets, Open, Pending, Resolved and Closed. 2TicketIts reference (the viewer was given it) and topic. 3MessageWhat the viewer wrote. Open the ticket for the purchase, app version and team notes. 4Reply toThe email the viewer asked you to answer. 5StatusOpen, Pending, Resolved or Closed. Support tickets with their topic, message, reply-to email and status.

Topic in the app Arrives as A refund Refund Coins didn't arrive Missing coins Video or playback Playback My account Account Something else Something else For refund and missing-coins requests, the viewer can pick which purchase it's about; the ticket links to it.

Open the ticket. You see the viewer (or "No account"), the purchase, the app version, and the message. Reply to the viewer from your support mailbox, to the Reply to address. Set the Status and add Team notes (viewers never see them), then Save. Status Use it for Open New, waiting for a first look. Pending Waiting on someone: the viewer, a store, a developer. Resolved Answered. Closed Nothing more to do. The app promises a reply within 24 hours (change it with EDRAMA_SUPPORT_REPLY_HOURS). Members who can see tickets get a bell notification for each new one. For a refund, open the purchase from the ticket and follow Transactions › Refund.

Users are your app's viewers. Find anyone by name, email, phone, user ID or a store order ID, and open their page to see everything about their account. Permission area: Users View See users (contact details masked) Edit See full contact details, grant episodes, change region, ban and unban your-domain.com/admin/users 12345678 1TabsAll, VIP, Payers, Free, Creators, Guests and Banned. 2SearchName, email, phone, user ID or store order ID. 3FilterBy region. 4A userName and user ID, or “Guest”. Email and phone are masked without Users (Edit). 5Sign-inGuest, Google, Apple, phone or email. 6CoinsPaid and bonus coins now. 7StatusActive, Banned or deleted. 8OpenThe user’s page: wallet and ledger, unlocks, purchases, VIP, progress and activity. Users on the All tab: sign-in method, region, joined, last active, coins, lifetime spend and status.

Email or phone: type it in full: search finds an exact match (contact details are stored encrypted, so partial matches aren't possible). User ID: the number on their page. Store order ID: the Google Play or App Store order from a receipt the viewer sent you. Name: the start of their name. Only the first matches are shown; type more to narrow it down. Privacy Email addresses and phone numbers are masked unless you have Users (Edit), and each time someone sees them in full it's recorded in the audit log ("Viewed users' contact details").

The top shows the user at a glance: balance, lifetime spend, VIP (and until when), unlocks, last active and sign-in method, plus their user ID, Firebase ID, devices and, if they're also a creator, their creator name. Tab What's there Wallet & ledger Total, paid and bonus coins (bonus is spent first; when the next bonus coins expire), and a reconcile check that the balance equals the sum of its ledger rows. Then the ledger: every coin movement, newest first, with the balance after it. Open a row's Details to see what the viewer sees, who made it, and what it was for (the purchase, unlock, refund or Series Pass). Unlocks Every episode they can watch and how: coins, ad, Series Pass, VIP, free or grant, with coins used. Purchases Coin pack purchases with store, product, amount, coins credited (paid + bonus), status and the receipt check. VIP Every subscription: plan, store, status, next charge, auto-renew and start date. Progress Where they stopped in each episode, and whether they finished it. Activity Sign-ins (time, method, device, IP address) and devices (platform, app version, OS version, last seen). note Ledger rows are never edited or deleted. A correction is always a new row. If a wallet doesn't reconcile, nothing is changed: report it to your developer.

Action Permission What it does Adjust balance Balance adjustments (Edit) Adds or removes paid or bonus coins with a reason the viewer sees. Over the approval limit, a second member must approve. See Balance adjustments. Grant episode Users (Edit) Gives access to released episodes of a live title with no coins moving and no revenue share, for example after a playback outage. Episodes already unlocked are skipped. Needs a reason. Change region Users (Edit) Moves the viewer to another active region: coin packs, VIP plans and prices follow it from their next app start. Their coins, purchases, unlocks, Series Passes and locked prices stay as they are. A viewer who has paid needs the extra tick Move a viewer who has paid. Ban account Users (Edit) Their sign-in stops working at once; the app stops working for them on their next request. Purchases, ledger and unlocks stay. Needs a reason. Unban account Users (Edit) They can sign in again with everything they had. Needs a reason.

A guest is a viewer who hasn't signed in (shown as "Guest #1234"). Guests get the welcome bonus and can watch and earn, but must sign in to buy coins or VIP. When a guest signs in, their history and coins merge into the account; the guest's page then says Merged into with a link.
Viewers can delete their account in the app. Their comment and review text, support ticket contact details and report text are removed. The page shows Account deleted.

AI usage shows what AI Studio produced this month: images and video takes, by creator and for the team, with the estimated cost and whose Gemini key paid: the platform's or the creator's own. your-domain.com/admin/ai-usage 1234 1Usage by creatorWhat each creator made this month. 2ProblemsCalls that failed, were blocked or ended unknown. 3The platform’s keySpent this month against its cap, and the team studio’s part. 4Creators this monthImages, takes, estimated cost, and how much was on their own key or the platform’s. AI usage for the current month on the Usage by creator tab.

Estimates use the prices set in Admin Panel›Settings›AI Studio›Prices for estimates. Google's own bill is the final word. On the platform's key means your company paid; on their own key means the creator paid Google directly. Unknown calls are ones where the answer from Google was lost after the request was sent: they may already be on the bill. To change who pays, the monthly caps and per-creator allowances, see AI Studio settings. To allow or block AI Studio for one creator, use AI Studio on their row in Creators.

Viewers comment on episodes and rate and review series in the app. Comments & reviews is where your team checks what was reported, approves what was held, removes what breaks the rules and replies. Permission area: Comments & reviews View See posts Edit Approve, keep, remove, restore and reply your-domain.com/admin/comments-and-reviews 12345678 1Comments, Reviews, LikesThree tabs. 2StatesAll, Needs attention, Reported, Held and Removed. 3A commentThe viewer, the text, where it was posted and when. 4Why it’s heldBlocked word, link, phone number or spam. 5StatusHeld, Reported, Visible or Removed. 6ApproveA held comment now shows in the app. 7RemoveHides it from everyone but its author; can be restored. 8ReplyReply as the team; the viewer gets a notification. Comments & reviews on the Comments tab, with held comments waiting for a decision.

A post is held automatically (only its author sees it, marked "Waiting for a quick check before others see it") when it contains: a word or phrase from your comment blocklist (Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Comment blocklist), a link, a phone number or long run of digits, text that looks like spam (such as many repeated characters).

Action What it does Approve A held post now shows in the app. Keep A reported post stays; its reports are closed. Remove Viewers stop seeing it (its author still does). Reports are closed. Add an optional note for the audit log; the viewer doesn't see it. Restore A removed post shows again. Reply (comments) Your reply joins the thread in the app under the app's name, marked Team, and the viewer gets a notification. Reply (reviews) One public reply under the review, from the team. It replaces a reply the creator wrote. Leave it empty to remove the reply. Who liked On the Likes tab: the newest likes of an episode. If two people act on the same post at once, the second is told someone already decided it.

A viewer can rate a series once they've reached episode 3. The score shown is a weighted average, so a handful of 5-star ratings can't outrank a series with thousands of ratings. Viewers can mark a review helpful, flag a comment as a spoiler, and report posts. Creators can reply to reviews and comments on their own series from the Creator Portal; those replies show with a Creator badge. See Comments & reviews in the Creator Portal. Comments and reviews can each be switched off for everyone in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Features.
documents.s: Ratings and reviews in the app

documents.t: Creators are invited people or studios who publish their own series through the Creator Portal and earn a share of everything their series make: coins, Series Passes, ads and VIP. This screen is where you invite them, decide applications and manage their agreements. Permission area: Creators View See creators and applications Edit Invite, accept, decline, suspend, reactivate and change shares your-domain.com/admin/creators 12345678 1Invite creatorSends an invite email with a link to the Creator Portal. 2Invite from a fileInvite many creators from a CSV or Excel file. 3Creators / ApplicationsYour creators, and the “Become a creator” applications. 4Status cardsAll creators, Active, Invited and Suspended. 5A creatorName, handle and verified tick. 6ShareTheir revenue share of what their series earn. 7Agreement and termsWhen the agreement was signed and which Creator Terms they accepted. 8ProfileOpens the creator’s page: titles, notices, agreement, earnings and payouts. Creators: status cards and the creator list with titles, share, agreement and terms.

Invited Active Suspended A suspended creator can be reactivated at any time. Status Meaning Invited Hasn't accepted the invite yet. Active Can sign in to the Creator Portal and submit work. Suspended Can't sign in or submit. Their live titles stay live unless a reviewer unpublishes them.

Choose Invite creator. Fill in: Display name: the name they publish under. Handle: lower-case letters, numbers, dots and underscores, such as night.shift. Contact email: where the invite goes. Revenue share: their percent of what their series earn. The default comes from Admin Panel›Settings›Payments (50% out of the box). Personal note: optional, added to the invite email. Choose Send invite. The email contains a single-use link to the Creator Portal that works for 7 days. If it expires, choose Resend invite on their row: a new link goes out and the old one stops working. warning If email delivery isn't set up, the creator is still added but no email goes out; the panel says so. Add your SMTP server in Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP), then use Resend invite.

Anyone can apply at https://your-domain.com/creator/apply (the app's Become a creator link goes there). The form asks for their name, email, links to past work (one per line) and a short pitch. Applications arrive on the Applications tab, with status cards for Pending, Accepted and Declined. Accept creates their creator account and emails them the Creator Portal link. Decline sends a polite email. The reason you type stays with the team; it's never in the email. You can close applications for a while with the "Become a creator" applications switch in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Features. The form then says applications are closed for now.

Click a creator to open their page: Section What's there At a glance Titles, episodes, followers, share, agreement and Creator Terms. Titles Their series, most recently changed first, with status and episode count. Notices sent What they see in the Creator Portal (review decisions and so on), read or unread. Profile Bio, contact, followers, verified, joined. Agreement Revenue share, agreement signed date, terms version accepted, the agreement file (download) and team notes. Earnings & payouts What they earned in closed months, what was paid, what's still owed (Creator revenue).

Action What it does Edit profile Photo (JPG, PNG or WebP up to 2 MB), bio, and the Verified tick shown in the app. Change share A new percent with a reason. Applies to new unlocks only: unlocks already made keep the share they saved. Edit agreement The date the agreement was signed, the signed PDF (up to 10 MB, kept privately; a new file doesn't delete the old one), and team notes only the team sees. Suspend Needs a reason, which the creator is emailed. They can't sign in or submit; live titles stay live. Reactivate They can sign in and send work again. They're emailed. AI Studio Allow or block AI Studio for this creator and set their limits and allowance on the platform's key (AI Studio settings). Record payout After paying them outside the app: amount, method (bank transfer, UPI, PayPal, Wise or other), reference, date and an internal note. Every action is recorded in the audit log.

Nothing a creator submits reaches viewers without a person's decision here. The Review queue also holds the problem reports viewers send from the player ("Video won't play", "Subtitles are wrong"…). Amber after 18 hours, red after 24. 4Rights declarationWhen and from where the creator declared their rights. 5DetailsSynopsis, age rating, categories, free episodes, coin price and where it’s shown; the episodes are below. 6ApproveConfirm free episodes, price and regions; it goes live at its release time. 7Request changesSends it back with your reason, which the creator sees. 8RejectIt won’t go live. Needs a reason. 9Assign to meSo two reviewers don’t watch the same item. The Review queue with a creator’s new series selected, and the Decision panel.

Type What it is Series A creator's new series, sent with its ready episodes. Episodes New episodes of a creator's live series, each on its own. Series updates Proposed changes to a live series' details. The series stays live as it is until you approve. Reports Problem reports from viewers in the player.

Choose Assign to me so two reviewers don't watch the same item. If someone else holds it and can't finish, Take over (recorded in the audit log). Keyboard shortcuts are listed at the top: move between items, approve and reject. Aim for a decision within 24 hours: items turn amber after 18 hours and red after 24.

Decision What happens Approve A series: confirm the free episodes and the coin price per episode (both within the limits in Admin Panel›Settings›Payments›Creator price limits) and where it's shown. It goes live at its release time, or now if none is set. An episode: it goes live at its release time, or now. Request changes Your reason (up to 1,000 characters) goes to the creator, who can fix it and send it again. Reject Your reason goes to the creator. It won't go live. Unpublish Takes a live series or episode out of the app at once, with a reason. Viewers who unlocked it keep it. For a series update, a table compares each changed field, Now and Proposed: name, subtitle, kicker, schedule line, audio languages, synopsis, categories, age rating, poster, banner, free episodes, coin price and regions. Approving applies them; requesting changes or rejecting leaves the series as it is. If you change where a creator's series is shown, the creator gets a notice and an email saying where. Every decision leaves a notice in the creator's portal and sends them an email, and is recorded in the audit log. Earlier decisions on the same work are listed under each item. A reviewer can't approve a title they own as a creator. Check the rights declaration Every creator submission records a rights declaration: when it was made, from which address, and the declaration version. If an item has none, ask the creator to declare their rights before you approve.

A report shows the reason, the episode, the moment in the episode, the device and app version, the viewer's message, and other reports on the same episode. Action Use it when Mark resolved You fixed or checked it. Write a resolution note (such as "re-encoded E14 and playback works again"). The note stays with the team. Ask the creator to fix it It's a creator's episode. They get your reason in the portal and by email; the episode stays live. The report is resolved. Unpublish this episode Viewers shouldn't see it meanwhile.

AI Studio helps make short dramas with Google's Gemini models: create characters with a consistent look, turn each shot into a storyboard image, generate video takes from it, then assemble the takes into an episode on a timeline. The team's AI Studio works on your own (eDrama Original and Licensed) series and always uses the platform's Gemini key. Creators have their own AI Studio in the Creator Portal. Before you start AI Studio is off until an Owner switches it on and adds the platform's Gemini key in Admin Panel›Settings›AI Studio. Every call is billed to that Google account. See AI Studio settings. your-domain.com/admin/titles/18/ai-studio 12345678 1CharactersStep 1: create the cast and their portraits. 2ShotsStep 2: plan shots, make storyboards and takes. 3EpisodesStep 3: cut kept takes into an episode in the episode editor. 4Who paysThe team studio always uses the platform’s Gemini key. 5Key noticeShown until the Owner adds the platform’s Gemini key in Settings › AI Studio. 6Series lookOne style line every prompt of this series opens with. 7Edit styleChange the style line. 8New characterA name and an identity profile; then generate the portrait. AI Studio for one of your own series, before any character has been made.

Characters Looks Shots Storyboard Takes Timeline Episode Open a series. Admin Panel›Content›AI Studio lists your series that take new work. Pick one. Set the series look. One style line every prompt opens with, such as realistic, soft daylight, Korean drama look. Create characters. Give each a name and an identity profile (age range, face shape, skin tone, eye colour, hair, build, height, distinguishing marks, usual clothes, voice), then Generate portrait (or upload a reference image you have the rights to). Every look and shot starts from the portrait. Add looks. Start from a preset (Casual, Office, Wedding, Night, Traditional) or describe one, such as Ivory wedding dress, hair up, pearl earrings. Regenerate, edit by prompt ("Change only the jacket to red"), or go back to an earlier version. Plan shots. Give each shot a title and an episode, pick up to the allowed number of characters (each in one of their looks), a framing template (Close-up, Wide, Two-shot, Over-the-shoulder, Walking, Conversation), a camera move (Static, Push in, Pull out, Pan, Tilt, Tracking, Handheld, Orbit) and lines of dialogue with an emotion. Make the storyboard. Generate a still for the shot and approve it: takes start from it. Generate takes. Choose the mode (from the storyboard, from start and end stills, or from the cast's images), resolution (360p, 720p or 1080p, up to the allowed maximum) and length. Keep the take you like; edit a take by prompt to make a new one from it. Assemble the episode. In the Episode editor, arrange kept takes (and imported videos) on a timeline and export. See AI episode editor; the team's editor works the same way. The finished video goes to the episode through the normal upload pipeline, and your series is reviewed and published as usual. Consistency AI characters won't look exactly the same in every image or take. The portrait, the look and the same profile in every prompt keep them close. Check each storyboard before you make takes: takes cost more.

Each button shows an estimate from the prices set in Settings; Google's bill is the final word. The team's spending on the platform key can be capped per month (Team studio a month), and every call appears on AI usage. Common messages: Message Meaning Google blocked this prompt Change the prompt and try again. Your Google project reached its limit Google's rate limit (Tier 1 allows 40 videos a day). Try later. We lost Google's answer It may already be on the Google bill: check before trying again. The server stopped before this was sent Nothing was sent or charged; try again.

When you have many titles, prices or translations to change, a spreadsheet is faster than the editor. Several screens have an Import button that takes a CSV or Excel file, shows you exactly what each row will do, and saves everything together, or nothing at all.

Choose Import and the kind of import. Choose Download the template. For prices and translations, the template already contains your current data, so you only change what you mean to. Fill it in, then save it as CSV (UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx). (In Excel, choose CSV UTF-8 when saving, or some letters will be lost.) Upload it. The Review step shows each row as Ready, Unchanged or Problem, with the reason for each problem. If there are no problems, choose Import. All rows are saved together. info Nothing is saved while a row has a problem. Fix the file, go back and upload it again. Columns the import doesn't read are listed and ignored.

Import Where What each row does New titles Admin Panel›Content›Titles›Import Creates a draft title with its owner, details, categories and default-region price. Posters and episodes are added in the editor afterwards. Prices Admin Panel›Content›Titles›Import Changes coin and Series Pass prices, with a column pair per region (coin_price:IN, series_pass_price:IN). Only prices that differ change. Asks for one reason, recorded for every title that changes and sent to the creator of a creator series. Translations Admin Panel›Content›Titles›Import and Admin Panel›Content›Categories Fills in each title's (or category's) text per language, with a column per language and field (such as name:hi). An emptied cell removes that translation. The default language's columns are there for reference only. Invite from a file Admin Panel›Community›Creators Invites each row as a creator, exactly as Invite creator does: name, handle, contact email and share percent (empty uses the default share).

A licensed title needs its licensor; its share is a number from 0 to 100. A creator title needs the creator's handle or contact email; invite them first. Age rating: one of All, 13+, 16+ or 18+. Categories must be active ones, separated by ;. A Series Pass price needs the coin price too. A title with the same name as an existing one is added under its own slug.
The default region always keeps a coin price. Leave a region's cells empty to remove its own price, so it uses the default region's. Viewers keep the price they unlocked at (price lock).

Every table has a Download menu next to its search. It saves exactly what the table shows, with your search and filters, as CSV, MS-Excel, JSON, XML, TXT or SQL. A table too big for one download asks you to narrow it first. Each download is recorded in the audit log as Table downloaded. For money reports, use Export CSV and Monthly creator report on Transactions.

Categories are the genre labels on your titles, such as Revenge, Rebirth or CEO Romance. They power the app's Browse pages, the category chips on Home, "Because you like…" rows, search, and the What hooks you? step of onboarding, where new viewers pick three or more. (In the code they're called tropes.) Drag rows to set the order. 4NameWhat viewers see. 5SlugUsed in app links, so it can’t change once saved. 6TitlesHow many titles use it. 7ActiveOff removes the category from the app; titles keep it. Categories: each category’s image, name, slug, number of titles and Active switch.

Choose New category. Fill in: Name: what viewers see. Slug: lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens, such as ceo-romance. The app's links use it, so it can't change once saved. Image: JPG, PNG or WebP, at least 300 × 300, up to 2 MB. Without one, the app shows the poster of the category's most-watched series. Active: on to show it in the app. Save. Translations of the name for other app languages are in the form's Other languages tabs. To translate them all at once, use Import translations (Bulk imports).
Drag the rows. The app shows categories in this order in Browse, in onboarding and in "Every active category" chips on Home.

Switch off (Active off): the category leaves the app, but titles keep it, so you can turn it back on later. Delete: only for a category no title uses. Otherwise the panel tells you how many titles use it; switch it off instead.
The installer creates a starting set, and Clear demo data restores it if none would be left, so an install never ends up with no categories.

Released episodes keep their numbers. 6Episode nameRename an episode right in the table. 7AccessFree (within the free episodes) or Locked. 8ProcessingUploading, Processing, Ready or Failed (with the reason). 9ReleaseWhen it was released, when it’s scheduled, or a Schedule button. 10Play and commentsPlay the episode here, or open its comments and likes. The Episodes tab of a title: the length floor, the episode table and its actions.

Column Meaning Episode Its number and name ("Untitled" until named). Length The video's length, once processed. Access Free (within the free episodes) or Locked. Status Draft, In review, Approved, Live and so on. Processing Uploading, Processing, Ready or Failed (with the reason). Subtitles Which languages have subtitles. Release Released on a date, scheduled for a date, or not scheduled yet.

Action What it does Play episode Plays it right in the panel, whether it's on this server, Cloudflare Stream or YouTube. If a replacement video is processing, you see the current one until the new one is ready. Comments and likes Opens what viewers said about this episode. Rename Click the name to change it. Schedule Sets the publish time (Release schedule). Delete episode Only an unreleased episode that no viewer has paid for. The episode and its video go for good. Allow short episode See below.

eDrama won't release a paid episode shorter than 45 seconds (the "length floor", set in Admin Panel›Settings›Video pipeline). Viewers complain when late episodes are cut into seconds-long pieces to sell more unlocks, so a coin should always buy a real scene. If an episode is shorter for a good reason, such as the finale's epilogue, use the warning button on its row: Allow short episode, give the reason, and choose Allow it. The reason goes in the audit log. Creators can't submit episodes under the floor at all.
Upload a new file with the same episode number. Viewers keep watching the current video until the new one is processed, then switch over. If the new upload fails, the old one stays.

Open the Localization tab. Each episode has a row and each app language a column, with how many episodes are covered. Choose Upload in the cell for the episode and language. Choose a WebVTT (.vtt) or SubRip (.srt) file: UTF-8 text, up to 1 MB. Choose Upload. The file is checked: times must run in order and end within the episode's length (plus one second). SRT files are converted to WebVTT automatically; the message says how many subtitle lines were found. A new file for the same episode and language replaces the old one. If the episode's video isn't processed yet, the file is checked against its length once it is. In the app, viewers choose subtitles in the player's menu or in App›Me›Settings›Subtitles ("Same as app language" by default).

The app's Home tab is built from sections you arrange here: a hero carousel at the top, Continue Watching, rows and grids of series, banners, category chips, notes and promo cards. A phone preview updates as you work, and nothing reaches viewers until you Publish. documents.t: Setting Meaning Heading / Subtitle Leave the heading empty to use the standard one in the viewer's own language. Style How the section looks (table above). Image (banners) JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 2 MB, in the shape of the style: 16:9 (1920 × 1080), 3:1 (1800 × 600), 4:5 (1080 × 1350) or 1:1 (1080 × 1080). Opens (banners, promos) A series, a category, or a web link; promos and banners can also open the store, VIP or Rewards. A section that would be empty for a viewer is left out, so Home never shows a blank row.

Make your changes. The list says Unpublished changes. Choose Publish layout, then Publish. The app shows the new layout the next time viewers open Home. The layout gets a new version number only if something changed; publishing an identical layout tells you there's nothing to publish. Each publish is recorded in the audit log. warning If a title in the hero was unpublished, it shows Not live: viewers no longer see it there. Remove it before you can publish the layout.

The Release schedule is a calendar of your drops. Every episode goes out at its own publish time; a background task checks every minute and releases what's due. Permission area: Schedule & Home View See the calendar Edit Set, change and clear publish times your-domain.com/admin/schedule?zone=Asia/Kolkata 12345678 1Schedule episodesOne episode a day at the same time, for a range of episodes. 2Time zoneRead and pick times in any region’s time zone. 3WeekPrevious and next week, and back to this week. 4This weekEpisodes dropping, series, followers to remind and held episodes. 5A dropTitle, episode and time. Drag it to another slot, or select it to change the time. 6Ready to scheduleProcessed episodes with no publish time yet. 7Set timeGive a ready episode its publish time. 8RemindersDrop alerts, the daily push limit, quiet hours and VIP renewal reminders. The Release schedule for this week in India time, with five drops of Ten Years Later.

Drag a block to another day or time. Or select it and choose Change time: pick the date and time and choose Save time. It goes out within a minute of that time. Leave the time empty to take the episode off the schedule. Times are stored in universal time and shown in the time zone you pick at the top, so a drop at 20:00 in India is still right for a teammate in London. Changing the clocks for daylight saving never moves a drop.

Choose Schedule episodes. Pick the Title, From episode and To episode. Pick the First day and the Time. Choose Schedule. One episode drops each day at the same local time. Released episodes keep their time; a new time replaces an old one.

If an episode's time has passed but it couldn't go out, it's held, and a card lists it with the reason: Reason Fix Not processed yet Wait for processing, or check Upload & pipeline. The upload failed Upload the file again. Under the length floor Allow it with a reason, or upload a longer cut. Not approved A creator's episode must be approved in the Review queue. The title isn't live Publish the title. Once fixed, the episode is released within a minute.

Creators set their own release times for approved episodes in the Creator Portal (Release times). If a team member changes one of those times here, the team's time wins; the change is recorded in the audit log and the creator gets a notice.

The Reminders card summarises what followers receive: one drop alert per series per day (later drops the same day update it, such as "E22–E25 of …"), at most the daily push limit per viewer, never during quiet hours, and VIP renewal reminders 24 hours before each charge. Change the limits in Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications.

Open any title from Admin Panel›Content›Titles to edit it. The editor has four tabs: Overview, Episodes, Monetization and Localization. your-domain.com/admin/titles/1/edit 123456789 1Poster, name and statusWith the format, episode count and owner (“eDrama Original”, “Licensed from…”, “Creator series by…”). 2At a glanceEpisodes out, free episodes, price per episode, views and revenue (30 days) and completion. 3Comments & reviews, AI StudioJump to what viewers say about this title, or to its AI Studio. 4Status actionsSubmit for review, Approve, Request changes, Publish, Unpublish or Delete draft, depending on the status. 5TabsOverview, Episodes, Monetization and Localization. 6DetailsTitle, slug, synopsis, subtitle, kicker, schedule line, audio languages, categories, age rating, Complete. 7Ownership & rightsWho shares the revenue: owner type, licensor or creator and their share, rights note. 8StatusThe current status and its history: who changed it, when and why. 9Save changesChanges take effect when you save. The Heiress Returns open in the title editor, on the Overview tab.

Field What it's for Title The name viewers see. Slug The title's address in the app and in share links. It becomes fixed once the title is published, because links use it. Subtitle A short line under the name on the series page. Kicker A small label above the name on Home, such as "New this week". Release schedule line When new episodes come out, such as "New episodes every Friday". Audio languages The languages it can be heard in. Press Enter after each. Synopsis Up to 280 characters. No spoilers past episode 3: it shows before people pay. Categories Drive Home rows, Browse and search. Creator titles pick up to 3. Age rating All, 13+, 16+ or 18+. Complete Tells viewers every episode is out: the app shows "Complete" instead of the next drop. It can be turned on only once every episode is released, and a new episode turns it off.

Image Size Formats Poster 2:3, at least 600 × 900 (1200 × 1800 is best) JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB Banner 16:9, at least 960 × 540 (1920 × 1080 is best) JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB The app crops each one for where it's shown.

Choose the Owner (eDrama Original, Licensed or Creator). For a licensed title, name the Licensor and their Licensor share of net revenue once the contract is set. For a creator title, pick the Creator; their share shows here ("Name gets 50% of net revenue"). Add a Rights note if useful. Once a title has been published, changing its owner asks for a reason: its revenue records depend on who owns it.

Under Other languages, a tab per app language holds translations of the name, subtitle, kicker, schedule line and synopsis. Leave a box empty to show the default language's text. To translate many titles at once, use Import › Translations on the Titles list.
A link to what viewers say about this title, on Comments & reviews.

The buttons at the top change with the title's status. Button When What happens Submit for review Draft or Changes requested A reviewer checks the episodes, artwork and prices. Approve In review (your team's titles) Needs Review queue (Edit). The title can then be published. Request changes In review Sends it back with your reason. It needs a new review before publishing. Publish Approved or Unpublished Released episodes appear in the app for every region with a price. Unpublish Live Asks for a reason. The title disappears from Home, Browse and search; viewers keep the episodes they unlocked. Delete draft Draft, never paid for Removes it for good.
Lists every episode with its length, access, status, processing, subtitles and release time. See Episodes & subtitles.

Setting Meaning Free episodes How many episodes from the start anyone can watch. The paywall sits at the next one. It can't be more than the number of episodes. Included in VIP VIP members watch every episode without coins. Ads can unlock Viewers may watch one ad (30 seconds or less) per episode instead of paying. Each region's daily ad limit applies.

Every region (the default), or Only these regions when you only have the rights in some places. Viewers elsewhere no longer find it in Home, search, categories or creator pages, and links to it say it isn't available in their region. Viewers who already unlocked an episode or bought its Series Pass keep it. note Your public website shows only what the default region's viewers see.

Choose Change prices to set, per region: Coin price per episode, Series Pass (optional): one price that unlocks every episode, including future ones. A region without its own price uses the default region's. Every price change needs a reason, kept in the audit log with the old and new prices. Price lock Viewers who already started the series keep the price they saw: a rise doesn't reach them, a drop does. The dialog shows how many viewers have locked a price for this title. See Coins & pricing.

A live preview of the cost card on the series page, for the region you pick: which episodes are free, the price per episode ("60 coins an episode, never more"), the ad option, the Series Pass and how many released episodes are left to unlock.

A reminder of the rules that can't be switched off per title: the price lock, unlocks never charge twice, and auto-unlock is off unless the viewer turns it on. To confirm This card also lists "A failed rewarded ad still unlocks the episode". The server code does not do this: an ad unlocks an episode only once AdMob's server-side verification confirms it was watched to the end (a failed ad unlocks nothing but still counts toward the daily limit). The Ads tab in Monetization describes the code's behaviour correctly. Ask WRTeam which wording is intended.
Subtitles, one file per episode and language. See Episodes & subtitles.

A title is one series in your catalogue. Titles lists all of them, whoever made them: your own originals, dramas licensed from a studio, and creators' series all share one content model. Click one to filter. 4Owner tabsAll, eDrama Originals, Licensed and Creator, with counts. 5SearchSearch by title name. Filter, refresh and download sit beside it. 6A titlePoster, name and categories. Every title has an owner type, which decides who shares its revenue: Owner type Meaning eDrama Original Made and owned by you. All revenue stays with you. Licensed Licensed from a studio or distributor. You name the licensor and, once the contract is set, their share of net revenue. Creator A series by an invited creator, who earns their share of every unlock. Creator series normally arrive from the Creator Portal.

Draft In review Approved Live Unpublished A title in review can also be sent back (Changes requested) or Rejected. A live title can be unpublished and published again. Status Meaning Draft Being prepared. Not visible in the app. In review Waiting for a reviewer's decision. Changes requested Sent back to its owner with a reason. Approved Checked and ready to publish. Live In the app now. Rejected Won't go live. Unpublished Taken out of the app. Viewers keep what they unlocked. Your team's titles are approved in the title editor by a member with Review queue (Edit). A creator's series is decided only in the Review queue.

Choose New title. Type its name (such as The Heiress Returns) and choose Create draft. The editor opens. Add details and artwork, upload the episodes, and set the free episodes and prices. Choose Submit for review, then Approve and Publish (with the right permissions). Every title starts as a draft. Before a title can go live, it needs: at least one episode whose video is ready, a coin price in the default region, no more free episodes than it has episodes. To add many titles at once, use Import › New titles (Bulk imports).
Only a draft that no viewer has paid for can be deleted: open it and choose Delete draft. Anything else is unpublished instead, so viewers' unlocks and the money records stay intact.

Upload & pipeline is where your team uploads episodes and watches them move through three stages: upload → process → ready. Everything after the upload happens in the background, so you can close the page once the files are sent. Permission area: Uploads View See the pipeline Edit Upload, import and retry your-domain.com/admin/upload 12345678910 1Import optionsBulk import (CSV), Add YouTube video and Import from URL. 2Drop episode files hereMP4, MOV or MKV, resumable after a dropped connection. 3Choose filesOr pick files from your computer. Title and episode are matched from file names. 4Stage cardsUploading, Processing, Failed and Ready. Click one to filter the pipeline. 5PipelineEvery episode from upload to release, refreshed by itself. 6RetryA failed upload shows why; Retry starts it again. 7ScheduleA ready episode waiting for its publish time. 8Encoding ladderThe qualities each video is turned into, vertical first. 9Storage & deliveryWhere videos are kept and streamed, and whether it’s ready. 10WorkersEpisodes uploading, processing or failed, and the jobs waiting. Upload & pipeline: the drop zone, the stage cards, the pipeline table and the side cards.

Drag the files onto Drop episode files here, or choose Choose files. Accepted: MP4, MOV or MKV, up to the size set in Admin Panel›Settings›Video pipeline (20 GB by default). Check each file's title and episode number. The number is read from the file name: EP07, or the first number that isn't a year. A file with no number asks you to type it. Read the flags under the files: Another file in this upload is the same episode. Replaces E7's video once the new one is ready; the current one stays live until then. Missing episodes, so you notice gaps. Choose Upload N files. Files go three at a time, straight from your browser to where videos live. Keep the page open until they're sent. Uploads are resumable: if your connection drops, the upload pauses ("waiting for the network") and carries on by itself. If you reload the page, drop the same file again to continue where it stopped. tip To upload to one title only, open the title and choose Upload episodes on its Episodes tab: the uploader opens already set to that title.

For a whole catalogue at once, choose Bulk import (CSV). Download the sample file to see the layout. One row per episode, with these columns: Column Example title The title's name or slug. The title must already exist. episode 1 to 9999 episode title The first meeting file name or URL A file name you'll drop next, an https:// link to a video file, or a YouTube link credit Optional, such as Title by Creator, CC BY publish time Optional, in the default region's time zone, such as 2026-11-02 20:00 Up to 500 rows. If one row has a problem, nothing is imported: the panel lists each problem by row number. Setting publish times needs Schedule & Home (Edit).

Import from URL downloads a video that's already online and processes it like an upload. Choose the Source (an https:// link to an MP4, MOV or MKV on a public website), the title and the episode. Only import content you own or license.

Add YouTube video makes an episode that plays in YouTube's own player inside the app. Paste a Shorts, watch or youtu.be link to a public video that allows embedding, and optionally a Credit. YouTube episodes are always free YouTube's rules forbid charging for, gating or rewarding views of its videos. So these episodes are never sold with coins, ads, VIP or a Series Pass, and earn creators nothing. Their quality and subtitles are YouTube's own. This option appears only when it's switched on in Admin Panel›Settings›Video pipeline. See YouTube.

The table below lists every episode from upload until it's released, with its stages and status. It refreshes by itself every few seconds. Stage Meaning Uploading Going to the video service. Processing Being encoded for the app: 1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p (never above the original), plus a poster. Failed Needs the file again. The Detail column says why; choose Retry. Ready Processed, not released yet. Choose Schedule to set its publish time. Filter by Stage, Title or whether it's Released.

Encoding ladder: the qualities each video is turned into, vertical first. Storage & delivery: where videos are kept and streamed, and whether it's ready ("ffmpeg not found" or "Not connected yet" means it isn't). Links to Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video. Workers: how many episodes are uploading, processing or failed, and the jobs waiting in the queue. Rights checklist: a reminder of what you need before an episode goes live: a licence or ownership document, territories matching the title's regions, a takedown contact, and cleared music.

Message What to do The connection dropped Choose Retry: it carries on where it stopped. The video service refused the file Check the file plays on your computer, then upload it again. The upload link expired Choose Retry to start the file again. Stuck on Processing Check the background workers are running (Cron & queues). Unfinished uploads are cleaned up after two days.

Website edits your public marketing website: a home page built from sections, plus automatic pages for every series, category and creator. You change a draft, check it in the live preview, and Publish when you're happy. Visitors see the change within a minute. Permission area: Website View See the editor Edit Change and publish the website Setting the website up The website itself is a separate Next.js project that you host (on Vercel or your own Node.js server) and connect to your server. Deploying and connecting it is covered in Website setup; this page covers editing its content. your-domain.com/admin/website 123456789 1TabsSections, Header & footer, Style, Languages, Search & stats, Connection and more. 2Page sectionsYour home page, top to bottom. Tips for editing are just below. 3Drag handleDrag to reorder, or move up and down. 4A sectionIts type and heading. Click to edit its Content, Design and Settings. 5Show on the websiteThe eye hides a section but keeps its content. 6PreviewUpdates as you type, on Computer or Phone, in each language. It needs the website’s address (Connection tab). 7Save draftKeep your changes without publishing. 8PublishVisitors see the changes within a minute. 9Switch website offVisitors see a short “back soon” page. Website on the Sections tab, with the page’s sections in order and the preview panel.

Tab What you set Sections The home page, top to bottom (below). Header & footer Header style (Floating bar, Classic full width, Centred logo, Minimal with menu), menu links, header button, an announcement bar; footer style (Columns, Big name, Compact, Download first), about line, link columns, legal pages, store buttons, contact email and copyright line. Style Theme (Midnight dark, Paper light, or follow the visitor's device), whether visitors can switch light/dark, headings (editorial serif italic or modern), corners and motion (Full, Subtle, None). Get the app Store buttons (from your App versions store links), an optional direct APK download link with its version and minimum Android, and a QR code for computers. Search & stats Site title and title pattern, description, share picture (1200 × 630), whether search engines and AI assistants may read the site, pages for every series, category and creator, llms.txt, Google Search Console and Bing codes, and per-page titles and descriptions. Social & analytics Social links (Instagram, YouTube, X, Facebook, TikTok, Threads, LinkedIn, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord) and visitor statistics (Plausible, Umami or Google Analytics). Languages Which app languages the website offers, a language menu in the header, and translations of every text. Connection Where the website lives and how it talks to your server (below). History Every published version. Load one into the draft, check it, publish it again. Your name, logos and theme colour come from Admin Panel›Settings›Branding, so the app, the panels and the website always match.

Section What it shows Styles Top slider Big pictures with your headline and buttons: your most popular series automatically, or slides you make. Cinematic full width, Poster stack, Split Numbers Live series, released episodes, categories, creators, app languages, or numbers you type. Band, Split Series showcase A row or grid of series: new, popular this week, Top 10 today, complete, one category, one creator, or ones you pick. Row of posters, Large posters, Top 10 with big numbers, Grid, One big and a list, Wide cards What is it? What your app is, with feature points and phone pictures. Text and phone, Editorial, Centred Categories Your categories with artwork, leading to each category's page. Artwork tiles, Chips, Mosaic Get the app Store buttons, a direct APK link and a QR code. Always on the page. Phone showcase, Band, Glowing card Creators Creators with live series, and an invitation to become one. Avatars, Cards with posters Questions Questions and short answers (search engines and AI assistants read these too). Accordion, Two columns Call to action A bold band with a heading and a button. Band, Split, Glowing card Text block A heading, paragraphs and an optional picture. Text only, Text and picture Each section also has a background (page colour, raised panel, accent glow or accent colour), spacing (compact, regular, airy), an optional section address for header links, and a feature condition (Only while VIP is on, Rewards are on, and so on) so a section disappears when you switch that feature off. Put *stars* around a word or two in a heading to set them in the accent style. While your catalogue is small, sample series can fill series sections until they have 4 live series. Turn this off when your catalogue is ready.

The website is a separate site. On the Connection tab: Copy This server's address for the website (EDRAMA_API_URL) into the website's settings. Choose Make a secret and paste the Refresh secret into the website's REVALIDATE_SECRET. It's shown only once; Make a new secret replaces it. Enter the Website address (such as https://www.your-domain.com) and choose Save address. It's used for previews and to tell the website about changes.

Save draft keeps your changes without publishing. Discard draft goes back to the live version. Preview opens the saved draft on your website for 30 minutes, marked "Preview · not published". Publish shows the changes to visitors within a minute. Switch website off shows visitors a short "back soon" page and asks search engines not to index it. The status above the tabs reads Live · version N, Unpublished changes or Everything is published.

The Dashboard answers one question: how is the platform doing? It opens when you sign in. Every member sees it, but each card shows only if your role can see that area: revenue cards need Transactions (View), viewer figures need Users (View). your-domain.com/admin 123456789 1GreetingWith today’s date, time and the region you’re looking at. 2ShortcutsUpload episodes, Review queue, Release schedule and Send a push. 3Recount nowWhen the figures were last counted (every 15 minutes); recount today straight away. 4RangeLast 7, 30 or 90 days. Every number on the page uses the same range and region. 5RevenueRevenue for the range, with the change against the period before. 6Viewer and unlock cardsNew viewers (signed in and guests), daily active viewers, paying viewers and unlocks, each with its trend. 7Revenue by sourceDaily revenue from coin packs and VIP, before or after the store fee. Table shows the numbers. 8Revenue sourcesCoin packs against VIP, after store fees and today so far. 9Needs attentionThings only a person can decide: review items, failed uploads, held episodes, refunds and adjustments waiting. The Dashboard over the last 30 days for All regions.

Card What it shows Revenue Money from coin packs and VIP in the range, in your reporting currency, with the change against the previous period of the same length, today's revenue so far, and the amount after store fees. Coin-pack revenue always equals the net on Transactions for the same days and region. New viewers New accounts in the range, split into signed in and guests. Daily active viewers The average number of viewers active each day. Paying viewers Viewers who paid in the range. Revenue by source A daily stacked chart of coin packs and VIP. Switch between Before store fee and After store fee. The Table button shows the same data as a table. How viewers unlock A donut of unlock methods. Useful for seeing whether ads, coins or VIP drive your catalogue. Top titles The top 10 titles, ranked by Revenue or Views, with their status. Needs attention Live counts: review items waiting (and how long the oldest has waited), failed uploads, episodes held past their publish time, refunds and balance adjustments waiting for approval. Each row links to where you act on it.

The Dashboard reads pre-counted figures, so it stays fast however big your catalogue gets. A background task recounts today and the two days before every 15 minutes, plus any day where a refund or a late purchase changed things. The line under the revenue card says when it was last counted. Need today's numbers now? Choose Recount now. It recounts today straight away (at most once a minute for the whole team).

Use the Region switcher in the top bar to see one region, or All regions for everything. All money is shown in your reporting currency (USD by default), converted at the exchange rate in force on each day. If a currency has no exchange rate for some days, that revenue is left out and the card names the currency, rather than guessing. Add the missing rate in Admin Panel›Settings›Regions & languages. note Days are counted in UTC (universal time), so "today" may start a few hours earlier or later than your local midnight.
Ads and Rewards are per region: choose it with the Region switch at the top of Admin Panel›Money›Monetization.
documents.s: Monetization › Ads, Rewards and Fair-play rules

documents.t: eDrama uses rewarded ads only: ads a viewer chooses to watch, either to unlock an episode or to earn bonus coins on the Rewards tab.

Setting Default Meaning Unlock ads per day 6 (Global), 20 (India) One ad unlocks one episode. Rewards ads per day Same as unlock Ads watched for coins. Coins per Rewards ad 15 Bonus coins per ad. Maximum ad length 30 seconds Never more than 30 seconds. Unlock and Rewards ads share one daily limit Off Off: each has its own limit.

An AdMob ad unit belongs to one app, so Android and iOS each have their own. A platform without a unit shows no ads. Field Format Unlock ad unit ID (Android) / (iOS) ca-app-pub-0000000000000000/0000000000 Rewards ad unit ID (Android) / (iOS) Same format Turn on server-side verification In AdMob, open each ad unit › Server-side verification and enter the callback URL shown on this tab. An ad unlocks an episode or pays coins only once AdMob confirms it there, so ads can't be faked. See AdMob.

1 ad = 1 reward. Never two ads that turn into six. Maximum length 30 seconds. No playable or interactive ads in the unlock path. Paid once AdMob confirms the ad. Never show ads to VIP, anywhere. Ads never auto-play an unlock: the viewer always taps to watch.

your-domain.com/admin/monetization?tab=rewards 12345678 1RegionRewards are set per region. 2Restore default rewardsFills the form with the default wheel, titles, shields and multiplier. 3Spin wheel6 to 12 prizes (an even number), in wheel order; drag to rearrange. 4A prizeIts coins and weight; the chance is worked out for you. 5ChanceWeight compared with the others. 6Streak titlesNames earned at a viewer’s best streak, with one-time bonus coins. 7TranslationsEach title’s name in other app languages. 8Save rewardsNothing changes for viewers until you save. The Rewards tab for the Global region: the spin wheel’s prizes and the streak titles.

Viewers spin a wheel once a day for free; every spin pays bonus coins. The server picks the prize, and viewers can see the odds. The default wheel (8 prizes, in wheel order): Prize 10 200 15 50 20 100 25 30 Weight 300 3 250 35 200 12 120 80 Chance 30% 0.3% 25% 3.5% 20% 1.2% 12% 8% Weight is a prize's chance compared with the others: a weight of 200 comes up twice as often as 100. Drag rows to rearrange the wheel. Use an even number of prizes (6 to 12) so the colours alternate. The tab shows the average spin and about how many coins a daily viewer earns a month. VIP spin multiplier (default 2): VIP viewers get the prize times this number. Title bonuses are never multiplied.

Each daily spin adds a day to the viewer's streak. Streak shields: one shield is earned every 7 days of streak (0 turns shields off), and a viewer holds up to 2. A shield covers one missed day by itself, so the streak carries on. Shields are only earned, never sold. Streak titles: names earned at a viewer's best streak and kept for good. Each title's bonus coins are paid once, the first time it's reached. The app colours titles by their order. Days Title Bonus coins 1 Extra 0 3 Understudy 5 7 Scene Stealer 20 14 Plot Twister 30 30 Drama Champion 75 60 Drama Royalty 100 100 Drama Legend 150 365 Hall of Famer 500 Titles can be renamed, added and translated per language.

Setting Default Meaning Welcome bonus: Coins 100 Bonus coins a new account gets once per device. Welcome bonus: Days to use them 7 When they expire. Bonus coins expire after 7 days Counted from the day they're earned. Applies to spin, ad and pack bonuses. Restore default rewards fills the form with the default wheel, titles, shields and multiplier. Nothing changes until you choose Save rewards; the welcome bonus and expiry stay as they are. Rewards can be switched off for everyone in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Features. The app's Rewards tab then becomes the Wallet tab.
The last tab lists the rules that protect what viewers pay for. They're locked, so a pricing change can never quietly undo them. See Fair-play rules.
Both tabs are per region: choose the region with the Region switch at the top of Admin Panel›Money›Monetization.
documents.s: Monetization › Coin packs and VIP plans

documents.t: A coin pack is what viewers buy in the store: a number of coins, often with bonus coins on top, for a price. your-domain.com/admin/monetization?tab=packs 1234567 1RegionCoin packs are set per region. 2New coin packAdd a pack to this region. 3PackCoins and bonus coins. 4Price and per coinIn the region’s currency. 5FlagsOnce per account (first top-up), Popular, Best value or Hidden. 6Store SKUThe Google Play and App Store product IDs. 7EditChange the pack, or turn it off. The Coin packs tab for the Global region: coins, bonus, price, price per coin, episodes, flags and store IDs.

Pack Bonus Price Flag 300 coins +300 $1.99 First top-up offer (once per account) 500 coins +50 $4.99 1,000 coins +200 $9.99 Popular 2,000 coins +600 $19.99 5,000 coins +2,000 $49.99 Best value India starts with the same coins at ₹99, ₹199, ₹399, ₹799 and ₹1,999 (placeholders).

Field Meaning Coins / Bonus coins Paid coins never expire; bonus coins expire after the days set on Rewards and are always spent first. Price In the region's currency. Google Play product ID Lower-case letters, digits, dots, underscores and dashes. Must match the product in Play Console. App Store product ID Must match the product in App Store Connect. Shown in the app Off hides the pack without deleting it. Order The order in the store. First top-up / Popular / Best value Only one pack per region can carry each flag. The first top-up offer can be bought once per account. See In-app purchases for creating the products in each store. note A pack someone has bought can't be deleted, so it stays in their history: turn off Shown in the app instead. A pack with a pending purchase can't be deleted either.

VIP is a subscription that unlocks every drama, with no ads. Each region has three plans: Weekly, Monthly and Yearly. Plan Global India (placeholder) Weekly $5.99 ₹49 Monthly $19.99 ₹149 Yearly $119.99 ₹999 Each plan card shows its price, the weekly equivalent and saving, subscribers and how many have auto-renew on. Edit a plan to change: Field Meaning Price Above zero. Offered in the app Off hides the plan. Google Play subscription ID and base plan ID The base plan itself, never an offer. App Store product ID Perks One per line, as the app lists them. Default: Every drama unlocked. No ads. No free trials VIP has no free trial: the price must be above zero, and no ID or perk may name a trial or a free introductory offer. The server refuses a subscription that started with a free trial.

The VIP page in the app lists the subscription's terms in plain words. By default it shows the built-in rules, translated into every app language. Choose Edit rules to write your own (one per line, per language), or Use built-in rules to go back.
These can't be switched off: No free trial that turns into a charge. A renewal reminder 24 hours before every charge. Cancel in two taps, in the app. VIP never sees an ad. See VIP subscriptions.

Creators earn from coins viewers spend on their series, and also from ads and VIP, which aren't tied to one series' price. Creator revenue works out each creator's share of the ad and VIP money month by month. The app imports and calculates it; your team reviews, adjusts and approves it before it reaches the creators' statements. Permission area: Transactions View See months Edit Import, calculate, adjust, approve and reopen ImportAdMob earnings CalculatePools and shares ReviewAdjust if needed ApproveOnto statements PayRecord payouts your-domain.com/admin/creator-revenue 1234567 1Import from AdMobReads the month’s unlock-ad earnings by country and ad unit. 2CalculateWorks out the pools and each creator’s share. 3MonthPick the month to review. 4StepsImport, Calculate, Review, Approve, Pay. 5AdMob noticeUntil AdMob is connected, ads pools stay at zero unless set by hand. 6TilesAds and VIP pools, and what creators get from coins, ads, VIP and in total. 7Pools by regionEach region’s ad and VIP money and the part shared with creators. Creator revenue for a month not yet prepared: the five steps, the tiles and Pools by region.

Ads. Each region's ads pool = its unlock-ad earnings from AdMob × the ads pool percent. A creator earns: pool × their verified ad unlocks ÷ all verified ad unlocks in the region × their share percent. A creator's own views and accounts under a day old don't count. VIP. Each region's VIP pool = the month's VIP charges, less refunds and store fees, × the VIP pool percent. A creator earns: pool × their VIP minutes on locked episodes ÷ all VIP minutes in the region × their share percent. Your own and licensed titles count in each region's total, so their part stays with the platform. Amounts are rounded down, in your reporting currency.

Prepare. On the import day (the 5th by default), the app imports the month before from AdMob and calculates it by itself, and members with Transactions (Edit) get a bell. Or choose Import from AdMob or Calculate yourself. Review. Check the tiles, Pools by region and each creator. Fix a pool if needed. Set a pool by hand only when the import or the charges are wrong. It keeps your amount (marked Set by hand) until you reset it. Adjust a creator if needed. Add (or, with a minus sign, take) an amount with a reason. Creators see the amount, not your reason. A void adjustment stays in the history, crossed out. Approve. The creators' statements get their ads, VIP and adjustments, and the month is locked. Reopen unlocks it; statements keep the approved amounts until you approve again. Pay. Pay each creator outside the app (bank transfer, UPI, PayPal, Wise…) and record it with Record payout on their page in Creators. If AdMob isn't connected, ads pools stay at zero until you set them by hand or connect AdMob in Admin Panel›Settings›Creator revenue.

In Admin Panel›Settings›Creator revenue (see Payments & creator revenue): Setting Default Prepare each month by itself On Import day of the month 5 (1–28; AdMob finalises a month's earnings in the first days of the next) Ads pool 100% of each region's unlock-ad earnings VIP pool 100% of each region's VIP revenue after refunds and store fees A second member approves Off. On: whoever last changed a month can't approve it.

On each creator's page, Earnings & payouts shows what they earned in closed months, what was paid, what's owed, and this month so far (an estimate). A month is closed automatically on the 1st of the next month, or with Close month for creators. Coins come from the monthly statement; ads and VIP come from this page once approved. Creators see the same figures on their Earnings page in the Creator Portal. See Creator earnings for the full picture.

Monetization is where you set what things cost. It has six tabs: Regions, Coin packs, VIP plans, Ads, Rewards and Fair-play rules. Everything except Regions and Fair-play rules is set per region: pick the region with the Region switch at the top of the page. Permission area: Prices & coin packs View See every tab Edit Change regions, packs, plans, ads and rewards A region is a group of countries that share a currency and prices. Selling the same drama at fair local prices in, say, India and the United States is what regions are for. your-domain.com/admin/monetization?tab=regions 12345678 1TabsRegions, Coin packs, VIP plans, Ads, Rewards and Fair-play rules. 2New regionStarts as a copy of the default region’s prices. 3Where regions come fromSays whether viewers’ countries come from your CDN or the app, and what to set. 4A regionName and code. The default region serves every other country. 5Coin valueWhat one coin is worth in the region’s currency. 6CountriesWhich countries it covers. 7StatusOn or off. 8Edit / Make defaultChange a region, or make it the default. Monetization on the Regions tab: each region’s currency, coin value, countries, ad unlocks and VIP price.

Region Code Currency 1 coin is worth Time zone Countries Global (default) GLOBAL USD $0.0099 UTC Every country no other region lists India IN INR ₹0.29 Asia/Kolkata India Placeholders India's coin value and prices are placeholders. Replace them with your own before launch.

A viewer's region comes from their country: the country their app store reports at sign-in, otherwise the country your CDN reports (Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry header), otherwise the default region. A note above the table says which source your server is using. A viewer can't choose another region; your team can move one in Users › Change region.
documents.s: How a viewer's region is chosen

documents.t: Choose New region. Fill in: Name and Code (capital letters, digits and underscores, such as JP; fixed once created). Currency (ISO code, such as JPY; fixed once created because prices, purchases and reports are stored in it) and the Currency symbol position (before or after the amount; applies to every region in that currency). Coin value: what one coin is worth in that currency, up to six decimals. Time zone. Countries: a country belongs to one region; picking one another region lists moves it here. Leave Active off and choose Save region. The new region starts as a copy of the default region's coin packs, VIP plans, title prices, ad limits and rewards, with money prices converted between the two coin values. Review them on each tab. Turn Active on.

Turn a region off: its countries use the default region for new sessions. Purchases, unlocks and price locks keep their region. Make default: this region then serves every country no active region lists. Viewers keep the prices they already locked. Exactly one region is the default, and it's always on. Delete: only a region that no viewer, purchase, unlock or report belongs to. Every change can carry an optional reason and is recorded in the audit log.

Every country belongs to one region. A country no active region lists uses the default region. Prices are set per region. A title without its own price in a region uses the default region's. The coin value turns coins into money. The app shows every price in coins and in the region's money before every unlock, and reports convert with it. Exchange rates into your reporting currency are set separately, in Admin Panel›Settings›Regions & languages. See Regions & currencies.

Transactions lists every coin-pack purchase across Google Play and the App Store. Receipts are verified on the server before coins land, and every purchase opens into a drawer with its receipt checks, ledger rows and refund. Permission area: Transactions View See purchases, export and create reports Edit (Refunds need the Refunds area) your-domain.com/admin/transactions 12345678 1Export CSVThe transactions in a date range, with your filters. 2Monthly creator reportPer series and region, so Finance can pay creators. 3Close monthWrites each creator’s statement for a finished month. 4StatsGross over 30 days, refund rate, chargebacks, and deliveries auto-retried. 5ShowAll, Completed, Refunds & chargebacks, Needs attention. 6SearchOrder ID or viewer. 7A purchaseThe user, order ID and pack. Click the row for its drawer: receipt checks, ledger rows and refund. 8ReceiptVerified, Retried, Awaiting store or Check failed. Transactions: the stat cards and every purchase with store, amount, coins, status and receipt check.

Filter by date, product and amount (in each purchase's own currency, or in the reporting currency at each day's rate). Under the table, Totals for the matching rows add up every page: the number of purchases, gross, refunds, and the net in your reporting currency. Currencies with no exchange rate on some days are named and left out rather than guessed.

Section What it shows Item and user The pack, coins credited (paid + bonus) and the viewer. Order ID, store product, country · region, store fee The fee saved at the time of purchase. Verification Four checks: Receipt signature valid, Purchase token unused (no replay), Coins delivered to the ledger, Store notification received, each Passed, Passed after a retry, Waiting for the store, Failed or Not reached. Ledger rows The coin movements this purchase caused, with the balance after. Refund If refunded: the source (Admin Panel, store notification or Google Play voided purchases), coins taken back, any shortfall, who asked and when.

Refunds from the panel are for Google Play purchases. Apple decides App Store refunds: the drawer has a link to send the viewer to Apple's refund request page, and Apple's notification updates the purchase when it's done. Open the purchase and choose Refund…. Pick the Reason: Charged twice, Coins not delivered, Accidental purchase, A child or family member bought it, or Something else (then a Note is required). Decide Take the coins back: On: a reversal is written to the viewer's ledger. If they already spent some, what's left is taken back and the rest is recorded as the shortfall: the balance never goes below zero. Off: the money goes back and the viewer keeps the coins. Choose Refund. The panel first checks your role's refund limit (shown in the dialog), then asks Google to refund. Only if Google agrees are the refund, the reversal and the audit record written. If Google refuses, nothing is written. Your role's limit What happens Within the limit You can refund. Over the limit Someone with a higher limit must refund it. No limit set Your role can't refund. Owner Any amount. Partial or second refunds aren't offered. Refunds the store makes Refunds and chargebacks made directly by Google or Apple arrive through the stores' notifications and a daily check of Google's voided purchases. They update the purchase and reverse the coins the same way, never twice.

Export CSV: the transactions in the dates you pick, with the filters you have on. A short export downloads at once; a long one is built in the background and its download link (good for 24 hours) arrives in the bell. Monthly creator report: for each series and region, the paid coins spent, Series Pass coins, ad unlocks and VIP minutes for one month, with the settings used. Its link arrives in the bell. It's also made automatically on the 1st of each month. Cells that look like spreadsheet formulas are written as plain text, for safety. Every export is in the audit log.

The Admin Panel, also called the Studio, is where your team runs eDrama: the catalogue, the release schedule, creators, viewers, money and settings. Open it at https://your-domain.com/admin. your-domain.com/admin 123456789 1Your logoFrom Settings › Branding, with the STUDIO label. Click it to return to the Dashboard. 2Hide sidebarMore room for wide tables. Shortcut: Ctrl + B (⌘ + B on a Mac). 3MenuGrouped into Overview, Content, Community, Audience, Money and System. You only see the screens your role allows; numbers show what’s waiting. 4Search or jump to…The command palette (Ctrl + K or ⌘ + K): find a title, creator or user by email, phone or ID, or jump to any page. 5RegionChoose the region that region-based screens show, or All regions. 6Studio languageThe language you see the Studio in. Only you see your choice. 7NotificationsThe bell: export links, approvals waiting for you, failed jobs and new support tickets. 8ThemeSwitch between the paper (light) and ink (dark) theme. Your choice stays in your browser. 9YouYour name and role. Open Your account (profile, password, two-factor); the arrow signs you out. The Admin Panel’s Dashboard, with the sidebar menu on the left and the top bar above.

Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP) eDrama sends team invites, password resets, every creator email and system alerts. SMTP is the standard way a server sends email through your email provider. The top of the page says how email is sent right now: Status Meaning Through the SMTP server below Every email the Studio and the Creator Portal send uses it. Not sent: emails are written to the server's log Nobody receives emails. Add an SMTP server. Through the server's own settings From .env. An SMTP server added here takes over.

Fill in the SMTP server card: Field Example SMTP host smtp.gmail.com (without https://) Port 587 with STARTTLS, or 465 with SSL/TLS Encryption STARTTLS (port 587), SSL/TLS (port 465), or None (only for a server on your private network) Username / Password Your SMTP login. For Gmail and Google Workspace, an app password, not the account password. From address An address your provider lets you send from, such as no-reply@your-domain.com From name Optional; your app's name when empty Save, then Send test email. Common providers: Gmail smtp.gmail.com (587, STARTTLS), Amazon SES email-smtp.<region>.amazonaws.com, SendGrid smtp.sendgrid.net with the username apikey. info Emails are sent by the background queue worker. If none runs, they wait (System shows the queues). Saving new details restarts the workers so they use them.
