Totals, the Dashboard and refund limits are shown in one reporting currency (USD by default). Each exchange rate says what one unit of a currency is worth in it, from a date until a newer rate starts. Stored purchases keep their own currency. Choose Add rate. Pick the Currency, the Rate (how many reporting-currency units one unit is worth, up to six decimals) and Valid from (rows on this day and later use it). Optionally give a Reason, then Save rate. Rates are marked In force, Scheduled (starts later) or Earlier. A rate for a currency and date that already has one replaces it. Remove a rate and its days use the rate before it, or are left out of totals if there's none. Add a rate for every currency you sell in If no rate is in force for a currency, its purchases are left out of totals and the Dashboard (the screens name the currency), and refunds in it can't be checked against a role's limit. Add one for each region's currency. Change the reporting currency on its card. Rates entered into the old currency stop applying, so enter rates into the new one straight away.

Admin Panel›Settings›Sign-in & security

Only the Owner can change this. The card shows how many active members use two-factor and names those who don't. Turn on Require two-factor for every member. Confirm. The dialog says how many members don't use it yet (including you, if you don't). From the next click, members without two-factor are held on the setup page, and nobody reaches the Studio without a second factor. Turning it off lets members sign in with their password alone; those who use two-factor keep it. A member who lost their phone and recovery codes can be helped with Reset 2FA on Team & roles.

These protections can't be switched off: Protection Details Lockout 5 failed sign-ins for one email from one address lock it for 15 minutes. Session length 12 hours from sign-in; no "remember me". Disabled members Signed out at their next click. Strong passwords At least 12 characters, not found in a known data breach. Same answer for every failure Sign-in and password reset never reveal whether an email has an account. Audit Every sign-in, failure, lockout and sign-out is in the audit log. Encrypted secrets Integration keys, viewers' email and phone, and two-factor secrets are stored encrypted.

Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video makes two separate choices: Choice Options What it decides Storage (files) This server (default), Amazon S3 (or another S3-compatible service), Cloudflare R2 Where images, documents, subtitles and the videos this server makes are kept. Video streaming This server (default, with ffmpeg), Cloudflare Stream What processes episode videos and streams them to viewers. your-domain.com/admin/settings?s=storage 123456 1Storage (files)Where images, documents and subtitles are kept: this server, Amazon S3 or Cloudflare R2. 2Video streamingWhat processes and streams videos: this server (ffmpeg) or Cloudflare Stream. 3In useThe option in use now. 4Set upAn option that needs keys says so; set it up, then switch. 5How switching worksFiles are copied and checked first; nothing is deleted. 6Key cardsAmazon S3, Cloudflare R2 and Cloudflare Stream, each with “Where do I find these?”. Settings › Storage & video: where files are kept and what streams videos.

Option Best for This server (files) Getting started and small catalogues. Nothing to set up. Amazon S3 When you already run on AWS. Amazon bills for every GB viewers download. Works with DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, Backblaze B2 and MinIO too. Cloudflare R2 Streaming at scale: R2 has no download fees, so viewers watching costs nothing extra. This server (video) Keeping videos with your files, at no extra cost. Needs ffmpeg (Video processing). Cloudflare Stream No video work on your server. Cloudflare bills for minutes stored and watched.

If the option says Needs setup, choose Set up and follow the steps: fill in its key card, Save, then Test connection. Choose Switch to … and confirm. Every image, document and video is copied to the new place in the background, in batches, and checked. The switch happens only once every file is there. The page shows the progress. Nothing is ever deleted from where it was, and links in the app keep working throughout. If some files can't be copied, nothing switches: fix the cause and choose Retry failed files. You can Cancel move at any time; files already copied are skipped by the next move. warning While a bucket holds your files, its service, region, endpoint and name can't change: move back to this server first. Keys can be replaced at any time.

A new engine applies to new uploads. Videos already uploaded keep playing from the engine that holds them: nothing is moved or deleted. Images, documents and subtitles stay where Storage (files) keeps them. Videos still on Cloudflare Stream? If you move from Cloudflare Stream back to this server, choose Move videos off Cloudflare Stream: each episode's video is downloaded from Cloudflare as MP4, transcoded here and stored with your files. Viewers keep playing the Stream video until its copy is ready. Nothing is deleted from Cloudflare.

Card Fields Amazon S3 bucket Service, access key ID, secret access key, region, bucket, endpoint (for other S3 services), public URL (optional, such as a CloudFront domain) Cloudflare R2 bucket Cloudflare account ID, jurisdiction (Default, EU or FedRAMP), access key ID, secret access key, bucket, public URL (optional) Cloudflare Stream Account ID, API token, webhook secret, signing key ID, signing key, customer subdomain, plus the webhook URL to register Without a public URL, posters and banners are served through secure links that last six days. Enter your email and password and choose Sign in. If two-factor is on for you, enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app (or one of your recovery codes). Rules that keep the panel safe: After 5 wrong passwords for one email from one address, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes. Every failure shows the same message, so nobody can guess which emails have accounts. There is no "remember me": a session ends 12 hours after sign-in. If an Owner or admin disables your account, you're signed out at your next click.

If a member added you with a temporary password, you're taken to Choose your password before anything else. Enter the temporary password, then a new one of at least 12 characters that isn't in a known data breach. If the team requires two-factor, you set it up next. If you were invited by email, the link takes you to a page where you set your own password straight away. The link works once and expires (see Team & roles).

Choose Forgot password? on the sign-in page and enter your email. If an account exists, a reset link is emailed to you. (The page answers the same either way, for privacy.) Email delivery must be set up for this to work: see Email.

Open your name at the foot of the sidebar › Your account. Section What you can do Profile Change your name and photo (JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 2 MB). They show to the team in the sidebar, the audit log and approvals. Your email is how you sign in, so it can't be changed here. Password Enter your current password and a new one. Your other devices are signed out; this one stays signed in. Two-factor authentication Turn it on or off, see how many recovery codes are left, and make new ones. Session When you signed in and when your session ends. Creator profile The Owner and members with Settings (Edit): how your platform appears as the "creator" of your own and licensed titles in the app: name, handle, bio, photo and the verified tick.

Two-factor adds a second lock: after your password, sign-in asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password or Authy. Open Your account › Two-factor authentication and choose Set up authenticator app. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or type the key it shows. Enter the 6-digit code and your password to confirm. Save the 8 recovery codes somewhere safe. Each one signs you in once if you lose your phone. tip The Owner can require two-factor for the whole team in Admin Panel›Settings›Sign-in & security. Members without it are then held on the setup page at their next click. If someone loses their phone and their recovery codes, the Owner can use Reset 2FA on Admin Panel›Team & roles.

The Audit log records every important change: sign-ins, price changes, refunds, role changes, review decisions, settings and more. It's append-only: nobody can edit or delete a row, not even the Owner, and the database itself refuses changes to it. Permission area: Audit log View See and export the log your-domain.com/admin/audit-log 123456 1ExportDownloads the filtered rows as CSV. Secrets stay masked. 2AreasEverything, Access, Money, Content, Settings, Viewers. 3FiltersWho, action, record type and date range. 4An actionWhat happened, by whom (a member, a creator, or System). 5IP addressWhere it came from. 6DetailsThe before and after of each changed field, and the device. The audit log: every change with when, who, action, record, reason and IP address.

A few examples of the actions you'll see: Area Examples Access Signed in, sign-in failed, locked out, password changed, member added, role changed, two-factor turned on, invite sent or revoked Money Purchase refunded, charged back, balance adjustment requested/approved, coin pack changed, VIP plan changed, exchange rate saved, transactions exported Content Title status changed, price changed, owner changed, episodes reordered, short episode allowed, publish time changed, Home layout published, review decisions, comments removed Settings Branding changed, features changed, maintenance mode changed, integration keys changed, legal page published, email template changed Viewers Account banned or unbanned, region changed, episodes granted, contact details viewed Each entry keeps the reason given, the IP address, and in Details, the before and after of every changed field. Fields named like password, token, secret or key are always masked.

Export downloads the filtered rows, newest first, as a CSV file through a signed link that works for five minutes. The export is itself recorded in the log. To confirm The project notes say audit rows are meant to be kept for two years, but no task currently deletes old rows. They're kept indefinitely until a retention rule is added.

If you imported demo data during installation, it shows how eDrama looks in use: sample dramas, creators, viewers and Dashboard figures, with artwork drawn for you. Clear it before you launch. Your own titles, viewers and settings stay. Only the Owner can clear demo data, and the page appears only while demo data is present.

Removed Stays The demo titles, with their episodes, translations, statistics, artwork and videos Regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ad and reward settings The demo categories and their pictures Settings, languages and language packs, roles, legal pages and email templates The demo creators, with their submissions and review items Your license, the Owner account and the platform's own creator profile The demo viewers, with their wallets, ledgers, purchases, unlocks, VIP, reviews, comments, follows, reports and tickets Everything you added yourself, and the audit log The demo team accounts The demo Dashboard figures, searches and pushes to demo titles Home goes back to the starting layout and the sign-in screens to the built-in photos. If no categories would be left, the starting categories are restored.

Open Admin Panel›System›Clear demo data and read both lists. Choose Clear demo data. Type CLEAR in capital letters to confirm. It can't be undone. The result says how many titles, viewers and creators were removed. If real viewers already paid for a demo title, that title is kept, hidden, so their purchases stay intact. tip You can import the demo data again on a test server with php artisan edrama:demo-data. Don't run it on your live server after launch.

Admin Panel›System›License & updates shows your license and installed version, and is where the Owner activates the license and installs updates. Card What it shows License Active or not active, the purchase code (masked), the domain it's registered to, the buyer, when it was last checked, and whether the check is enforced on this install. Version The installed version, the last update, and the update history (from → to, applied or failed). Activate your license / Install an update One form for both: the purchase code, an optional update package (.zip), and the backup confirmation. Only the Owner can submit the form. The full steps, what's checked and why an update can be refused are in License & updates.

System shows the health of eDrama's background work: whether the scheduler's cron is running, every scheduled task's last run, the queues, and failed jobs you can retry. Permission area: Settings View See System Edit Retry and delete failed jobs your-domain.com/admin/system 1234567 1System at a glanceScheduled tasks, last runs, jobs waiting and failed jobs. Each card jumps to its section. 2Server setup“Cron running” once the scheduler runs; until then the steps stay open. 3Where you set it upSSH / crontab, hosting panel (command) or hosting panel (PHP script). 4Crontab entryThe exact line for your server, with a Copy button. 5Queue workersShown when supervisor runs the workers. 6Copy all commandsThe cron line and the list of tasks it runs. 7Server logsOpens the log viewer. System on a server whose cron isn’t set up yet: overview cards, Server setup and scheduled tasks.

Section What it shows Server setup Whether the cron is running and how to set it up. If EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED is off, also the worker command to keep running under supervisor. See Cron & queues. Scheduled tasks Every task from the schedule. A task that's late asks whether the scheduler's cron is running. Queues Waiting and running jobs per queue (webhooks, notifications, default, video, reports) and the oldest waiting since. Failed jobs Newest first, with the first line of the error. Retry puts one back on its queue; Retry all does them all; Delete removes one that no longer needs to run. When a task or job fails, the team is alerted by email, Slack and the bell (at most once per job per 15 minutes). Set where alerts go in Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications›System alerts.

System checks the server and shows a red card when something is unsafe: Warning Fix The .env file can be opened from the web Point the domain at the public folder, or upload the package's .htaccess. Then change the database password and replace APP_KEY (put the old one in APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS). The check runs once an hour. This server isn't set up as a live server Set APP_ENV=production and APP_DEBUG=false in .env, then run the commands shown. Visitors reach the app through a proxy it doesn't trust Add EDRAMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES=cloudflare (behind Cloudflare) or * (behind your host's CDN or load balancer) to .env. The "not set up as live" warning also appears on the Dashboard's Needs attention.
Server logs opens the log viewer, where developers can read the application's logs. Logs are JSON lines with a request ID, and passwords, tokens, receipts and codes are masked.

Team & roles manages who can use the Studio and what they can do. Everyone gets the least access their job needs, and every change is in the audit log. Permission area: Team & roles View See members, invites and roles Edit Add, invite, change roles, disable and enable Owner Create, edit and delete roles; reset two-factor your-domain.com/admin/team 1234567 1InviteEmails a link to set their own password. 2Add memberAdds them with a temporary password you share. 3The team at a glanceMembers, two-factor coverage, open invites and roles. 4MembersSearch by name or email. 5A memberRole, last sign-in, two-factor and status; change role, disable, reset 2FA. 6PermissionsWhat each role can do in each area: Edit, View or None. 7New roleOwner only: start blank or from a copy. Team & roles: overview cards, the members table and the permissions matrix.

Invite by email (recommended) Add with a temporary password Choose Invite, enter their Email and pick a Role. Choose Send invite. They get an email link to set their own password. It works once and for 7 days. Pending invites are listed with who invited them and when the link expires: Resend sends a new link (the old one stops working), Revoke cancels it. Choose Add member: Name, Email, Role and a Temporary password of at least 12 characters (or Generate a password). Choose Add member. Share the password with them in person or over a secure channel. It's never shown again. At their first sign-in they must choose their own password before anything else.

Action What happens Change role Applies from their next click. Disable They're signed out at their next click and can't sign in. Their history stays; you can Enable them again with the role they had. Reset 2FA Owner only. Their authenticator and recovery codes stop working; they set it up again (at once, if the team requires it). Protections: nobody can change the Owner. A member can't change their own role or status, and can't give anyone more access than they have.

The Permissions matrix shows what each role can do in each of the 18 areas: None, View or Edit (Edit includes View). The Owner always has everything; that row can't be edited. Only the Owner creates, edits and deletes roles: New role: give it a name and Start from a blank role or a copy of an existing one, then set each area. Edit: change the levels and the refund limit: the most one refund may be, in a currency you choose. Empty means no refunds. Delete: only a role nobody uses. The four templates (Admin, Content Manager, Moderator, Finance & Support) keep their names; copy one to make a role with another name. See Roles and access for what each template can do.

eDrama shows rewarded ads only: ads a viewer chooses to watch to unlock one episode or earn bonus coins. Setting them up has two halves: Where What In the app (this page) Your AdMob app ID for Android and for iOS. In the Admin Panel The ad unit IDs, daily limits and coin amounts, per region: Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Ads. See Ads & rewards. Replace the test IDs The app ships with Google's sample test app IDs: ca-app-pub-3940256099942544~3347511713 (Android) and ca-app-pub-3940256099942544~1458002511 (iOS). Every build shows test ads and earns nothing. An Android release build without admob.appId prints a WARNING about the test ID; iOS doesn't warn, so check Info.plist yourself before you publish. What Where Format AdMob app ID, Android admob.appId in android/key.properties or android/local.properties ca-app-pub-…~… (with a ~) AdMob app ID, iOS GADApplicationIdentifier in ios/Runner/Info.plist ca-app-pub-…~… Ad unit IDs (unlock and Rewards, per platform) Admin Panel › Monetization › Ads, per region. Not in the app. ca-app-pub-…/… (with a /) Server-side verification callback AdMob › each ad unit https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/admob-ssvCopy WRTeam common app guideGoogle AdMobCreate the AdMob account and the Android and iOS apps, with screenshots. (opens in a new tab)
In AdMob, choose Apps › Add app, once for Android and once for iOS. Each app gets an app ID that looks like ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 (note the ~).

Put the Android app ID in android/local.properties (not committed to version control) or android/key.properties: android/local.properties admob.appId=ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 The build reads it and writes it into the Android manifest for you: don't edit AndroidManifest.xml by hand.
Put the iOS app ID in ios/Runner/Info.plist: ios/Runner/Info.plist <key>GADApplicationIdentifier</key> <string>ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~0987654321</string>

The app asks for ad consent where the law requires it (using Google's consent message), and viewers can change their choice in App›Me›Settings›Privacy choices. On iOS it also shows Apple's tracking prompt, with this text from Info.plist: This lets eDrama show ads that fit you better. Your choice doesn't change what you can watch. Change the app's name in that line when you rebrand. The consent messages themselves come from Google's User Messaging Platform: create them in AdMob › Privacy & messaging, a GDPR message for Europe and an IDFA explainer for Apple's tracking prompt (plus a US state regulations message if you serve the US).

After the IDs, everything else is in the Admin Panel: ad units per platform and region, daily limits, coins per ad and server-side verification, which makes sure an ad really was watched before anything is unlocked or paid. Follow AdMob integration.
documents.s: The rest happens on the server

documents.t: The app is drawn from one colour file and two fonts. Screens never use a colour directly; they use roles such as "background" or "accent", so changing a value here changes it everywhere.

The accent colours buttons, switches, progress and highlights. You have two ways to set it: From the Admin Panel (no new release): Admin Panel›Settings›Branding›Theme colour. The app picks it up at its next start, and the Admin Panel and Creator Portal use the same colour. The default in the app: used until the server sends one. lib/app/config/app_config.dart /// The brand accent until the admin panel sends one. static const AppAccent defaultAccent = AppAccent.greenlight; The built-in accents, defined at the bottom of lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dart: Accent On dark On light Greenlight (default) #C6EB3B #4A7300 Ember #FF8A4C #B4410E Iris #9B8CFF #4F3FD0 Rose #FF7FA8 #B21C55 Aqua #4FDCCB #0B6E64 Each accent has a brighter value for buttons and a darker one for text on the light theme, where the bright one would be too faint.

lib/app/config/app_config.dart /// The theme a new install starts in; viewers can change it in Settings. static const ThemeMode defaultThemeMode = ThemeMode.dark; Use ThemeMode.light, ThemeMode.dark or ThemeMode.system (follow the phone). Viewers can change it in App›Me›Settings›Appearance.
documents.s: Light or dark to start with

documents.t: lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dart lists every colour by name, with a note on where it's used. The important ones: Colour Default Used for coin #F2C25B Coins only: the coin, prices, balances. Nothing that isn't a coin is gold. coinGradient #FFD98A → #E9AE3F Buttons that buy coins (Top up). vip / vipGradient #F1DDB3, champagne to bronze VIP badges, the VIP card and VIP buttons. like #FF4F6E Likes and hearts. streak and the flame* colours Orange to deep red The daily streak's flame and card. titleTiers Grey → teal → blue → purple → pink → orange → red Streak titles, lowest to highest. darkBackground #000000 The dark theme's background: pure black. lightBackground #F6F6F3 The light theme's background. dark… / light… Surfaces, text, borders and status colours for each theme. Also change the Android notification colour (brand_green in android/app/src/main/res/values/brand_colors.xml) and the splash screens, which are drawn before the app starts (Logo & icons).

The app uses two fonts, both free under the SIL Open Font License: Instrument Serif Italic for big headings, Geist for everything else. Put your font files in assets/fonts/YourFont/. Declare them in pubspec.yaml under fonts:, with a family name and each file's weight (and style: italic where needed). In lib/core/theme/app_typography.dart, change the family names in AppFonts at the top of the file. Run flutter pub get, then rebuild. note Keep a font with good coverage of the languages you offer. Hindi, Arabic and other scripts may need their own font family; test each language after a font change.

The app reaches your server through two addresses, both in one file: lib/app/config/app_config.dart. There are no build flags or environment files: whatever this file says is what the build uses. Setting What it's for Example apiBaseUrl Every request the app makes: catalogue, unlocks, purchases, sign-in. It ends in /api/v1/. https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/ shareBaseUrl The address in links viewers share (…/s/12). No trailing slash. It must serve your share pages and link files. https://admin.your-domain.com Open lib/app/config/app_config.dart. Change the two values: lib/app/config/app_config.dart /// Your admin panel's API, ending in `/api/v1/`. static const String apiBaseUrl = 'https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/'; /// Where shared links point, e.g. `https://yourdomain.com/s/12`. No /// trailing slash. static const String shareBaseUrl = 'https://admin.your-domain.com'; Run the app again. The Home screen now shows your own catalogue (or the demo data, if you imported it). warning apiBaseUrl must end with /api/v1/, including the last slash. shareBaseUrl must not end with a slash. Use https://. Phones refuse plain http:// addresses in release builds.
documents.s: Connect the app to your server

documents.t: At every start, the app asks your server for its configuration. That's how these things reach viewers without a new release: the app name and theme colour from Admin Panel›Settings›Branding, the feature switches and maintenance mode from Admin Panel›Settings›App & support, the minimum and latest app versions (to ask viewers to update), push limits and quiet hours, the daily spend cap choices, the viewer's region: its currency, coin packs, VIP plans and ad units, every language other than English. So after your first build, most changes happen in the Admin Panel. You rebuild the app only for changes to the files listed in Prerequisites.
documents.s: What the app learns from the server

documents.t: If you change shareBaseUrl, the same domain must also be set as the Android shareHost and in iOS's associated domains, or shared links open in the browser instead of the app. See Deep links.

The same file holds the rest of the app's own settings. The download's values are on the left; change them as you rebrand. Setting In the download What it does apiBaseUrl https://your-domain.com/api/v1/ Your Admin Panel's API (above). shareBaseUrl https://your-domain.com Where shared links point (above). appName 'eDrama' The name on the splash and Home header until the Admin Panel's App name arrives (Name & package name). appId 'com.example.edrama' Your application ID / bundle ID. YouTube's player needs it (Name & package name). companyName 'WRTeam' Your company's name, read out for the logo at the foot of the splash. showCompanyLogo true Shows "Made by" your company on the splash. Replace assets/branding/company_logo.svg, or set false (Logo & icons). defaultThemeMode ThemeMode.dark The theme a new install starts in. Viewers can change it. defaultAccent AppAccent.greenlight The accent until the Admin Panel sends one (Colours & fonts). followDeviceLanguage true Start in the phone's language when you offer it (Languages). signInWithGoogle, signInWithApple, signInWithPhone, signInWithEmail true The sign-in methods. Turn off any you haven't set up in Firebase (Defaults & limits). protectScreen true Blocks screenshots and recordings of the player (Defaults & limits). Prices, coin packs, VIP plans, ad unit IDs, feature switches, languages and texts are not here: they come from the Admin Panel. The AdMob app IDs are the exception: they're build settings (Ads setup).

When a viewer shares a series, an episode or a creator, the link looks like https://admin.your-domain.com/s/12. On a phone with the app installed, that link should open in the app. Without the app, it opens a share page with the poster, synopsis and store buttons. For that, three places must agree on the domain, and your server must prove the app is yours. Use this page, not the common guide eDrama's link setup is its own (two hosts, link files served by your server and website), so follow this page rather than the common guide's deep-link page.

Setting File Value shareBaseUrl lib/app/config/app_config.dart https://admin.your-domain.com shareHost android/app/build.gradle.kts admin.your-domain.com applinks: ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements applinks:admin.your-domain.com android/app/build.gradle.kts manifestPlaceholders["shareHost"] = "admin.your-domain.com" manifestPlaceholders["websiteHost"] = "www.your-domain.com" ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements <key>com.apple.developer.associated-domains</key> <array> <string>applinks:admin.your-domain.com</string> <string>applinks:www.your-domain.com</string> </array> The app opens these addresses: Domain Paths Share host /s/… (a series), /c/… (a creator) Website host /series/…, /creators/…, and also /s/… and /c/… The website host is your public website's domain (see Website). If you don't use the website, set it to your share domain too.

Your server publishes the two "proof" files phones check: /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android) and /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS). Fill them in through .env: .env EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE=com.yourcompany.drama EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256=AB:CD:EF:... EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID=TEAMID.com.yourcompany.drama SHA-256: your release signing certificate's fingerprint. If Google Play signs your app (Play App Signing), copy it from Play Console › Setup › App signing. Separate several with commas. iOS app ID: your Apple Team ID (Apple Developer › Membership), a dot, then your bundle ID. Run php artisan config:cache. Then open https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json in a browser: it should show your package name. While these are empty, share links still work: they just open the web page.
Your public website serves the same two files itself, from the app settings in the Admin Panel. See Website.

Server files: open both addresses below in a browser. Each should list your package name or app ID; empty values mean the .env lines are missing (run php artisan config:cache after adding them). https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.jsonCopy https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-associationCopy Android: after installing a release build, run adb shell pm get-app-links com.yourcompany.drama. Both hosts should say verified. Without a computer: Settings › Apps › your app › Open by default lists your domains as verified links. iOS: send yourself a link in Notes or Messages and long-press it: Open in "Your App" should appear. End to end: share a series from the app to yourself and tap the link on a phone with the app installed: it opens on that series. On a phone without the app, the link opens a share page with your store buttons.

lib/core/constants/constant.dart holds the defaults a viewer starts with and a few timings. Several are only used until the server answers: your Admin Panel's values then take over. Setting Default Meaning spendLimitSteps 100, 300, 600, 1000 The daily coin limits a viewer can pick, until the server sends its own (Admin Panel›Settings›Payments›Daily spend cap). defaultSpendLimit 300 The limit a new viewer starts with, until the server says. heroAutoAdvance 5 seconds How long each featured series stays on the Home slider. A swipe restarts the wait. defaultAutoplayNext on Play the next episode when one ends. Viewers can turn it off. defaultDataSaver off Start every episode at 360p, then sharpen. Viewers can turn it on. dataSaverPreloadAt 60% With data saver on, how far into an episode the next one starts loading. upNextCountdown 3 seconds The countdown on the Up Next card before the next episode plays. cleanExitFade 2 seconds In the player's clean view, how long the way out stays before fading. playbackSpeeds 0.75×, 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2× The player's speed menu. emailVerifyPoll 3 seconds How often the "check your email" page checks whether the link was opened. emailResendSeconds 30 How long before the verification email may be sent again. defaultQuietHours 23:00 to 08:00 Quiet hours in the viewer's time, until the server sends its own (Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications). defaultHaptics on Vibration feedback. Viewers can turn it off.
Prices, coin amounts, ad limits, rewards, VIP plans and feature switches all come from the Admin Panel, so they can change without a new release. See Monetization and App & support.

Turn off any sign-in method you haven't set up in Firebase, in lib/app/config/app_config.dart: lib/app/config/app_config.dart static const bool signInWithGoogle = true; static const bool signInWithApple = true; static const bool signInWithPhone = true; static const bool signInWithEmail = true; Apple's rule Apple requires Sign in with Apple on iOS whenever Google sign-in is offered. Keep both on, or both off. Phone sign-in can also be switched off for everyone from Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Features, without a new release.

lib/app/config/app_config.dart static const bool protectScreen = true; While on, Android blocks screenshots and recordings of the player, and iOS hides the video while the screen is being recorded or mirrored (the viewer sees "Screen recording is on"). Turn it off only if your content may be captured freely.

Firebase is Google's app platform. eDrama uses it for viewer sign-in, push notifications, App Check (proof that requests come from your real app), crash reports and analytics. The app and your server must use the same Firebase project. WRTeam common app guideFirebase setupCreate the Firebase project, install the Firebase CLI and run flutterfire configure, with screenshots. (opens in a new tab) Do this after changing the package name Firebase apps are tied to your package name and bundle ID. Change those first (Name & package name).
Open the Firebase console and choose Create a project. Give it a name and finish the steps (Google Analytics is optional).

The download has no Firebase files: they belong to a Firebase project, so you make your own. Until you do, the Android build stops (no google-services.json), Xcode can't find GoogleService-Info.plist, and the placeholder firebase_options.dart stops the app at start with Firebase is not configured yet. The project's Firebase keys are generated, not typed by hand. Terminal, in the app folder npm install -g firebase-tools firebase login dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli flutterfire configure --project=your-project-id --out=lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart Choose android and ios. The command registers both apps in your Firebase project and writes three files: File Platform lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart (replaces the placeholder) Both android/app/google-services.json Android ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist iOS Keep the --out path eDrama reads its options from lib/app/config/, not from FlutterFire's default lib/firebase_options.dart. Without --out, the app keeps the placeholder and won't start.

Google and phone sign-in on iPhone return to the app through two URL schemes. In ios/Runner/Info.plist › CFBundleURLSchemes, replace the two placeholders: Placeholder Replace with Used by com.googleusercontent.apps.YOUR_REVERSED_CLIENT_ID The REVERSED_CLIENT_ID value from GoogleService-Info.plist Google sign-in app-1-YOUR_SENDER_ID-ios-YOUR_APP_HASH The Encoded App ID shown for your iOS app in Firebase › Project settings Phone sign-in ios/Runner/Info.plist <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key> <array> <string>com.googleusercontent.apps.123456789012-abcdefg</string> <string>app-1-123456789012-ios-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b</string> </array>
documents.s: Fill in the iOS URL schemes

documents.t: In the Firebase console, open Authentication › Sign-in method and enable: Provider Needed for Notes Anonymous Guests Required. Every viewer starts as a guest. Google "Continue with Google" Add your Android app's SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints in Project settings › Your apps: the debug key, your upload key and, after your first Play release, the Play App Signing key. Then download google-services.json again. Apple "Continue with Apple" Required on iOS when Google is offered. Set up the Apple provider with your Apple Developer account; until then, the button reports a failure. Phone "Continue with Phone" SMS codes. Needs Firebase's pay-as-you-go Blaze plan (common guide › Firebase billing). Can be switched off from the Admin Panel. Email/Password "Continue with Email" The app verifies the address with a link. Turn off in app_config.dart any method you don't enable here (Defaults & limits). Under Authentication › Settings › Authorized domains, add your Admin Panel's domain. The Creator Portal signs creators in from it in the browser.

The full setup, with the APNs key, the server keys and a test push, is on Push notifications. In short: Android works with no extra step: google-services.json is enough. The app sorts notifications into four channels, so viewers can mute one kind in Android's settings: Channel ID Name viewers see in Android's settings drops New episodes account Account & purchases offers Offers quiet Quiet hours (low importance, silent) iOS needs an APNs key: in your Apple Developer account, create a key with Apple Push Notifications service enabled, download it, then upload it in Firebase under Project settings › Cloud Messaging › Apple app configuration. In Xcode, check that the Push Notifications capability is on.

App Check proves requests come from your real app on a real device. The app already uses Play Integrity on Android and App Attest (falling back to DeviceCheck) on iOS in release builds. In Firebase, open App Check › Apps and register the Android app with Play Integrity and the iOS app with App Attest. For testing: a debug build prints an App Check debug token in its log on first run. Add it in App Check › your app › Manage debug tokens, so your test phones and emulators pass. On your server, start with EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=monitor in .env (checks and logs, refuses nothing), then run php artisan config:cache. When the logs show your real app passing, switch to EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=enforce. caution Don't use enforce until the build from the store passes App Check. Older builds and test devices without a debug token would be refused.

Your server checks every viewer's sign-in token, sends pushes, and signs creators in, so it needs the same project's keys. In Firebase, open Project settings › General. Copy the Project ID. Under Your apps, add a Web app if you don't have one, and copy its apiKey and authDomain. Open Project settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key. A JSON file downloads. In the Admin Panel, open Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications, find the Firebase card and fill in: Project ID, Service account JSON (paste the whole file), Web API key and Auth domain (needed for the Creator Portal's sign-in). Choose Save, then Test connection. tip Send yourself a test push from Admin Panel›Audience›Push›Test send after signing in to the app with your own email. It's the quickest way to check the whole chain. More: Firebase integration.

You set up your computer once. After that, every build of eDrama (and every update) uses the same tools. Do it before you open the project. WRTeam common app guideFlutter and Java JDK setupInstalling Flutter, the Java JDK and your IDE, with screenshots for Windows, macOS and Linux. (opens in a new tab)

These come from the project itself. Use them exactly: a newer Flutter or Java may need code changes. Tool Version Set in Flutter 3.47.7 .fvmrc Dart 3.13 or newer (comes with Flutter) pubspec.yaml › environment Java (JDK) 17 android/app/build.gradle.kts Gradle 9.3.1 (downloaded by the project's wrapper) android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties Android Gradle Plugin / Kotlin 9.1.0 / 2.4.0 android/settings.gradle.kts Android Runs on Android 7.0 (API 24) and newer; targets API 36 minSdk in build.gradle.kts; Flutter's default target iOS Runs on iOS 15.0 and newer ios/Podfile, Xcode deployment target
documents.s: The versions eDrama is built with

documents.t: With FVM (recommended) Without FVM FVM (Flutter Version Management) reads the project's .fvmrc and installs the matching Flutter for this project only, so other Flutter projects on your computer aren't affected. Terminal dart pub global activate fvm # or: brew install fvm (macOS) cd path/to/edrama-app fvm install # installs Flutter 3.47.7 from .fvmrc fvm use 3.47.7 fvm flutter --version From now on, write fvm flutter … wherever these pages say flutter …, and fvm dart … for dart …. In VS Code or Android Studio, point the Flutter SDK path at .fvm/flutter_sdk in the project. Download Flutter from the Flutter archive, choosing 3.47.7 for your system, unzip it to a folder such as ~/development/flutter, and add its bin folder to your PATH: ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc export PATH="$HOME/development/flutter/bin:$PATH" On Windows, add C:\src\flutter\bin to Environment Variables › Path. Then open a new terminal: Terminal flutter --version # should say Flutter 3.47.7 If you already use another Flutter version for other projects, use FVM instead: it keeps both.

Install Android Studio, then its Flutter and Dart plugins (Settings › Plugins). Install the SDK parts. Android Studio › Settings › Languages & Frameworks › Android SDK: SDK Platforms: Android 16 (API 36). SDK Tools: Android SDK Build-Tools, Android SDK Command-line Tools, Android SDK Platform-Tools and Android Emulator. Use Java 17. Android Studio's own JDK works: Settings › Build, Execution, Deployment › Build Tools › Gradle › Gradle JDK › a JDK 17. From the terminal, check with java -version. Accept the Android licenses: Terminal flutter doctor --android-licenses Create an emulator (Device Manager › Create device), or connect an Android phone with Developer options › USB debugging on.

The iOS app can only be built on a Mac. Install Xcode from the Mac App Store, open it once and let it install its components (including an iOS simulator). Point the command-line tools at it and accept the license: Terminal sudo xcode-select --switch /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch sudo xcodebuild -license accept Install CocoaPods (it installs the iOS libraries): Terminal brew install cocoapods # or: sudo gem install cocoapods pod --version Sign in to Xcode with your Apple ID: Xcode › Settings › Accounts › +. Building for a real iPhone and for the App Store needs an Apple Developer Program membership (see Signing & certificates).

The app's Firebase files are generated with the Firebase CLI and the FlutterFire CLI (Firebase). Install them now: Terminal npm install -g firebase-tools # needs Node.js: nodejs.org firebase login dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli Make sure Dart's global tools are on your PATH ($HOME/.pub-cache/bin on macOS and Linux), so flutterfire runs from any folder.

Terminal flutter doctor -v Every line should be ticked: Flutter, Android toolchain, Xcode (on a Mac), Android Studio and Connected device. Fix anything it marks before you continue; its message says how. flutter doctor says Fix Android license status unknown flutter doctor --android-licenses cmdline-tools component is missing Install Android SDK Command-line Tools in Android Studio's SDK Manager CocoaPods not installed brew install cocoapods Xcode installation is incomplete sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch Unable to find bundled Java version Set Gradle JDK to a JDK 17 in Android Studio

VS Code with the Flutter and Dart extensions, or Android Studio with the Flutter plugin. For iOS signing, capabilities and archives you'll also open the project in Xcode: always open ios/Runner.xcworkspace, never Runner.xcodeproj. Next: with your computer ready, start the first build: your package name comes first.

Viewers buy coin packs (one-time purchases) and VIP (a subscription) through Google Play and the App Store. The app itself needs no code change: it asks your server which products to show, then the store sells them, and your server checks every receipt before coins land. What you must do is create the same products in each store, with IDs that match the ones in Admin Panel›Money›Monetization. The Series Pass is paid in coins, so it needs no store product.

Your app exists in Play Console and App Store Connect, with your own package name. Google Play: a payments profile is set up for your developer account, and a build with billing has been uploaded to a testing track at least once. Play Console only lets you create products after that. App Store: the Paid Applications Agreement is signed, with your banking and tax details, in App Store Connect › Business. WRTeam common app guideIn-app purchasesPayments profile, agreements, and creating products in Play Console and App Store Connect, with screenshots. (opens in a new tab)
You can keep these or change them, as long as the store and the Admin Panel agree.
documents.s: The product IDs the installer created

documents.t: Pack Google Play product ID App Store product ID 300 + 300 bonus (first top-up offer) coins_300_first com.edrama.app.coins.300.first 500 + 50 bonus coins_500 com.edrama.app.coins.500 1000 + 200 bonus (Popular) coins_1000 com.edrama.app.coins.1000 2000 + 600 bonus coins_2000 com.edrama.app.coins.2000 5000 + 2000 bonus (Best value) coins_5000 com.edrama.app.coins.5000 Create these as consumable products (they can be bought again and again).

Plan Google Play App Store Weekly Subscription vip, base plan weekly com.edrama.app.vip.weekly Monthly Subscription vip, base plan monthly com.edrama.app.vip.monthly Yearly Subscription vip, base plan yearly com.edrama.app.vip.yearly Create these as auto-renewable subscriptions, step by step below. On iOS, put the three in one subscription group. No free trials eDrama's VIP never starts with a free trial or a cut-price introductory offer: it's one of the fair-play rules. The server refuses a subscription the store started with a free trial (and leaves a Google Play one unacknowledged so Google refunds it). Don't add offers or trials to these products in either store.

On Google Play, a subscription holds one or more base plans, each with its own billing period and prices. eDrama stores both IDs for each VIP plan, so either layout works: one subscription with three base plans (subscription vip, base plans weekly, monthly, yearly), or three subscriptions with one base plan each. Play Console › your app › Monetize with Play › Products › Subscriptions › Create subscription. Enter the Product ID (such as vip; it can't change later) and a name. This is the Google Play subscription ID in eDrama. In the subscription, Add base plan: Base plan ID weekly (the Google Play base plan ID in eDrama), type Auto-renewing, billing period Weekly, and the prices per country (Google can fill other countries from one price). Save, then Activate the base plan. Repeat for monthly and yearly. Don't create offers (free trials or intro prices) on these base plans.

On the App Store, subscriptions live in a subscription group. A viewer can hold only one subscription of a group at a time and can move between them, so put all three VIP plans in one group. App Store Connect › your app › Monetization › Subscriptions › Create a subscription group, such as VIP. Add a group localization (the name viewers see in their subscription settings). In the group, Create a subscription for each plan: a Reference Name (such as VIP Weekly), the Product ID (such as com.yourcompany.drama.vip.weekly; it can never be reused: this is the App Store product ID in eDrama), the Subscription Duration (1 Week, 1 Month or 1 Year), the price, a localization (display name and description) and Review Information (a screenshot of the VIP screen and a short note). Drag the three into levels in the group, with your best-value plan (often yearly) at the top. Apple uses the order for upgrades and downgrades. Leave Introductory Offers, Promotional Offers and Offer Codes empty. Your first subscriptions are reviewed with an app version: select them in the version's In-App Purchases and Subscriptions section before you submit it.

Admin Panel›Money›Monetization, pick the region, open VIP plans and Edit each plan: the Price in the region's currency (matching the store price), the Google Play subscription ID, the Google Play base plan ID, the App Store product ID, the Perks (one per line) and Offered in the app. Do it for every region you sell in: the store IDs are usually the same everywhere, the prices are per region. A price of zero, or an ID or perk that names a trial, is refused.
documents.s: Enter the IDs in the Admin Panel

documents.t: Each store sets its own price tiers per country. Set the store prices to match what you entered in the Admin Panel for each region, as closely as the tiers allow. The coin store in the app lists your Admin Panel prices (with a line such as "Prices in INR · India"), and the store confirms its own price at checkout: if the two differ, viewers notice.

The server needs keys to check receipts and to hear about refunds and renewals: Google Play setup: a service account, and real-time developer notifications. App Store setup: an In-App Purchase key, and App Store Server Notifications.
documents.s: Connect the stores to your server

documents.t: Store How Subscription renewals while testing Google Play Add your testers in Play Console › Settings › License testing, then install the app from a testing track. Speeded up: weekly and monthly renew about every 5 minutes, yearly about every 30 minutes. App Store Create a Sandbox tester (App Store Connect › Users and Access › Sandbox) and sign in with it on a TestFlight or development build. No server setting changes: purchases are checked with the live App Store, then the sandbox. Speeded up: 1 week ≈ 3 minutes, 1 month ≈ 5 minutes, 1 year ≈ 1 hour. Buy a coin pack and check that it appears on Admin Panel›Money›Transactions with its receipt checks passed. After a few VIP renewals, the test subscription shows on the viewer in Admin Panel›Audience›Users with Auto-renew on.

The app never decides how many coins a purchase gives: it sends the store's receipt to your server, which checks it with the store and then adds the coins or turns VIP on. Each renewal, cancellation, refund or chargeback reaches eDrama through the stores' server notifications, and VIP is extended or ended to match. Set them up in Google Play and App Store. Viewers get a reminder 24 hours before every renewal charge, and cancel from the app's VIP screen, which opens the store's own subscription page. Restore purchases in the coin store claims anything that was interrupted.

The app ships with one language built in: English. Every other language is a file you upload in the Admin Panel; the app downloads it at its next start. So you add a language, fix a typo or roll back a translation without releasing a new version.

All English text is in assets/l10n/template.json, as "key": "text" pairs grouped by screen: assets/l10n/template.json { "splash.tagline": "Stories that hook you. Prices that don't.", "unlock.title": "Keep watching", "store.title": "Top up" } Change the text, never the keys. Words in braces, such as {coins} or {app}, are filled in by the app: keep them as they are. tip You can also change English without a release: upload an English pack in the Admin Panel. Keep the app's template.json and the server's resources/language-packs/app-template.json the same so the two never disagree.

Languages are added in the Admin Panel, not in the app: Open Admin Panel›Settings›Regions & languages and choose Add language: its code (such as hi or pt-BR), name and native name (such as हिन्दी), and whether it is right to left. Choose Files on its row, download the Sample JSON (the English file with every key) and translate the text. Upload it under Mobile app and turn on Offered in the app. Full details: Regions & languages. Hindi is already on A fresh install lists Hindi as offered in the app, but no Hindi file comes with it. Before you launch, upload its app file, or edit Hindi and turn off Offered in the app. Otherwise viewers who pick Hindi see English.

With followDeviceLanguage = true (the default in app_config.dart), the app starts in the phone's language when you offer it. Otherwise it uses your default app language from the Admin Panel. Viewers can switch any time in App›Me›Settings›App language, and pick their language during onboarding. Series names, synopses, category names, push messages and legal pages can also be translated per language in the Admin Panel; viewers see them in their language when a translation exists.
documents.s: How the app picks a language

documents.t: For Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and similar languages, tick Right to left when you add the language. The app turns its whole layout around automatically.

All of the app's brand images live in assets/branding/. To rebrand, replace each file with yours under the same name: nothing in the code needs to change. 1234 1Brand markedrama_mark.png: the mark alone. It draws itself as the app starts. 2Logoedrama_logo_dark.png (on dark) or edrama_logo_light.png (on light). 3Tagline“Stories that hook you. Prices that don’t.” Change it in assets/l10n/template.json (splash.tagline). 4Made bycompany_logo.svg and company_logo_light.svg. Hide it with showCompanyLogo = false. The splash screen as the app starts: the brand mark and the logo, the tagline, and the company logo at the bottom.

File What it is Tips edrama_mark.png The mark alone, on a transparent square. Also the source of the app icons. edrama_logo_dark.png Mark and name together, with a light name, for dark backgrounds. Both logo files share one shape: 2197 × 512 px. If yours differs, change brandLogoAspect in lib/core/constants/app_assets.dart. edrama_logo_light.png The same with a dark name, for light backgrounds. coin.svg The coin, in full colour. Shown wherever coins appear. coin_mono.svg The coin in one colour (drawn black, tinted in the app). For toasts and buttons. vip.svg / vip_mono.svg The VIP crown, in colour and in one colour. company_logo.svg / company_logo_light.svg "Made by your company" at the foot of the splash, for dark and light. SVG recommended. Never recoloured. To hide the company logo, set this in lib/app/config/app_config.dart: static const bool showCompanyLogo = false;

WRTeam common app guideApp iconIcon sizes, adaptive icons and the flutter_launcher_icons options. (opens in a new tab) Replace the four files in assets/branding/launcher/, keeping their names: ic_launcher.png: the full icon (1024 × 1024 recommended), ic_launcher_background.png and ic_launcher_foreground.png: Android's adaptive icon layers (the foreground already leaves Android's safe margin), ic_launcher_monochrome.png: Android's themed (single-colour) icon. Generate every size for both platforms: Terminal dart run flutter_launcher_icons

The very first screen is drawn by the phone's own system, before the app's code runs: your mark centred on black. dart run flutter_launcher_icons doesn't change it, so replace these images yourself, at the same sizes: Platform Image Background Android 12 and newer splash_icon.png in each android/app/src/main/res/drawable-*dpi/ folder brand_black in values/brand_colors.xml (#000000) Android 11 and older launch_mark.png in the same folders, drawn by drawable*/launch_background.xml the same brand_black iOS LaunchImage.png, @2x and @3x in ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/LaunchImage.imageset/ the view's background colour in ios/Runner/Base.lproj/LaunchScreen.storyboard (open it in Xcode) The animated splash that follows is drawn by the app from your brand images above.

Android draws the small notification icon in one colour: Replace android/app/src/main/res/drawable-*/ic_stat_edrama.png with your icon, white on a transparent background, in each density folder. Change brand_green in android/app/src/main/res/values/brand_colors.xml to your accent colour.
The app's interface icons are chosen in lib/core/constants/app_icons.dart; the bottom bar's tab icons are the SVGs in assets/icons/tabs/. Change them only if you want a different icon style.

Your app needs its own name and its own package name (on iOS, bundle ID): a unique identifier such as com.yourcompany.drama that the stores use to tell your app apart from every other app. Choose it carefully: it can't change once the app is published. WRTeam common app guidePackage nameWhy the package name matters, how to pick one, and changing it in a Flutter project. (opens in a new tab)

There are three places, because the platforms read the name under the icon before the app starts: Where File Setting Inside the app (splash, Home header, share text) until the server sends its own lib/app/config/app_config.dart appName Under the icon on Android android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml android:label="eDrama" Under the icon on iOS ios/Runner/Info.plist CFBundleDisplayName (or Display Name in Xcode › Runner › General) iOS permission prompts (photo library, camera, ad tracking) ios/Runner/Info.plist NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, NSCameraUsageDescription and NSUserTrackingUsageDescription: each sentence names "eDrama", so change it to your app's name lib/app/config/app_config.dart static const String appName = 'eDrama'; static const String companyName = 'WRTeam'; companyName is read out for the company logo at the bottom of the splash screen. tip Inside the app, the name from Admin Panel›Settings›Branding›App name wins once the server answers, so keep both the same.

Android iOS Open android/app/build.gradle.kts and change both namespace and applicationId: android/app/build.gradle.kts namespace = "com.yourcompany.drama" // … applicationId = "com.yourcompany.drama" Move MainActivity.kt to match: in the download it lives in android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/edrama/. Create the folders com/yourcompany/drama/, move the file there, delete the old folders, and change its first line to package com.yourcompany.drama. Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace in Xcode. Select Runner › Signing & Capabilities and change Bundle Identifier (this sets PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER) for every build configuration. Choose your Apple Team for signing. The download has none, so iOS builds fail until you pick one. The RunnerTests target uses com.example.edrama.RunnerTests: change it to match, such as com.yourcompany.drama.RunnerTests. With automatic signing, Xcode registers the capabilities the app already uses for your new App ID: Push Notifications, Sign in with Apple, Associated Domains and App Attest. Then update the same value in app_config.dart. YouTube's embedded player requires it as the referrer: lib/app/config/app_config.dart static const String appId = 'com.yourcompany.drama'; Or rename it automatically The change_app_package_name tool renames the Android and iOS IDs and moves the Kotlin folder in one go: Terminal, in the app folder dart pub add --dev change_app_package_name dart run change_app_package_name:main com.yourcompany.drama Check the places above afterwards, and set appId in app_config.dart yourself: the tool doesn't touch it.

Everything else that uses the package name: Where What to set Firebase Add apps with the new IDs and run flutterfire configure again (Firebase). Do this step first, Firebase second. Admin Panel In Admin Panel›Settings›Payments: Package name on the Google Play card, and Bundle ID on the App Store card (Google Play, App Store). Server .env EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE (your application ID) and EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID (your Apple Team ID, a dot, then your bundle ID, such as ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.drama) (Deep links).

The viewer app is a Flutter project: one codebase that builds both the Android and the iOS app. You set it up on your own computer, point it at your server, give it your name and look, and build the release files you upload to Google Play and the App Store.

Tool Version Why Flutter 3.47.7 exactly (the project pins it in .fvmrc) Builds the app. Dart 3.13 or newer (comes with Flutter) Flutter's language. Android Studio A recent version Android SDK, emulator and signing tools. Java (JDK) 17 or newer Needed by Android's build tools. Xcode A recent version, on a Mac Only for the iOS app. CocoaPods A recent version, on a Mac Installs iOS libraries. Firebase CLI and FlutterFire CLI Latest Connect the app to your Firebase project (Firebase). The app runs on Android 7.0 and newer and iOS 15 and newer, on phones and tablets. Installing and checking these tools step by step: Set up Flutter. Use FVM to get the exact Flutter version FVM (Flutter Version Management) reads .fvmrc and installs the matching Flutter for this project only: fvm install then use fvm flutter instead of flutter. Using a different Flutter version is the most common cause of build errors. info Setting up Flutter, Android Studio and Xcode on your computer is done once and follows the official guides: Flutter install, Android Studio, Xcode.
documents.s: What you need on your computer

documents.t: The app comes as edrama-app-<version>.zip. It leaves out everything tied to WRTeam's own accounts, so a few things must be filled in before the first build. The project's own FIRST_BUILD.md lists the same steps in short. In the download What it means Fix it in Package name com.example.edrama A placeholder application ID and bundle ID Name & package name No Firebase files The Android build stops and the app won't start until you generate them Firebase YOUR_… URL schemes in Info.plist Google and phone sign-in on iPhone can't return to the app Firebase Server https://your-domain.com/api/v1/ A placeholder: the app loads nothing until it's your server Connect to your server Link hosts your-domain.com and www.your-domain.com Share and website links can't open the app Deep links Google's test AdMob app IDs Every build shows test ads and earns nothing Ads setup android/key.properties.example, no keystore and no Apple team Release builds can't be signed for the stores yet Release build WRTeam common app guideCommon app guideSteps that are the same for every WRTeam Flutter app (installing Flutter, Firebase, AdMob, in-app purchases, store accounts and publishing), with screenshots. These pages add everything specific to eDrama, and link to the matching common-guide page on each topic. (opens in a new tab)

Set up Flutter and the Android and iOS tools on your computer. Give it your package name first: Firebase and the stores are tied to it. Connect Firebase: the app doesn't build or start without its files. Connect it to your server by changing two addresses, then run it on an emulator or your phone. Make it yours: name, logo and icons, colours and fonts, defaults and languages. Connect services: push notifications, ads, in-app purchases and share links. Get ready to release: check the permissions and platform settings, set up signing and certificates, and build the release. Publish to the stores, then tell your server about the new version.

documents.s: Each topic, here and in the common guide

documents.t: The project keeps everything a rebrand touches in a handful of files, each marked Reskin here at the top. You don't need to edit any screen code. To change Edit App name, server address, share domain, default theme and accent, sign-in methods, screen protection lib/app/config/app_config.dart Firebase keys lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart (generated), android/app/google-services.json, ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist Colours lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dart Fonts AppFonts in lib/core/theme/app_typography.dart, and fonts: in pubspec.yaml Defaults and limits lib/core/constants/constant.dart Logo, coin, VIP badge, company logo The files in assets/branding/ (keep the same names) App icon The files in assets/branding/launcher/, then dart run flutter_launcher_icons Icons lib/core/constants/app_icons.dart API paths lib/core/network/api_endpoints.dart (only if your server's differ) English text assets/l10n/template.json Name under the icon android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, ios/Runner/Info.plist Package name / bundle ID android/app/build.gradle.kts, the MainActivity.kt folder, Xcode Share and website link domains android/app/build.gradle.kts, ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements AdMob app IDs android/local.properties or android/key.properties, ios/Runner/Info.plist Prices, coin amounts, ad limits, VIP plans, feature switches and every language except English are not in the app: they come from your Admin Panel, so you change them without releasing a new version.

The project is already configured for both platforms. This page lists what's there, why each item exists, and the few you change when you rebrand. Use it when you fill in the stores' privacy forms, so your answers match what the app does.

Setting Value Where Minimum Android 7.0 (API 24) minSdk in android/app/build.gradle.kts Target Android API 36 (Flutter's default for 3.47.7) targetSdk (from Flutter) Java 17 build.gradle.kts Code shrinking R8 on for release (shrink, optimise, obfuscate) build.gradle.kts

The app itself declares two permissions; the libraries it uses add the rest when Android builds the app. Permission Added by Why POST_NOTIFICATIONS The app Pushes on Android 13+. Asked once, when the viewer first shows interest, never at launch. VIBRATE The app Touch feedback on taps, unlocks and errors (viewers can turn it off). INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE Flutter, Firebase, video player Everything online, and noticing when the connection drops. WAKE_LOCK, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, com.google.android.c2dm.permission.RECEIVE Firebase Cloud Messaging Receiving pushes. com.android.vending.BILLING In-app purchases Coin packs and VIP through Google Play. com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_TOPICS Google Mobile Ads (AdMob) Rewarded ads. Declare "Yes, my app uses advertising ID" in Play Console. BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE Firebase Analytics Where an install came from. The app asks for no camera, location, contacts or storage permission on Android: profile photos are picked through the system's photo picker.

Setting Value Why Backup allowBackup="false", no device-to-device copy The app's data is a cache of your server's, tied to this install; a new phone signs in instead. Launch mode singleTop Tapping a push or a link reuses the open app. App links Two https hosts with autoVerify Share and website links open the app (Deep links). Notification defaults Icon ic_stat_edrama, colour brand_green, channel drops (Push notifications) AdMob app ID ${admobAppId} from admob.appId Filled in by the build; don't edit the manifest (Ads setup) Screen protection FLAG_SECURE while the player is open, when protectScreen is on Blocks screenshots and recordings of episodes (Defaults & limits) You change: only android:label (the name under the icon) and the two link hosts in build.gradle.kts.
Setting Value Where Minimum iOS 15.0 ios/Podfile and the Runner target's deployment target Devices iPhone and iPad iPad is supported, so App Store Connect asks for iPad screenshots too

ios/Runner/Info.plist: Key Value in the download Change it? CFBundleDisplayName eDrama Yes: the name under the icon NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription "Choose a photo for your eDrama profile." Yes: name your app NSCameraUsageDescription "Take a photo for your eDrama profile." Yes: name your app NSUserTrackingUsageDescription "This lets eDrama show ads that fit you better…" Yes: name your app. Shown in Apple's tracking prompt (Ads setup) GADApplicationIdentifier Google's test AdMob app ID Yes: your AdMob iOS app ID CFBundleURLTypes › CFBundleURLSchemes Two YOUR_… placeholders Yes: from your Firebase files (Firebase) SKAdNetworkItems Google's ad network IDs No: AdMob needs them to attribute ads UIBackgroundModes remote-notification No: pushes in the background ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false No: the app only uses standard encryption (HTTPS), so App Store Connect doesn't ask the export-compliance question on every build LSApplicationQueriesSchemes mailto, message No: lets Help open the email app NSAppTransportSecurity › NSAllowsLocalNetworking true No: only allows plain http to local addresses while developing; your server must still be https FlutterDeepLinkingEnabled true No: links open the right screen CFBundleShortVersionString, CFBundleVersion From pubspec.yaml No: change version: in pubspec.yaml instead (Release build)

ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements: Entitlement Value Change it? com.apple.developer.associated-domains applinks:your-domain.com, applinks:www.your-domain.com Yes: your share host and website host (Deep links) aps-environment development No: Xcode sets production for App Store builds com.apple.developer.applesignin Default No: Sign in with Apple com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment production No: App Check with App Attest Each needs its capability on your App ID. With automatic signing, Xcode adds them when you pick your team (Signing & certificates).

Store question Answer for eDrama Google Play › Advertising ID Yes, the app uses it (AdMob). Google Play › Data safety and Apple › App Privacy Collected: email or phone number (sign-in), user ID, purchase history, app interactions (watching, likes, comments), crash logs and diagnostics (Crashlytics), device or other IDs (ads, push). Encrypted in transit. Viewers can delete their account in the app. Apple › Export compliance Standard encryption only (already answered by ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false). Apple › Tracking Yes if you show personalised AdMob ads to iPhone viewers who allow tracking; the app shows Apple's prompt first. Check these against what you actually turn on (for example, without phone sign-in you don't collect phone numbers), and against your privacy policy.
documents.s: What this means for the store forms

documents.t: You have signed release builds (Release build). This page takes them to Google Play and the App Store, then tells your server about the new version. Google Play$25 once. Review usually takes hours to a few days.→App Store$99 a year. Review usually takes one to three days.→

You need Notes Privacy policy URL Publish it in Admin Panel›Settings›Legal pages; it lives at https://admin.your-domain.com/legal/privacy. Both stores require it. Terms of service URL https://admin.your-domain.com/legal/terms. Support email or URL The one in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support. A reviewer account php artisan edrama:review-account review@your-domain.com makes an email-and-password account that needs no inbox (Server commands). Your server live Reviewers use the real app: your catalogue, prices and sign-in must work. Clear the demo data first if you don't want reviewers to see it. Products created Coin packs and VIP subscriptions in both stores (In-app purchases). Screenshots and icon Phone screenshots (and iPad, for the App Store), a 512 × 512 icon for Play, a 1024 × 500 feature graphic for Play.

Pick your store: Google Play App Store WRTeam common app guidePlay Store deploymentDeveloper account, store listing, content rating and release, with screenshots of every Play Console screen. (opens in a new tab) Developer account. Create one at Play Console ($25, once). Choose Organization (needs a D-U-N-S number) or Individual. Complete identity verification and, for paid products, a payments profile. Register your package name and signing key for Android developer verification (Signing). Create the app. Create app: name, default language, App (not game), Free (in-app purchases are still allowed), and accept the declarations. Store listing. Main store listing: app name (30 characters), short description (80), full description (4,000), the 512 × 512 icon, the 1,024 × 500 feature graphic and at least two phone screenshots. App content (Policy › App content), answer every section: Privacy policy: your /legal/privacy URL. App access: All or some functionality is restricted: add the reviewer's email and password. Ads: Yes, my app contains ads. Content rating: the questionnaire; answer for the dramas you'll publish. Target audience: 18+ or 13+ to suit your catalogue. Don't target children. Data safety: as in Permissions & platform settings. Advertising ID: Yes, used for advertising and analytics. Upload to internal testing first. Testing › Internal testing › Create new release › upload app-release.aab, add release notes, roll out, and add your testers' emails. Products can be created once a build is uploaded (In-app purchases). Closed testing, if Google asks. New personal developer accounts must run a closed test before production (currently at least 12 testers opted in for 14 days in a row). Organization accounts can go straight to production. Production. Testing passed: Production › Create new release, promote the build (or upload it), choose the countries, and Send for review. Use a staged rollout (such as 20%) for updates. After the first release: copy the App signing key SHA-256 into Firebase and EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 (Release build). WRTeam common app guideApp Store deploymentDeveloper account, App Store Connect record, signing, upload and review, with screenshots. (opens in a new tab) Developer account. Enrol in the Apple Developer Program ($99 a year). Organizations need a D-U-N-S number. Agreements. App Store Connect › Business: sign the Paid Applications Agreement and add banking and tax details. Without it, purchases and subscriptions can't be tested or sold. Create the app record. App Store Connect › Apps › + › New App: iOS, the name (30 characters), primary language, your bundle ID (it appears once Xcode or the developer portal registered it), and a SKU (any reference of yours). App information: category (Entertainment), the age rating questionnaire, privacy policy URL, and App Privacy answers (Permissions & platform settings). Upload the build. Archive and upload from Xcode, or upload the .ipa with Transporter (Release build). It appears under TestFlight after Apple processes it (often 10 to 30 minutes). Test with TestFlight. Add internal testers (your team) and try sign-in, a coin purchase with a Sandbox account, and a push. External testers need a short Beta App Review. Prepare the version. On the version page: screenshots for iPhone 6.9" (or 6.5") and iPad 13" (the app supports iPad), promotional text, description, keywords, support URL, the build, and under In-App Purchases and Subscriptions select your coin packs and VIP plans (their first review happens with the app). App Review information. Sign-in required: the reviewer's email and password. Notes: explain that episodes unlock with coins, one ad or VIP, and where to find a free episode. Submit for review. Choose Manually release if you want to pick the launch moment, or a phased release for updates. Common App Review answers Sign in with Apple: offered, because Google sign-in is (keep signInWithApple on). Account deletion: viewers can delete their account in the app (App›Me›Settings›Delete account). Restore purchases: in the coin store and the wallet. Subscriptions: the VIP screen shows the price, period and terms before purchase, and opens Apple's subscription page to cancel.

Open Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›App versions and, for each platform: Field What to enter Latest The version you just published, such as 1.0.1. Older builds are offered the update. Minimum supported Raise it only when an old build must stop working; those builds then must update. Store link Your Google Play or App Store page. The update screen, share pages and the website's store buttons use it.
documents.s: After each release: tell the server

documents.t: Raise version: in pubspec.yaml, such as 1.0.1+2: the number after + must go up for every upload (Release build). Build with the same upload keystore (Android) and team (iOS). Upload as a new release (Play) or a new version (App Store), with release notes. Update Latest in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support once it's live.

Pushes go from your server through Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to the phone. On iPhone, FCM hands them to Apple's APNs. The app's code is already complete: you only connect the accounts. WRTeam common app guideNotifications (FCM)Firebase Cloud Messaging for a WRTeam Flutter app, with screenshots of the Firebase and Xcode screens. (opens in a new tab) Admin PanelPush, drop alerts, replies Your serverQueue, daily cap, quiet hours Firebase Cloud Messaging APNsiPhone only The phone
Firebase is connected: flutterfire configure has made google-services.json and GoogleService-Info.plist. Your server's queue runs: pushes are sent from it.

Nothing to add in the app: google-services.json is enough. What's already set up: Already in the project Where The notification permission (POST_NOTIFICATIONS). On Android 13 and newer it's asked once, when the viewer first shows interest (such as following a series), never at launch. AndroidManifest.xml, push_service.dart The small icon (white mark on transparent) and its tint colour drawable-*/ic_stat_edrama.png, brand_green in values/brand_colors.xml (Logo & icons) The default channel for messages without one: drops AndroidManifest.xml The app sorts notifications into four channels, so viewers can mute one kind in Android's settings without missing the rest: Channel ID Name viewers see in Android's settings drops New episodes account Account & purchases offers Offers quiet Quiet hours (low importance, silent)

iPhones only receive pushes through Apple, so Firebase needs an APNs key from your Apple Developer account. Create the APNs key. Apple Developer › Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles › Keys › +: give it a name, tick Apple Push Notifications service (APNs), Continue, Register, then Download the .p8 file. Apple lets you download it once: keep it safe. Note its Key ID, and your Team ID (top right of the developer site). Upload it to Firebase. Firebase console › Project settings › Cloud Messaging › Apple app configuration › your iOS app › APNs Authentication Key › Upload: the .p8 file, its Key ID and your Team ID. One key works for both development and production builds. Check the capabilities in Xcode. Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace › Runner › Signing & Capabilities. The project already has Push Notifications and Background Modes › Remote notifications; with automatic signing, Xcode adds them to your App ID. If either is missing, add it with + Capability. On iPhone the system asks the viewer for permission the same way: once, when they first show interest, never at launch. Development and production aps-environment in Runner.entitlements says development. Xcode switches it to production by itself when you archive for the App Store or TestFlight, so you don't edit it.

Your server sends every push, so it needs the same Firebase project's keys: Firebase console › Project settings › General: copy the Project ID. Project settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key: a JSON file downloads. Admin Panel › Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications › Firebase card: enter the Project ID and paste the whole Service account JSON. Save, then Test connection: it checks the key with FCM without sending anything. On the same page you set the push limits (at most 3 a day per viewer to start, quiet hours 23:00 to 08:00 in each viewer's own time), the wording of the automatic notifications in each language, and system alerts (Notifications).

Install the app on a real phone and sign in with the same email as your Admin Panel account. Allow notifications when asked (follow a series to be asked). Admin Panel › Admin Panel›Audience›Push › New push › Test send. It says Test sent to N of your devices. The push arrives on the phone, and in the app's inbox.

At start the app registers the phone's FCM token with your server (POST /api/v1/devices). A token that changes is sent again by itself. Drop alerts (new episodes of followed series), replies to comments, new series from followed creators and VIP renewal reminders are sent automatically.
