You send others from Admin Panel›Audience›Push (Push). Each viewer gets at most the daily cap; the rest wait for the next day. Pushes due in quiet hours wait until they end. The in-app inbox still gets every message. Viewers choose which kinds they get in the app's App›Me›Settings›Notifications.

Symptom Check Test connection fails The Project ID and the service account JSON are from the same Firebase project as the app's files. Nothing arrives anywhere The queue isn't running (Cron & queues); look for failed jobs on Admin Panel›System›System. Android works, iPhone doesn't The APNs key isn't uploaded in Firebase, or Push Notifications is missing in Xcode. Test on a real iPhone. "Test sent to 0 of your devices" The app on your phone isn't signed in with your Admin Panel email, or notifications are off for it. Some viewers get fewer pushes The daily cap and quiet hours are working as designed (Notifications).
This page builds the files you upload to the stores. Signing is set up once on Signing & certificates; uploading and store review are on Publish to the stores.

The version lives in one place, pubspec.yaml: pubspec.yaml version: 1.0.1+2 Part Here Android iOS Rule Version name 1.0.1 versionName CFBundleShortVersionString What viewers see. Also what you enter as Latest in the Admin Panel. Build number 2 versionCode CFBundleVersion Must be higher for every upload, even a re-upload of the same version. The build reads both from pubspec.yaml: don't edit them in Gradle or Xcode.

The app points at your server (Connect to your server). Name, package name, logo, icons and colours are yours. Firebase is connected and the sign-in methods are on (Firebase). Your AdMob app IDs replace the test IDs (Ads). Your own shareHost, websiteHost and applinks: domains replace your-domain.com (Deep links). flutter analyze prints "No issues found!" and flutter test passes. The version is raised in pubspec.yaml: version: 1.0.0+1 means version 1.0.0, build 1. Every upload to a store needs a higher build number.

Google Play needs every update signed with the same key. Create it once and keep it safe: if you lose it, you can't update your app. Terminal keytool -genkey -v -keystore ~/upload-keystore.jks -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias upload Copy android/key.properties.example to android/key.properties and fill it in (never share it or commit it to version control; the download's android/.gitignore already leaves out key.properties and *.jks): android/key.properties storeFile=/Users/you/upload-keystore.jks storePassword=your-store-password keyAlias=upload keyPassword=your-key-password admob.appId=ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 storeFile is read from the android/app/ folder when it's a plain file name; a full path works too. The build reads this file automatically. Without it, a release build is signed with the debug key, which Google Play refuses.
Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace in Xcode, select Runner › Signing & Capabilities and pick your Team for the Release configuration. The download has none, so flutter build ipa fails until you do.

The project includes tool/build_release.sh, which runs flutter build <target> --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=build/debug-info: obfuscated Dart code, with the debug symbols kept separately in build/debug-info for crash reports. Clean once before a store build: Terminal, in the app folder flutter clean && flutter pub get Google Play (.aab) App Store (.ipa) APK (direct download) Terminal tool/build_release.sh appbundle Upload build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab in Play Console (Publish to the stores). Google Play only accepts app bundles (.aab), signed with your upload key (Signing). R8 also shrinks and obfuscates the Android code; Crashlytics uploads its mapping file by itself. Two ways, both on a Mac, with your Team chosen in Xcode (Signing): From the terminal Terminal cd ios && pod install && cd .. tool/build_release.sh ipa The file is build/ios/ipa/*.ipa. Upload it with Apple's Transporter app (sign in, drag the .ipa in, Deliver). From Xcode flutter build ios --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=build/debug-info Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace, choose Any iOS Device (arm64) as the destination. Product › Archive. When the Organizer opens: Distribute App › App Store Connect › Upload. Make sure Xcode shows Push Notifications, Background Modes, Sign in with Apple, Associated Domains and App Attest under Signing & Capabilities. Terminal tool/build_release.sh apk The file is build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk. Useful for testing, or for the website's direct-download button.

Run it on a real phone before uploading: release builds behave differently from debug ones (no debug banner, real App Check, real ads once your IDs are set). Terminal flutter run --release Check sign-in, an episode playing, a purchase with a test account, a push, and a shared link.

Error Fix Keystore file not found / keystore password was incorrect Check storeFile and the passwords in android/key.properties (Signing). Play Console: You uploaded an APK or Android App Bundle that was signed in debug mode android/key.properties is missing, so the debug key was used. Play Console: Version code 1 has already been used Raise the number after + in pubspec.yaml. WARNING: this release build uses Google's TEST AdMob app ID Set admob.appId (Ads setup). No profiles for '…' were found / Signing requires a development team Pick your Team in Xcode › Signing & Capabilities. pod install errors cd ios && pod repo update && pod install. On Apple silicon, update CocoaPods first. File google-services.json is missing Run flutterfire configure (Firebase).

Keep build/debug-info for every release you ship: stack traces from an obfuscated build can only be read with it. To see readable Dart stack traces in Crashlytics, upload it with the Firebase CLI: Terminal firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload --app=<your Firebase app ID> build/debug-info

Google Play signs the app it delivers with its own app signing key. Copy that key's SHA-256 from Play Console › Test and release › App integrity › App signing, then: add it to EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 in the server's .env, after your upload key's and separated by a comma, so share links keep opening the app (Deep links); add it (and its SHA-1) to your Android app in Firebase, so Continue with Google works for Play installs (Firebase).
documents.s: After the first Google Play release

documents.t: Open Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›App versions and, for each platform, fill in: Field Meaning Latest The version you just published. Viewers on older builds are offered the update. Minimum supported Builds below this must update before they can use the app. Raise it only when an old build breaks something. Store link Your app's Google Play or App Store page. Used by the update screens, share pages and the website's store buttons. The On latest column shows how many devices seen in the last 30 days run the latest version.

Google Play's Data safety form and Apple's App Privacy answers must cover sign-in (email, phone), purchases, ads (AdMob) and crash reports (Crashlytics). Link your privacy policy: https://admin.your-domain.com/legal/privacy (published from Admin Panel›Settings›Legal pages). If you use YouTube episodes, your privacy policy must say the app uses YouTube API Services and link to Google's privacy policy (YouTube). Store reviewers need to sign in. Create an email-and-password account for them on the server with php artisan edrama:review-account (Server commands) and put it in Play Console (App content › App access) and App Store Connect (App Review Information). Apple reviewers can buy with their sandbox account; nothing needs switching on the server. WRTeam's common guide walks through the store listings: Play Store and App Store.

Before the first run, three things must be in place, because the download ships with placeholders (what's in the download): your own package name, your Firebase files (the Android build stops without google-services.json, and the app won't start without firebase_options.dart), your server's address in app_config.dart. Then run it: if it opens and shows your catalogue, your computer is set up correctly. Open the project. Unzip the app source code and open the folder in Android Studio or VS Code. Check your Flutter version. Terminal, in the app folder flutter --version It should say 3.47.7. (With FVM: fvm install, then use fvm flutter.) Not set up yet? See Set up Flutter. Install the packages. flutter pub get Generate the code files. Some files (ending in .g.dart and .freezed.dart) are generated from others. They are included, but regenerate them after changing anything marked @riverpod or @freezed: dart run build_runner build Start an emulator or connect your phone (with USB debugging on, for Android). Run it. flutter run The app opens on the splash screen, then onboarding, then Home with your server's catalogue (or the demo data, if you imported it). For iOS, run pod install in the ios folder once before the first iOS build.
Before a release, these should all pass: Terminal dart format lib test flutter analyze # should print: No issues found! flutter test

Problem Fix Errors mentioning a Dart or Flutter version Use Flutter 3.47.7. Undefined name errors in .g.dart files Run dart run build_runner build. iOS build fails at pod install In ios/, run pod repo update then pod install. Android build complains about Java Point Android Studio at JDK 17 or newer (Settings › Build Tools › Gradle › Gradle JDK). The app shows "No internet connection" The emulator has no network, or the server address is wrong (Connect to your server). Android build stops: File google-services.json is missing Run flutterfire configure (Firebase). The app stops at start: Firebase is not configured yet firebase_options.dart is still the placeholder: run flutterfire configure with --out=lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart. Nothing loads, or Server error apiBaseUrl is still your-domain.com, isn't https://, or doesn't end in /api/v1/. If you turned on EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=enforce, test with monitor first.

Every store build is signed: the stores use the signature to prove an update comes from you. This page sets up signing once for Android and iOS, and lists every key and certificate eDrama's services need. Keep your keys forever Your Android upload keystore and its passwords, and Apple's .p8 keys, can't be downloaded again. Store them in a password manager and keep an off-site backup. Never commit them to Git or send them by email.

Key Who holds it What it signs Upload key You (upload-keystore.jks) Every .aab you upload to Play Console App signing key Google (Play App Signing, on by default for new apps) The app Google delivers to phones If you lose the upload key, Play Console support can reset it. The app signing key never leaves Google.
documents.s: Two keys: upload key and app signing key

documents.t: Create the keystore once, from the app folder: Terminal, in the app folder keytool -genkey -v -keystore android/app/upload-keystore.jks \ -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias upload It asks for a keystore password, your name and organisation, and a key password (pressing Enter reuses the keystore password). Copy android/key.properties.example to android/key.properties and fill it in: android/key.properties storePassword=your-store-password keyPassword=your-key-password keyAlias=upload storeFile=upload-keystore.jks admob.appId=ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 storeFile is read from android/app/ when it's a plain file name; a full path works too. admob.appId is your AdMob app ID (Ads setup). Build a release (Release build). android/app/build.gradle.kts reads key.properties by itself. Without it, the release falls back to the debug key, which Google Play refuses. The download's android/.gitignore already leaves out key.properties, *.jks and *.keystore.

Firebase and your server identify your app by its signing fingerprints. There are three you may need: Fingerprint How to get it Used by Debug key keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android Firebase (Google sign-in in debug builds) Upload key keytool -list -v -keystore android/app/upload-keystore.jks -alias upload Firebase; EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 (release builds installed outside Play) App signing key Play Console › Test and release › App integrity › App signing Firebase (Google sign-in for Play installs); EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 (share links) Or list the debug and release fingerprints in one go: Terminal, in the app folder cd android ./gradlew signingReport # gradlew.bat signingReport on Windows Where each goes: Firebase › Project settings › your Android app › Add fingerprint: the SHA-1 and SHA-256 of all three. Then download google-services.json again (or re-run flutterfire configure). Without them, Continue with Google fails. Server .env › EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256: the SHA-256 of the app signing key and the upload key, comma-separated, so share links open the app (Deep links).

Google now asks developers to register each package name and its signing key in Play Console before an app can be installed on certified Android devices, by uploading a signed APK that proves you own the key. WRTeam common app guideAndroid developer verificationRegister your package name and signing key in Play Console, for a new or an existing package name. (opens in a new tab)
An Apple Developer Program membership (yearly). Your Team ID is shown at the top right of the developer site. Xcode signed in with that Apple ID: Xcode › Settings › Accounts.

Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace › Runner target › Signing & Capabilities. Tick Automatically manage signing and pick your Team (for Debug, Profile and Release). The download has none. Set your Bundle Identifier (Name & package name). Xcode then registers the App ID with the capabilities the project already uses, and creates the certificates and provisioning profiles for you: Capability Why eDrama needs it Push Notifications Pushes through APNs (Push notifications) Background Modes › Remote notifications Handling pushes in the background Sign in with Apple "Continue with Apple" Associated Domains Share and website links open the app (applinks: entries, Deep links) App Attest Firebase App Check on real iPhones (Firebase)

In the Apple Developer portal: create an App ID with your bundle ID and the capabilities above, an Apple Distribution certificate (from a certificate signing request made in Keychain Access), and an App Store provisioning profile for that App ID. Download the profile, untick Automatically manage signing and choose it for the Release configuration.
documents.s: Manual signing (if your team requires it)

documents.t: These are keys (.p8 files), not certificates. Each is downloaded once. Key Create it in Paste it into APNs key (Apple Push Notifications service) Developer › Keys Firebase › Cloud Messaging (Push notifications) In-App Purchase key App Store Connect › Users and Access › Integrations › In-App Purchase Admin Panel › Settings › Payments › App Store (App Store) Sign in with Apple key (only for "Continue with Apple" on Android) Developer › Keys, with Sign in with Apple, plus a Services ID Firebase › Authentication › Apple provider Sign in with Apple outside iPhone On iPhone, "Continue with Apple" works with the capability alone. On Android, Firebase signs in through Apple's web flow, which needs a Services ID, your Team ID, a Sign in with Apple key and its Key ID in Firebase › Authentication › Sign-in method › Apple. Add Firebase's handler (https://<your-project>.firebaseapp.com/__/auth/handler) as a return URL on the Services ID. Firebase's guide: Apple sign-in on Android.
documents.s: Keys from Apple your services need

documents.t: Item Platform You'll need it again for upload-keystore.jks + passwords Android Every update on Google Play android/key.properties Android Every release build on this computer SHA-1 / SHA-256 fingerprints Android Firebase, EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256, developer verification Team ID iOS EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID (TEAMID.bundle.id), Firebase APNs key (.p8) iOS Push notifications In-App Purchase key (.p8) iOS Verifying purchases on your server Sign in with Apple key (.p8) + Services ID Android "Continue with Apple" on Android

The Episode editor in AI Studio turns your kept takes (and videos made outside eDrama) into one episode. You arrange, trim and split pieces on a timeline; nothing ever changes the original files. When it's right, export: the finished video goes to the episode through the normal upload pipeline. your-domain.com/creator/titles/13/ai-studio?tab=episodesFull page · scroll 12345678910 1StepsCharacters, Shots, Episodes. The editor is the Episodes step. 2Your Gemini keyAI Studio runs on your own Gemini key, added on Your account, so it has no eDrama limits. 3Episode tabsOne tab per episode, and New episode. 4Import videoBring in a video made elsewhere to use on the timeline. 5LibraryTakes by shot and imported videos. Click to preview; drag onto the timeline, or press + to add after the last clip. 6Episode / Clip previewPlays the whole timeline as one episode, or the clip picked in the library. 7PropertiesTrim the selected clip, set its sound or replace it, and the export settings. 8Export checksEach must pass: clips on the timeline, every shot placed, files available, at least 45 seconds. 9ExportRenders the episode once every check passes. 10TimelineV1 video and A1 audio with the playhead: Split, Delete, Ripple, Snap, Close gaps and Add kept takes. AI Studio’s Episodes step, the Episode editor, for a series with no takes yet: the library, the preview, Properties with the export checks, and the V1/A1 timeline.

Add kept takes puts the kept take of every shot not on the timeline yet, in shot order. Drag a take or imported video onto the timeline: drop on a clip to put it before or after, or in empty space to place it there. The + after the last clip adds another video at the end. Select a clip to edit it in Properties: In and Out points (set to the playhead with I and O, or one frame at a time), Volume, Mute this clip, or Use another take of this shot.

Tool Shortcut What it does Split S Splits the clip at the playhead. Delete Delete Removes the clip and leaves a gap (gaps play as black). Delete and close the gap Shift + Delete Removes it and moves the rest left. Ripple R When on, trimming or deleting moves the clips after it. Snap N Snaps to clip edges and the playhead. Close gaps Moves every clip left so nothing plays black. Zoom + / − Zoom in and out; Fit shows the whole timeline. Undo / Redo ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z Mute the audio track The export is silent. The editor saves automatically. If the timeline changed in another tab, it asks you to reload.

Import video brings in a video made outside eDrama. It joins the series' library, ready for any episode. Nothing is sent to Google and nothing is charged. Confirm you own the video or have permission to use it. Limits (defaults): 300 MB, 30 minutes, 200 imported videos per series. If a file can't be read, export it again as MP4 (H.264). You can also merge an episode's existing video with new clips, when the original upload is kept on the server.

Export settings: Frame (same as the first clip, 720p or 1080p), Frame rate (same as the first clip, 24, 25 or 30 fps) and Quality (Standard, High, Best). The panel shows the output, such as 1080 × 1920 · 30 fps · 1:32. Export waits until every check passes: Clips are on the timeline Every shot of the episode is on the timeline Every clip's file is available It's at least 45 seconds long The episode can take a new video (it isn't in review or released) The server can render video If the episode already has a video, you're asked to confirm replacing it. The export goes through Waiting for the server → Gathering the clips → Rendering → Handing to the video pipeline → Processing as an upload. When it's done you get a notice: Episode 3 is assembled. Then send it for review as usual. Labelled as AI-generated Episodes made in AI Studio carry an AI-generated label for the review team, with how each shot was made. Every frame also carries Google's SynthID watermark.

AI Studio helps you make a short drama with Google's Gemini models: create characters who look the same from shot to shot, turn each shot into a storyboard image, generate video takes from it, then cut the takes into an episode. What you make is reviewed like any upload. AI Studio appears in your menu only when the platform has switched it on for your account.

The platform decides how AI Studio is paid for. Your Your account › AI Studio card says which applies to you: Mode What it means for you Your own key You add your own Gemini API key; calls are billed to your own Google account, with no limits from the platform. The platform's key The platform pays, within your monthly allowance and daily limits (shown on your account). You don't add a key. Your choice You may use either. Choose Pay with on your account.

Create a key in Google AI Studio in a Google project with billing switched on. On Your account › AI Studio, choose Add key, paste it and choose Test and save. Google checks it before it's saved. Your key is stored encrypted; only its last 4 characters are ever shown. Test checks it again; Remove stops new calls (calls already sent finish).
Set budget caps your own estimated spend each calendar month (UTC), from $1. You get a notice and an email at 80% and 100%; at 100%, nothing new starts. Leave it blank for no budget.

Open AI Studio and pick a series. It has two tabs, Characters and Shots, and a progress line ("4 characters, 3 with a portrait · 12 shots, 8 with a kept take"). Series look. Write one style line every prompt starts with, such as Realistic, soft daylight, warm colours. Characters. Choose New character: a name and an identity profile (age range, face shape, skin tone, eye colour, hair, build, height, distinguishing marks, usual clothes, voice). The profile is repeated word for word in every prompt, and locks once a storyboard uses it. Portrait. Generate portrait (tick Higher quality for the better image model), or Upload a reference you have the rights to (never a real, recognisable person or a minor). Looks. New look from a preset (Casual, Office, Wedding, Night, Traditional) or your own description. Regenerate, Edit by prompt ("Change only the jacket to red"), and switch between Versions. Shots. On the Shots tab, add a shot with a title and its episode. Pick its cast (each in a look), framing (Close-up, Wide shot, Two-shot, Over-the-shoulder, Walking scene, Conversation), camera (Static, Push in, Pull out, Pan, Tilt, Tracking, Handheld, Orbit), and lines of dialogue with an emotion (neutral, calm, happy, sad, tearful, angry, scared, excited, whispering). Drag shots to reorder them or onto another episode. Storyboard. Generate a still of the shot and approve it. Takes start from it. Takes. Choose the mode (from the storyboard, from start and end stills, or from the cast's images), the resolution and the length (from 3 seconds), and generate. Keep the take you like. Edit take makes a new take from one with your change; the original stays. Episode. Assemble the kept takes in the Episode editor. AI characters drift Characters won't look exactly the same in every image or take. The portrait, the look and the same profile in every prompt keep them close. Check each storyboard before you make takes: takes cost more.

Every button shows an estimate first. Every take asks you to confirm; images ask above a set amount. Now generating shows live progress of every call. You can leave the page; each result appears where it belongs. Google doesn't report progress, so the percentage is estimated; the stage (preparing, making the image, rendering the video, downloading) is real. Message What to do Google blocked this prompt Change the prompt and try again. Your Gemini key was refused Check it on Your account. Your Google project reached its limit Tier 1 allows 40 videos a day; try later. You reached today's limit Limits on the platform's key reset at midnight UTC. We lost Google's answer It may already be on your Google bill: check before trying again. Unused files (rejected storyboards, takes you didn't keep, unused versions) are deleted after 30 days. Anything in use stays.
There are two ways in: apply, or be invited by the team. Either way you end with an invite email.

Open https://your-domain.com/creator/apply (or Become a creator in the app's Me tab). Fill in: Your name: the name you publish under. Email: where the team replies. Use the email you'd like to be invited with. Links to your past work: one per line (YouTube, Instagram, a portfolio or a festival page). Your pitch: what you'd publish, in a few sentences. Choose Send application. The team watches your work, usually within a few days, and emails you either way. If it's a yes, the email has your link to the Creator Portal. If the platform isn't taking applications right now, the form says Applications are closed for now.

The invite email says Welcome to platform, your name, with a Sign in to accept button. The link works once, for 7 days. Open the link. The invite page shows the name you'll publish as and until when the invite is valid. Sign in with the account you use in the app (below). This accepts the invite and makes your creator account Active. If you see… It means This invite link doesn't work A newer invite replaced it, or the link is incomplete. Use the newest email, or ask the team to resend. This invite expired Ask the team to send a new one. This invite was already used Sign in to the Creator Portal with the account you used. A guest account can't become a creator account Sign in with Google, your email or your phone number. This account already belongs to another creator Use a different account.

your-domain.com/creator/login 12345678 1Tagline“Your stories, on every phone.” Set in Settings › Sign-in screen. 2Welcome backCreators sign in with the same account they use in the eDrama app. 3Continue with GoogleOne-tap sign-in with the Google account used in the app. 4Email / PhoneEmail and password, or your phone number and a 6-digit SMS code. 5Email and passwordWith Forgot password? beside the password field. 6Sign inTakes you to Home, or to the Creator Terms first if you haven’t accepted them. 7Create an accountSwitches the card to Create account, for someone new to eDrama. It is the same account they use in the app. 8Not a creator yet?Opens the creator application form. The Creator Portal's sign-in page: the photo stage and tagline on the left, and on the right Continue with Google, the Email and Phone tabs, and Sign in. Sign-in methods: Google, email and password, or phone (when the platform allows it). Sign in with Apple isn't available in the portal. Common messages: That email and password don't match, That code isn't right (check the SMS), That code expired (send a new one), Your browser blocked the Google window (allow pop-ups for the site). If the account you sign in with isn't a creator yet, you see This isn't a creator account yet, with a link to apply. If your account is suspended, you see Your creator account is suspended, with the platform's support email.

Before you can create a series, you read and accept the Creator Terms: a reading page with an outline of its sections, the version and the date it was updated. Read the terms. Tick I have read and agree to the Creator Terms (version N). Choose Accept and continue. When the platform publishes a new version, you're asked to read and accept it again before continuing. Your accepted version and date are on Your account › Agreement.

Comments & reviews (in the menu, or on a series page) gathers what viewers say about your series, so you can thank them, answer questions and share what's coming. your-domain.com/creator/comments-and-reviews 12345678 1RatingThe average of every rating across your series, with how many there are. 2Ratings by starsPick a row to see only those reviews. 3Waiting for your replyReviews and comment threads that still need your answer. 4Reviews / CommentsSwitch between reviews and comment threads. 5FiltersAll series or one, and All or Needs a reply. 6A reviewThe viewer, stars, when, how many episodes they watched, and the text. 7ReplyOne public reply per review. It shows under the review in the app, with your name. 8Post replyViewers get a notification when you reply to their comment. Comments & reviews: the average rating and its breakdown by stars, Waiting for your reply, the Reviews tab with its filters, and a reply being written.

The rating is weighted the way the app ranks series, so a handful of ratings doesn't swing it. Viewers can rate once they've reached episode 3. Choose a star row in the breakdown to see those reviews.

Reviews Comments One public reply per review, shown under the review in the app, with your name. Thank them, answer a question or share what's coming next. If the team has already replied to a review, their reply stays and you can't add one. Your reply joins the comment thread in the app, with your name and a Creator badge. The viewer gets a notification. Waiting for your reply counts the reviews and comment threads you haven't answered. When it's empty: You're all caught up. You can edit or remove your own replies at any time. To report or remove a viewer's post that breaks the rules, contact the platform's team: moderation is done in the Admin Panel.

Choose New series (on Home or My series). You need to have accepted the current Creator Terms first. your-domain.com/creator/titles/createFull page · scroll 12345678 1DetailsTitle, synopsis (up to 280 characters, no spoilers past E3), subtitle, kicker, schedule line and audio languages. 2CategoriesUp to 3. 3Age ratingAll, 13+, 16+ or 18+. 4Other languagesOptional translations. Anything left blank shows the default language’s text. 5ArtworkA 2:3 poster (required, at least 600 × 900) and an optional 16:9 banner (at least 960 × 540). JPG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB. 6Free episodes and priceYour proposal, within the platform’s limits (here at least 5 free, 30 to 90 coins). A reviewer confirms it. 7Where it’s shownEvery region, or only the regions you pick. A reviewer confirms your choice. 8CreateSaves the series as a draft. Then upload episodes and submit it for review. The whole New series form: Details, Other languages, Artwork, Free episodes and price, Where it’s shown, and Create.

Field Notes Name Required. Subtitle A short line under the name on the series page. Kicker A small label above the name on Home. New episodes (schedule line) Such as "New episodes every Friday". Audio languages Press Enter after each. Synopsis Up to 280 characters. It shows before people pay, so no spoilers past episode 3. Categories Up to 3. They decide where viewers find your series. Age rating All, 13+, 16+ or 18+. Other languages Optional translations; empty shows your default text.
Image Size Poster (required) 2:3, at least 600 × 900 Banner (optional) 16:9, at least 960 × 540

This is your proposal; a reviewer confirms it (and may adjust it within the platform's limits) before the series goes live. Field Rule (defaults) Free episodes At least 5. Viewers watch these before they need coins. Coin price per episode Between 30 and 90 coins.

Every region: viewers in every country can find and watch it. Only the regions I pick: when you have the rights only in some countries, or made it for one market. Viewers anywhere else won't find it. Anyone who already unlocked an episode or bought the Series Pass keeps it. Each region lists the countries it covers. A reviewer confirms your choice; if they change it, you get a notice and an email.
Tick: I own this work or have the rights to publish it, including its music, images and text. It's required. Choose Create series: it's saved as a Draft. Next: upload its episodes.

How editing works depends on the status: Status Editing Draft or Changes requested Edit directly. Changes are saved at once. Live Your changes go to the review team as a series update. Viewers keep seeing the series as it is until a reviewer approves. While an update waits, Update in review shows, and you can't send another. In review, Approved, Rejected Can't be changed now. Unpublished Contact the team. If the team changes your series' prices, you get a notice and an email with the reason.

Earnings shows your share of what viewers paid for your series, after store fees and refunds. Bonus coins and your own viewing don't count. The platform pays you under your agreement. your-domain.com/creator/earnings 1234567 1Waiting to be paidWhat the platform still owes you, with your last payout. 2Paid to youEverything paid so far. “Earned” under it is everything from closed months. 3This month so farAn estimate until the month closes. 4Monthly statementsOne row per closed month: coins share, ads, VIP, adjustments, refunds and the total. 5Where it came fromEach series, region and source behind the amounts. 6StatusWaiting for payment, then Paid once the platform records a payout. 7PayoutsEach payment: date, amount, method and reference. Earnings: Waiting to be paid, Paid to you and This month so far, the monthly statements with where each amount came from, and the payouts.

Source How you earn Coins When viewers unlock your episodes or buy your Series Pass with paid coins, you get your share of what those coins are worth. Ads Your share of the region's ad money, in proportion to the verified ad unlocks on your episodes. VIP Your share of the region's VIP money, in proportion to the minutes VIP members watched your locked episodes. Adjustments Corrections by the team (you see the amount). Your share percent is on Your account › Agreement. A change to it applies to new unlocks only. YouTube episodes are free and earn nothing.

A month's statement appears after the month ends. Coins come first; the Ads & VIP part is reviewed by the team and shows In review until they approve it. Each statement line can show the series, the region and the paid coins, and for ads and VIP the verified ad unlocks or minutes. Status Meaning In review Ads and VIP for this month are being reviewed. Approved Final, ready to pay. Waiting for payment / Partly paid / Paid Where the payment stands. Nothing to pay No earnings that month.

The team pays you outside the portal (bank transfer, UPI, PayPal, Wise or other) and records each payment with its date, amount, method and reference, so you can match it to your bank statement. If a later refund takes back more than a month earned, the balance comes off your next statements.

Home is the first page after sign-in. It answers: how are my series doing, and what's waiting on me? your-domain.com/creatorFull page · scroll 12345678 1WelcomeYour series and what the review team said about them, with shortcuts. 2At a glanceSeries (how many need you), Live, In review, Views and New followers over the last 28 days. 3Viewer engagementViews and unlocks across your series, day by day, over the last 28 days. Table shows the numbers. 4Earnings by monthWhat each closed month came to. The Earnings page has the details. 5Your seriesYour newest work, most recently changed first. Click a poster to open it. 6Ratings & reviewsYour average rating, reviews and comments, and how many wait for your reply. 7Needs your attentionSeries where the next step is yours, such as a draft to finish and submit. 8Latest noticesAnd how many are unread. Creator Home: the greeting, the at-a-glance cards, the viewer engagement and earnings charts, your newest series, ratings, Needs your attention and the latest notices.

Each series where the next step is yours, with what to do: Status What to do Draft Finish it and send it for review. Changes requested See the reason and resubmit. Not approved See why in its history. When nothing is waiting: All caught up. Nothing is waiting on you.

Ratings & reviews: your average rating across all series, and how many reviews and comments wait for your reply. Your series: your newest work, most recently changed first, with See all. If you have no series yet, Home suggests starting your first one: add its details, then upload the episodes. note Figures leave out your own viewing, unlocks and follows. They're recounted every 15 minutes.

Notices collects review decisions, your submissions, release-time changes by the team, AI Studio budget alerts and other news. The bell in the top bar shows how many are unread. Open a notice to go to what it's about. Mark as read, or Mark all as read. Most notices also arrive by email.

Open your name at the foot of the sidebar › Your account. Card What's there Profile What viewers see on your page in the app: Photo (JPG, PNG or WebP up to 2 MB) and Bio (with optional translations). Choose Edit profile to change them. Your Verified tick is set by the team. Sign-in How you sign in (Google, email or phone), when you signed in and when the session ends. Preferences Time zone: release times are shown and picked in it. Portal language: change it from the language menu in the top bar. These are for the portal only; your app keeps its own settings. Agreement Your share of what your series earn (coins, Series Passes, ads and VIP), the Creator Terms version you accepted (with Read them), and when your signed agreement was filed. The team changes these; ask them if something looks wrong. AI Studio Who pays for your AI calls, your Gemini key, what you used today and this month, and your monthly budget (AI Studio).

Viewers can open your creator page from any of your series ("Created by"). It shows your photo, bio, verified tick, followers and series, with a Follow button. Followers are told when you publish a new series. (The platform can switch creator pages off.)

The Creator Portal is where invited creators (independent filmmakers, studios, storytellers) publish their own series on your platform. A creator sees only their own work: they create series, upload episodes, send them for review, set release times, follow their stats and reviews, see their earnings, and can use AI Studio. It's at https://your-domain.com/creator. This section is written for creators: share its link with yours. your-domain.com/creator 12345678 1Platform logoThe portal wears the platform’s logo, with the Creators tag. 2New seriesStart a new series from any page. 3MenuHome and Earnings, then My series, Upload episodes, AI Studio, Release schedule, Comments & reviews (with how many wait for your reply) and Notices. 4Portal languageOnly you see the portal in the language you pick. 5Notices bellReview decisions and other news, with the unread count. 6ThemeLight or dark, just for you. 7YouYour account: profile, sign-in, preferences and agreement. Sign out sits beside it. 8Greeting“Good afternoon” and your name, with shortcuts to New series, My series and Notices. The Creator Portal for the demo creator Amara Okafor: the menu on the left, the top bar, and Home.

Create a seriesDetails, artwork, free episodes and price, regions.→Upload episodesStraight from the browser, with subtitles.→Send for reviewEvery series and episode is checked by the team.→Set release timesPick when each approved episode drops.→Talk to viewersReply to reviews and comments.→See earningsMonthly statements and payouts.→
Apply or get invitedThe team accepts you Accept the termsCreator Terms Create a seriesUpload its episodes In reviewThe team checks it LiveViewers watch it EarnYour share, monthly

The portal is part of your Admin Panel's server, at https://admin.your-domain.com/creatorCopy. Before your first creator signs in: Add the Firebase web keys. The portal signs creators in with Firebase in the browser, so it needs the Web API key and Auth domain in Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications › Firebase (Firebase). Allow your domain in Firebase. Firebase console › Authentication › Settings › Authorized domains › Add domain: your Admin Panel's domain, such as admin.your-domain.com. Turn on the sign-in methods creators use in the app: Firebase console › Authentication › Sign-in method (Google, Email/Password, Phone). Phone sign-in on the portal also follows the Phone sign-in switch in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support. Publish the Creator Terms in Admin Panel›Settings›Legal pages. Creators can't create a series until they're published. Set the creator limits: the price range and free episodes in Payments, and the upload limits in Storage & video › Video pipeline. Check it worked: open /creator. The sign-in page shows the sign-in methods. If it says Creator sign-in isn't set up yet, the Firebase web keys are missing. If Firebase says the site isn't allowed, add the domain to Authorized domains.
documents.s: Turn the portal on (for the platform team)

documents.t: New series sits above the menu on every page. The menu has two groups, Overview and Your work: Item What it's for Home Your series at a glance and what needs you (Home). Earnings Statements and payouts (Earnings). My series Every series you've made, by status (My series). Upload episodes Pick a series and upload (Upload episodes). AI Studio Characters, storyboards and video takes, when the platform allows it (AI Studio). Release schedule Every episode not out yet, across your series (Release times). Comments & reviews What viewers say about all your series (Comments & reviews). Notices Review decisions and news from the team (Notices & account).

The portal is in your own language if the platform offers it: pick it from the language menu. Your app keeps its own language. Times are shown in your time zone, which you set in Your account › Preferences. A session lasts 12 hours. If your account is suspended, you're signed out at your next click.

You decide when your approved episodes drop. Times are shown and picked in your time zone. your-domain.com/creator/titles/13/releases 1234567 1Schedule episodesApproved episodes in a range drop one a day at the same time. 2Time zoneTimes you already set stay at the same moment. 3The ruleThe earliest is 2 hours after the review team approves the episode (the platform sets this). 4A release timeIn your time zone. The episode goes out at that moment. 5Not set“Not set: waiting for your time” until you pick one. 6Earliest allowedNo release time can be earlier than this. 7Set time / ClearPick a time no earlier than Earliest allowed, or clear it. Release times for one series: Schedule episodes, the time zone, the rule, and the approved episodes with their release time and earliest allowed time.

Open the series and choose Release times (or Release schedule in the menu for every series at once). On an approved episode, choose Set time. Pick the date and time. The earliest you can pick is shown. Save. It reads Episode 7 drops 12 Dec, 20:00 (Asia/Kolkata). Clear removes a time: the episode stays approved and waits until you set a new one.
Schedule episodes: approved episodes in the range drop one a day at the same time. The first can't be earlier than the delay after approval. Episodes not approved yet are skipped.

When you send new episodes of a live series for review (Submit new episodes on the series page), the dialog has a Hold them for my release times switch. It is off unless you turn it on, and it decides what happens when the team approves those episodes: On: each one waits here until you set when it drops. Off: each one goes out as soon as it's approved.
documents.s: Hold new episodes for your times

documents.t: Release schedule in the menu lists every episode of yours that isn't out yet, across all your series, so you can plan your drops in one place. info The platform's team can change a release time when needed (for example to avoid two big drops at once). When they do, you get a notice.

My series lists every series you've made, with where it stands. your-domain.com/creator/titles 123456 1New seriesStart a new series. 2Status cardsAll series, Drafts, In review, Changes requested, Live. Click one to filter. 3Search, filter, downloadFind a series by name, filter the list or download it. 4A seriesClick to open its page. “Update in review” shows under the name while a change waits. 5StatusDraft, In review, Changes requested, Approved, Live, Rejected or Unpublished. 6EditOpens the series form. My series: the status cards (All series, Drafts, In review, Changes requested, Live) and the list of series with status, episodes and last update.

Draft In review Approved Live From In review, a series can also come back as Changes requested, or be Rejected. A live series can be Unpublished by the team. Status What you can do Draft Edit everything, upload episodes, send for review, delete. In review Wait. The series can't be changed or take new episodes meanwhile. Changes requested Read the reason in History, fix it, send again. Approved Wait for its release time. Can't be changed now. Live Upload and send new episodes; propose changes as an update. Rejected Can't be changed. See why in History. Unpublished Contact the team to change it.

your-domain.com/creator/titles/13 12345678 1Series and statusPoster, name and status, with what changed and when. 2At a glanceEpisodes out, free episodes, price per episode, and views, unlocks and followers over the last 28 days. 3ActionsStats, Comments & reviews, Release times, AI Studio, Upload episodes and Edit series. A draft shows Submit for review and Delete series too. 4CompleteMarks the series complete (no more episodes coming). Clear undoes it. 5EpisodesEach episode’s status and what it needs before you can send it. Rename or delete unreleased ones. 6An approved episodeApproved and waiting for its release time. Set it on Release times. 7AboutSynopsis, categories, subtitle, schedule line, age rating, regions, VIP, ads and Complete. 8HistoryEvery status change and review decision, newest first, with the reviewer’s reason. A live series page: the hero with status and the at-a-glance strip, the actions, the episode list with each episode’s status, About and History. Part What's there At a glance Episodes out; views, unlocks and followers over the last 28 days. Episodes Each episode's status. Before it can be sent: Ready to submit? Yes, or why not (still processing, the upload failed, or shorter than 45 seconds). Rename an episode (leave the name empty to show its number) or Delete one that isn't released and nobody paid for. About Where it's shown, categories, age rating, subtitle, new-episode schedule, whether it's included with VIP, whether ads can unlock episodes, and Complete. History Every status change and decision, by You, the Review team or Automatic, with reasons.
When every episode is out, choose Mark as complete: viewers then see "Complete" instead of the next drop. A new episode clears it; Clear Complete removes it yourself.
Delete series removes a draft for good. You can only delete a draft no viewer has paid for.

Open a series and choose Stats to see how viewers watch it over the last 28 days. your-domain.com/creator/titles/13/stats 123456 1TotalsViews, unlocks and followers gained in the last 28 days. 2What countsMoney is on Earnings. Your own viewing doesn’t count; the numbers refresh every 15 minutes. 3EpisodeEach episode in order. 4Watched to 90%The share of viewers who watched almost all of it. 5Unlocks by methodCoins, ad, VIP, Series Pass, free and granted. 6Went onSuch as “71% to E4”: how many continued to the next episode. Stats for one series: totals for views, unlocks and followers gained, and the per-episode table with views, watched to 90%, unlocks by method and went on. Figure Meaning Views How many times episodes were watched. Unlocks Episodes unlocked, by method. Followers gained New followers of the series. Watched to 90% The share of viewers who reached 90% of the episode: your best sign that an episode holds attention. Went on The share who continued to the next episode. A big drop after one episode is worth a look. Your own viewing, unlocks and follows aren't counted. Numbers refresh every 15 minutes; the page says when they were last counted. Money isn't shown here: see Earnings.
Nothing you make reaches viewers until the platform's review team approves it. Every decision comes with a reason and is kept in your series' History.

Open the series (a Draft or one with Changes requested) and choose Submit for review. Check the list of episodes that go with it: only episodes that are ready are sent. Tick the rights declaration: I own this work or have the rights to publish it, including its music, images and text. Choose Send for review. The series moves to In review and can't be changed meanwhile. You get a notice and an email confirming it arrived.

On a live series, choose Submit new episodes, pick the episodes, tick the rights declaration, and send. Each episode goes to the review team on its own and is released once approved. The series stays live as it is.
documents.s: Send new episodes of a live series

documents.t: The episodes themselves (they watch them), the subtitles, the runtime, the artwork, the synopsis and categories, your proposed free episodes and price, where it's shown, and your rights declaration. Their aim is a decision within 24 hours.

Decision What it means for you Approved A series: it goes live at its release time, or right away if none is set. The reviewer confirms (or adjusts) your free episodes, price and regions. An episode: it's released at its time. Changes requested Read the reason in the series' History (and in the email), fix it, and send again. Earlier decisions stay on record. Rejected It won't go live. The reason is in History. Unpublished A live series or episode was taken down, with the reason. Viewers who unlocked it keep it. Contact the team. Every decision arrives as a notice in the portal (the bell) and an email. If viewers report a problem with one of your live episodes, the team may ask you to fix it: you get the reason by notice and email; the episode stays live meanwhile.
Editing a live series sends your changes as a series update (Create & edit). The reviewer sees each changed field side by side. Approving applies them; otherwise the series stays as it is.
documents.s: Proposing changes to a live series

documents.t: Open a series and choose Upload episodes, or use Upload episodes in the menu and pick the series. A series takes uploads while it's a draft, sent back for changes, or live. your-domain.com/creator/titles/25/upload 123456789 1Your limitsFiles up to 2 GB each, and up to 10 episodes uploading or processing at once (the platform sets both). 2Add YouTube videoWhen the platform allows it. YouTube episodes are always free to watch. 3Drop episode filesMP4, MOV or MKV, or Choose files. Episode numbers are read from file names, such as EP07: check them, then upload. 4ResumesA dropped connection picks up where it stopped. 5EpisodesEvery episode from upload until release: upload → process → ready. 6FailedSays why and what to do, such as “Upload it again”. 7UploadingStill on its way. “Ready to submit?” says what it waits for. 8ReadyProcessed and ready to schedule. 9SubtitlesAdd the episode’s subtitle files. Uploading episodes to one series: your limits, the drop zone, and the Episodes pipeline with each file’s stages and status.

Drag your files onto the page, or choose them. MP4, MOV or MKV. Check each file's episode number: it's read from the file name (EP07, or the first number that isn't a year). Type it if it's missing. Upload. Keep the page open until the files are sent. If your connection drops, the upload carries on where it stopped.

The platform sets these (defaults shown): Files up to 2 GB each. 10 episodes uploading or processing at once; more wait until one finishes. At least 45 seconds per episode. Creators can't submit shorter episodes: upload a longer cut.

You can replace the video of an episode that isn't in review, approved or released by uploading a new file with the same number. An episode in review, approved or already out can't be changed here: upload it as a new episode, or ask the team to replace it.

If the platform allows it, Add YouTube video makes an episode that plays in YouTube's own player. Paste a link to a public video that allows embedding (Shorts suit it best). These episodes are always free: YouTube's rules don't allow charging for them, so they earn nothing. Only add videos you own or may show; use the Credit field for attribution.
On an episode, choose Subtitles: pick the language and an SRT or WebVTT file (UTF-8, times in order and within the episode). A new file replaces the old one for that language.

On the series page, each episode shows Ready to submit?: Shows Means Yes It can be sent for review. Not yet: still uploading or processing Wait a few minutes. No: the upload failed Upload it again (the reason is shown). No: shorter than 45 seconds Upload a longer cut. Next: Send for review.

The words you'll meet in eDrama and in these pages, in alphabetical order. Term Meaning Ad unlock Watching one rewarded ad (30 seconds at most) to unlock one episode. AdMob Google's ad network. eDrama uses its rewarded ads, which the viewer chooses to watch in return for something. Age rating All, 13+, 16+ or 18+, set on each title. API The set of addresses the app uses to ask your server for data and actions, under /api/v1. Append-only A record that is only ever added to, never edited or deleted. The coin ledger and the audit log are append-only. Audit log The history of every important change in the Admin Panel: who did it, when, and why. Auto-unlock An option a viewer can turn on: the next locked episode is unlocked with coins as it starts. Off by default and always held to the daily spend limit. Bonus coins Free coins from the welcome bonus, the daily spin, ads or a coin pack's bonus. They expire and are always spent first. Category (also trope) A genre label such as "Revenge" or "Rebirth". Titles have categories; viewers pick favourites during onboarding. In the code they are called tropes. Coin The app's currency. Bought in coin packs, spent to unlock episodes. A coin's money value is set per region. Coin value What one coin is worth in a region's currency, for example 1 coin = 0.0099 USD. Creator An invited person or studio who publishes their own series through the Creator Portal and earns a share of the revenue. Creator share The percent of a series' revenue that goes to its creator. Default 50%. Cron A server feature that runs a command on a timetable. eDrama needs one cron line that runs every minute. Drop The release of a new episode. "Drop alerts" tell followers about it. Exchange rate How much one unit of a currency is worth in your reporting currency, from a date. ffmpeg A free program that converts video. eDrama uses it to turn uploads into streams. Firebase Google's app platform. eDrama uses it for viewer sign-in and push notifications. Free episodes The first episodes of a series anyone can watch without paying. The first locked one is the paywall. Guest A viewer using the app without signing in. Guests can watch and earn bonus coins but can't buy. HLS The streaming format eDrama uses: the video is cut into small pieces at several qualities, and the player picks the best one for the connection. Home builder The Admin Panel screen where you design the app's Home tab from sections. Idempotent Safe to repeat. If a viewer taps "Unlock" twice or the connection retries, they are charged once. Ledger The list of every coin in and out of a viewer's wallet, with the balance after each line. Paid coins Coins bought with money. They never expire. Price lock Once a viewer unlocks their first episode of a series with coins, their per-episode price for that series can never rise. A lower price still applies. Push notification A message that appears on the phone's lock screen, sent through Firebase. Queue / queue worker A waiting list of background jobs and the process that works through it. Region A group of countries that share a currency, prices, coin packs, VIP plans, ad limits and rewards. Reporting currency The one currency the Dashboard and totals are shown in. Default USD. Rewarded ad An ad the viewer chooses to watch, in return for an unlock or bonus coins. Series Pass One price in coins that unlocks every episode of a series, including future ones. SMTP The standard way servers send email. You give eDrama your email provider's SMTP details. Spend guard (daily spend limit) The most coins a viewer allows themselves to spend in a day. Unlocks past it pause and ask first. SSV (server-side verification) AdMob telling your server directly that an ad was watched to the end, so an ad can't be faked. Streak The number of days in a row a viewer has used the daily spin. Studio Another name for the Admin Panel. Title A series in the catalogue. Every title has an owner type: eDrama Original (made by you), Licensed (from a studio) or Creator. Two-factor (2FA) Signing in with a code from an authenticator app as well as the password. VIP A weekly, monthly or yearly subscription that unlocks every episode with no ads. Welcome bonus Bonus coins a new account gets once per device. Default 100 coins for 7 days.
Before you install anything, it helps to see the whole picture: what runs where, which outside services eDrama connects to, and how an episode and a coin move through the system.

Piece What it is Where it lives Viewer app The Android and iOS app your audience uses. Built from the Flutter project on your computer, then published to Google Play and the App Store. Admin Panel (also called the Studio) Your team's back office. https://your-domain.com/admin Creator Portal Where invited creators publish their own series. https://your-domain.com/creator API The "language" the app uses to talk to your server: every list of series, every unlock and every purchase goes through it. https://your-domain.com/api/v1 Public pages Share pages for a series (/s/…) and a creator (/c/…), legal pages (/legal/…), the creator application form (/creator/apply). On the same server. Public website (optional) A separate marketing website whose sections, look and pages you edit from the Admin Panel's Website screen. Its own address, connected to your server. The Admin Panel, the Creator Portal, the API and the public pages are one Laravel application (Laravel is the PHP framework the server software is written in). You install it once, on one server. To confirm The public website is a separate project that reads its content from your server. Its own source code was not part of the material reviewed for these pages, so this documentation covers only how you manage it from the Admin Panel. See Website.

eDrama works on its own server, but it relies on a few well-known services for things a single server shouldn't do alone. Each one is set up once, mostly by pasting keys into Admin Panel›Settings. Service What eDrama uses it for Needed? Firebase (Google) Viewer sign-in (Google, Apple, phone, email and guest accounts), push notifications, and app attestation. Yes Google Play and App Store Selling coin packs and VIP subscriptions, and telling your server about refunds and renewals. Yes, for the stores you publish in AdMob (Google) Rewarded ads that unlock an episode or pay bonus coins. Only if you use ads ffmpeg A free program on your server that turns each uploaded video into streams at several qualities. Yes, unless you use Cloudflare Stream Amazon S3 / Cloudflare R2 Storing files and videos outside your server's own disk. Optional Cloudflare Stream Processing and streaming videos instead of your server. Optional SMTP email Sending invites, password resets, creator emails and alerts. Strongly recommended Google Gemini AI Studio: generating characters, storyboards and video takes. Optional YouTube Adding a YouTube video as a free episode. Optional Full instructions for each are in Integrations.

UploadFrom the Admin Panel or Creator Portal Processffmpeg or Cloudflare makes 1080p–360p ReviewOnly for creators’ work ScheduleA publish time per episode ReleasedFollowers get a drop alert Upload. Your team uploads episode files on Admin Panel›Content›Upload & pipeline; a creator uploads on their series in the Creator Portal. Uploads go straight from the browser and carry on after a dropped connection. Process. The server (or Cloudflare Stream) turns each file into adaptive streams at 1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p, never above the original's quality, plus a poster image. Review. A creator's series and episodes wait in the Review queue until a person approves them. Your own team's titles are approved in the title editor. Schedule. Each episode gets a publish time. A background task checks every minute and releases episodes whose time has come. Release. The episode appears in the app. Viewers who follow the series get one "new episodes" alert per series per day.
documents.s: From upload to a viewer's phone

documents.t: Buy a coin packIn Google Play or the App Store Server checks receiptCoins land only after it passes Unlock an episodeAt the price shown first Ledger rowEvery coin in and out is recorded Creator shareSaved with each unlock A viewer buys coins in the store. Your server checks the receipt with Google or Apple before a single coin lands. When the viewer unlocks an episode, the price they were shown is the price they pay, and the coins leave their wallet as a new line in an append-only ledger (a history nobody can edit or delete). If the series belongs to a creator, the creator's share is saved with that unlock, so a later change to their share never rewrites the past. Read more in Monetization.

Some jobs can't happen while someone waits for a page: processing video, sending pushes, releasing episodes on time, counting the Dashboard's numbers. eDrama does them in the background with two things your server must keep running: The scheduler, started by one cron line (a server feature that runs a command on a timetable, here every minute). Queue workers, which take jobs from a waiting list one by one. On shared hosting the scheduler can run them for you. If either stops, videos stop processing and episodes stop releasing. Cron & queues shows how to set them up and how to check them on Admin Panel›System›System.

Use this page as your map. Each line links to the page with the full instructions. Tick them off in order: later steps depend on earlier ones. Your ticks are saved in this browser, so you can come back to it as you work.

eDrama has four kinds of people, and each one signs in a different way and sees a different part of the system. Person Signs in with Uses Owner (the Super Admin) Email and password, optional two-factor Everything, including the team and its roles. There is exactly one Owner. Team member Email and password, optional two-factor The Admin Panel, limited by their role. Creator Google, email or phone, through Firebase The Creator Portal, and only their own series. Viewer Google, Apple, phone, email, or as a guest The mobile app.

The Owner is created during installation (by the web installer, or with the php artisan edrama:create-owner command). Nobody can delete, disable or change the Owner or the Owner's role, not even another member with full access. Only the Owner can: create, edit and delete roles, require two-factor sign-in for the whole team, activate the license and install updates, change AI Studio's keys and billing, clear the demo data.

The Admin Panel is divided into 18 permission areas. For each area a role gets None (the screen is hidden), View (they can look) or Edit (they can change things; Edit includes View). The server checks the permission on every screen, button and action, so hiding a menu item is never the only protection. Permission area Covers Titles & episodes The Titles list and title editor Categories Categories (the genres on titles and in onboarding) Uploads Upload & pipeline Schedule & Home Release schedule and Home builder Website The public website editor Review queue Approving creators' work and viewer problem reports Comments & reviews Moderating what viewers post Creators Inviting and managing creators Users Viewers and their accounts Support tickets Help requests from the app Balance adjustments Adding or removing coins Refunds Refunding store purchases Transactions Purchases, exports, creator reports and Creator revenue Prices & coin packs Monetization: regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ads, rewards Push Sending push notifications Settings Settings and System Team & roles Members, invites and roles Audit log The history of every change

Four roles are created at installation. The Owner can edit them or create new ones. Role What it can do Refund limit Admin Edit everywhere except Team & roles (None); the audit log is view only. 100.00 in the reporting currency Content Manager Titles, uploads and the release schedule; can look at the review queue. No refunds Moderator The review queue and creators. No refunds Finance & Support Users, balance adjustments and refunds; can look at transactions and prices. 20.00 in the reporting currency The refund limit is the largest single refund a member with that role may make. A role without one can't refund. The Owner can refund any amount. See Team & roles. Least access Give each person the smallest role their job needs. Every role change, sign-in and decision is recorded in the Audit log.

Five wrong passwords for one email from one address lock that sign-in for 15 minutes. A session ends 12 hours after sign-in, and at the next click when a member is disabled. Passwords need at least 12 characters and must not appear in a known data breach. A member added with a temporary password must choose their own before anything else.

A creator is Invited until they accept their invite, then Active. A Suspended creator can't sign in to the portal or send new work, but their live series stay live unless a reviewer unpublishes them. See Becoming a creator.

A viewer who opens the app for the first time becomes a guest automatically, with a welcome bonus. Signing in turns the guest into an account and carries over their coins and unlocks. Buying coins or VIP requires a signed-in account. A banned viewer is refused on their next request. See Accounts.

Each answer has its own link: hover a question and choose Share to copy it.

What are the default login details?Share There are none. You choose the Owner email and password in the installer's last step. If you lost them, run php artisan edrama:create-owner on the server only if no Owner exists; otherwise use Forgot password? on the sign-in page (email must be set up). Do I need Composer, Node.js or a build step on the server?Share No. The package includes vendor/ and the built public/build. Upload, point the domain at public, and run the web installer. Can I install eDrama on shared hosting?Share Yes, if you can choose PHP 8.5 and allow proc_open. Video processing needs ffmpeg in your home folder, or use Cloudflare Stream so your server does no video work. One cron line runs both the schedule and the queues. See Shared hosting. Episodes don't release at their time, and pushes don't go out. Why?Share The scheduler isn't running. Add the cron line from Admin Panel›System›System›Server setup and wait until it shows Cron running. See Cron & queues. Can I jump straight to the newest version?Share No. Updates go one version at a time: install 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, then 1.1.0 → 1.2.0. Back up first. See License & updates. Can I move to a new domain?Share The purchase code is registered to one domain. After moving, the panels ask for the code again at /activate. If it's refused as registered elsewhere, contact WRTeam support with your purchase code to release it. Step by step: Move to another domain. Your viewers' app keeps working meanwhile: the license never locks the API. /install shows "404".Share The installer closes itself once the install finishes: sign in at /admin instead. It also answers 404 while EDRAMA_INSTALLER isn't true in .env. To install again on an empty database, contact support. The installer marks something "Missing".Share Your server lacks a PHP extension, runs PHP below 8.5, or a folder isn't writable. Fix the items marked Missing (or ask your host), then choose Check again. See Server installation. An episode stays "Processing".Share With this server or Amazon S3: ffmpeg isn't found, or the host stops long jobs. Check the ffmpeg line on Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video, and that the cron line runs (Video processing). With Cloudflare Stream: the webhook isn't registered. Run php artisan edrama:video-webhook (Cloudflare Stream). Videos stuck in processing are also re-checked every 10 minutes. Emails don't arrive.Share Until you add an SMTP server in Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP), emails are only written to the server's log and nobody receives them. Emails also go out through the queue, so the cron line must be running (Email).

Why won't an episode publish? It says it's under the floor.Share Paid episodes must be at least 45 seconds long. Upload a longer cut, or open the title's Episodes tab and use Allow short episode with a reason. Creators can't submit episodes under the floor. I changed Home but the app still shows the old one.Share Changes in the Home builder reach the app only after Publish layout. Viewers see it the next time they open Home. A live title doesn't appear for some viewers.Share Check its Where it's shown (title editor › Monetization): it may be limited to some regions. Also check it has a price in the default region, and that the viewer's audience matches the Home section it's in.

A viewer paid but says the coins didn't arrive.Share Search their order ID on Admin Panel›Money›Transactions and open the purchase: the four verification steps show where it stopped. Purchases waiting on the store finish by themselves; the viewer can also choose Restore purchases in the app. If needed, use a balance adjustment with a reason. Why can't I refund an App Store purchase from the panel?Share Apple decides App Store refunds. Send the viewer to Apple's refund request page (linked in the purchase drawer); Apple's notification updates the purchase when it's done. I raised a series' price but some viewers still pay the old one.Share That's the price lock: viewers who already started the series keep their price. A rise doesn't reach them; a drop does. See Coins & pricing. The Dashboard says some revenue is left out.Share A currency has no exchange rate into your reporting currency for some days. Add the rate in Admin Panel›Settings›Regions & languages. Can I offer a free trial for VIP?Share No. It's a locked fair-play rule: VIP never starts with a free trial that turns into a charge. The server refuses a subscription that started with one. Viewers watch ads but nothing unlocks.Share Server-side verification isn't set up. In AdMob, set the callback URL shown in Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Ads on every rewarded ad unit. See AdMob. A viewer moved country and sees the wrong prices.Share If they've never paid, the app moves them to the right region by itself at its next start. If they have paid, open their page in Admin Panel›Audience›Users and use Change region, with a reason (Regions). Can I show a series in some countries only, or charge different prices per country?Share Yes, both. On the series' Monetization tab, set Where it's shown to Only these regions. For different prices, create a region for those countries in Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Regions, with its own currency, coin value, packs, VIP plans and title prices (Regions & currencies). How are creators paid?Share eDrama works out each creator's share every month and writes a statement. Your team pays them outside eDrama (bank transfer, UPI, PayPal, Wise or other) and records the payment with Record payout on the creator's page, so nobody is paid twice. Creators see their statements and payouts on Earnings in the Creator Portal (Creator earnings).

A creator didn't get their invite email.Share Email delivery may not be set up: add your SMTP server in Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP), send a test, then use Resend invite on the creator. Invites expire after 7 days. A creator can't sign in to the Creator Portal.Share Check that the Firebase Web API key and Auth domain are in Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications, and that your domain is in Firebase's Authorized domains. Creators sign in with Google, email or phone; Sign in with Apple isn't available in the portal, and a guest account can't become a creator. Creators can't create a series.Share The Creator terms must be published in Admin Panel›Settings›Legal pages, and each creator must accept the version in force.

I changed the app name in Settings, but the name under the icon didn't change.Share The name under the icon is part of the app build: change it in AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist and publish a new version. See Name & package name. Shared links open in the browser, not the app.Share The share domain must match in app_config.dart, build.gradle.kts and Runner.entitlements, and your server must publish the link files (EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE, EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256, EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID). See Deep links. "Continue with Apple" fails.Share Enable the Apple provider in Firebase Authentication with your Apple Developer account, and check Sign in with Apple is on in Xcode's capabilities. How do I add a language without releasing the app?Share Add it in Admin Panel›Settings›Regions & languages, upload its translated JSON file for the mobile app, and turn on Offered in the app. The app downloads it at its next start. See Languages. The app can't reach my server.Share Check apiBaseUrl in lib/app/config/app_config.dart: it must be your server, use https:// and end in /api/v1/. If you turned on EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=enforce, go back to monitor until your store build passes App Check (Connect to your server). The app shows "maintenance" or asks to update.Share Maintenance mode is on, or the app's version is below Minimum supported. Both are in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support (App & support). What login do I give Google Play and App Store reviewers?Share Create an email-and-password account for them on the server with php artisan edrama:review-account review@your-domain.com, and put it in each store's review notes (Server commands). Didn't find your answer? Check Troubleshooting for step-by-step fixes, or contact WRTeam support with your purchase code. Contact support →
