Find the symptom, check the likely cause, apply the fix. Most problems show up first on Admin Panel›System›System: start there.

Symptom Likely cause Fix The installer shows Folder permissions The web server can't write storage, bootstrap/cache or .env. Folders 755/775, files 644/664, owned by the site's user. Upload the hidden .env if missing. Connected, but the tables could not be created The database user can't create tables. Give it All privileges on the database; press Continue again. A 500 error page after installing Wrong permissions, or a missing PHP extension. Check storage/logs/laravel.log; the System page names permission problems. /.env opens in the browser The domain points at the project folder. Point it at public, or upload the package's .htaccess. Then change the DB password and APP_KEY. This server isn't set up as a live server APP_ENV/APP_DEBUG are development values. APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, then php artisan config:cache. Everyone shares one IP (lockouts hit everybody) A proxy/CDN isn't trusted. EDRAMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES=cloudflare (or *), then config:cache. Both panels redirect to /activate The purchase code was refused (invalid or another domain). Owner enters the code again; contact WRTeam if it's refused.

Symptom Likely cause Fix Cron not running on System No cron line, or the wrong PHP/folder. Copy the line from System › Server setup; wait 2 minutes. Tasks marked late The cron stopped. Same as above; check the hosting panel didn't disable it. Jobs pile up under Jobs waiting No queue worker. Shared hosting: keep EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=true. VPS: start supervisor. Failed jobs A job hit an error (shown in its first line). Fix the cause, then Retry. Changes to .env have no effect Config is cached; workers run old code. php artisan config:cache and php artisan queue:restart.

Symptom Likely cause Fix ffmpeg not found Not installed, or not on the path. Install it, or set EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH/EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH. Stuck on Processing No queue worker. See Background work. Processing, then Failed The host killed the long job (memory/CPU limits). Use Cloudflare Stream or a bigger server. Upload stops at a percentage Connection dropped. Choose Retry: it resumes. Upload refused immediately Over the size limit, or not MP4/MOV/MKV. Check Admin Panel›Settings›Video pipeline. Episodes upload but nginx returns 413 Request body limit. client_max_body_size ≥ 16M (8 MB chunks). Video won't play in the app Not processed, not released, or the viewer hasn't unlocked it. Play it from the title's Episodes tab; check its status and release.

Symptom Likely cause Fix Purchases fail verification Store keys missing or wrong, or the product IDs don't match. Check the Google Play / App Store cards and press Test connection. Check the IDs in Monetization match the store products. (The App Store card's Environment doesn't affect purchases: they're checked with production, then the sandbox.) Refunds made in the store don't show Notifications not set up. Set up Google's Pub/Sub push and Apple's Server Notifications. Ads play but don't reward No server-side verification. Set the callback URL on each AdMob unit. No ads at all on one platform No ad unit for that platform in the region. Fill in the unit IDs in Monetization › Ads. Revenue left out of totals Missing exchange rate. Add it in Settings › Regions & languages. Creator revenue ads pools are zero AdMob Reporting API not connected. Connect AdMob in Settings › Creator revenue, or set pools by hand.

Symptom Likely cause Fix Pushes aren't set up yet No Firebase keys. Settings › Notifications › Firebase. Test push: No app account … has a device that takes pushes Your app account doesn't use the same email, or notifications are off. Sign in to the app with your Studio email; allow notifications. iOS gets no pushes No APNs key in Firebase. Upload the APNs key in Firebase › Cloud Messaging. Pushes arrive late Quiet hours or the daily cap. Expected; adjust in Settings › Notifications. No emails at all Mailer writes to the log. Add an SMTP server; Send test email. Emails in spam Missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC. Add them for your sending domain.

Symptom Likely cause Fix No internet connection on every screen Wrong apiBaseUrl, or http://. https://…/api/v1/ with the trailing slash. Signed out right after signing in Server clock drift, or a different Firebase project. Sync the server clock; use one Firebase project for app and server. Google sign-in fails on Android Missing SHA-1/SHA-256 in Firebase. Add debug and release fingerprints, re-download google-services.json. Update required for everyone Minimum version set too high. Lower it in Settings › App & support › App versions. Maintenance screen won't go away Maintenance mode is on. Turn it off in Settings › App & support. Release build won't sign No android/key.properties. Create the keystore and the file (Release build). Still stuck? Send us the symptom, a screenshot, the last lines of storage/logs/laravel.log and your purchase code. Contact support →
The installer gives you a working Admin Panel. These steps make it ready for real viewers. Do them in this order.
Open https://your-domain.com/admin (the domain's root address also takes you there) and sign in with the Owner email and password you chose in the installer.

Open Admin Panel›System›System. Look for: Cron running in green. If not, add the cron line. No red warning cards. The page warns you if: the .env file can be opened from the web, the server isn't set up as a live server (APP_ENV or APP_DEBUG), visitors reach the app through a proxy it doesn't trust. Each warning names the exact line to change.
Open your name at the foot of the sidebar › Your account and set up two-factor authentication. See Sign-in & your account.
Without email, team invites, password resets and creator emails can't be sent. Open Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP), enter your provider's details and choose Send test email. See Email.
Viewer sign-in, the Creator Portal's sign-in and push notifications all need Firebase. Open Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications, fill in the Firebase card and choose Test connection. See Firebase.

Admin Panel›Settings›Branding: app name, logos, theme colour. Admin Panel›Settings›App & support: support email, store links. Admin Panel›Settings›Legal pages: terms, privacy policy, refund policy and Creator Terms.
Open Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video. The This server option should show ffmpeg in green, or set up another option. Upload one short test episode and watch it reach Ready.

If you imported demo data, look around first, then remove it before launch with Admin Panel›System›Clear demo data. See Clear demo data. Continue with the Launch checklist for money, content and the app.

You'll rarely need these, but they're good to know. Run them in the project folder. Every command, including the store reviewer account and Cloudflare Stream's webhook, is on Server commands. Command What it does php artisan edrama:create-owner Creates the Owner if the installer didn't (reads EDRAMA_OWNER_* from .env when run without a terminal). php artisan edrama:demo-data Imports the demo data. php artisan config:cache Applies changes to .env. php artisan queue:restart Makes the workers reload after a change or update. php artisan optimize Speeds up the app after an update. php artisan edrama:repair-encryption Clears saved secrets that can no longer be read because APP_KEY was lost, so you can enter them again.

Most of eDrama is run from the Admin Panel. A few jobs are done from the server's command line, over SSH or in your host's Terminal (cPanel › Terminal). Run every command from the project folder, the one that holds the artisan file: Server cd /var/www/edrama php artisan list edrama Which php? If php -v doesn't print 8.5, use the full path of PHP 8.5 instead of php, for example /usr/local/bin/php or the path your host gives. Admin Panel›System›System shows the PHP binary your server uses.

Command What it does php artisan edrama:create-owner Creates the Owner once, if the installer didn't. It asks for the name, email and password (twice), and refuses when an Owner already exists. For a deploy script, it reads EDRAMA_OWNER_NAME, EDRAMA_OWNER_EMAIL and EDRAMA_OWNER_PASSWORD from .env instead: remove the password from .env once the Owner exists. php artisan edrama:demo-data Imports the demo data (dramas, creators, viewers and their activity). Adds nothing if it's already there. On a live server it asks to confirm first; --force skips the question. php artisan edrama:review-account <email> Creates, or resets, an app account that signs in with email and password, for store reviewers and testers. More below. php artisan edrama:video-webhook Registers Cloudflare Stream's webhook to https://<your domain>/api/v1/webhooks/video and saves its signing secret in Settings. Pass another address as an argument if your panel lives elsewhere. See Cloudflare Stream. php artisan edrama:video-status <episode-id> --refresh Shows one episode's video status and a signed playback link. --refresh asks the video service for the latest status first. php artisan edrama:move-stream-videos Moves every episode video off Cloudflare Stream to your own storage (the same as the button on Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video). php artisan edrama:creator-report --month=2026-10 Builds the monthly creator report again for a month (last month when --month is left out) and sends its link to Finance. php artisan edrama:creator-revenue --month=2026-10 Imports AdMob earnings and calculates creator revenue for review, for a month (last month by default). The same as Import from AdMob and Calculate on Creator revenue. php artisan edrama:ai-recover Re-queues, ends or fetches AI Studio calls that a stopped worker left behind. It also runs by itself every 5 minutes. php artisan edrama:wallet-reconcile Checks that every wallet's balance equals its coin history and bonus lots. It only reports: it never changes a balance. Runs by itself daily. php artisan queue:restart Makes running queue workers finish their current job and load new code. Run it after every update and after editing .env. php artisan config:cache Reloads .env after you edit it. (php artisan config:clear also works; it reads .env on every request until you cache again.) php artisan storage:link Re-creates the public storage link, if images stop showing after a move. The installer runs it for you.

Google Play and App Review sign in to your app to check it. Give them an account that needs no inbox or phone: Server php artisan edrama:review-account review@your-domain.com --name="App Review" It asks for a password (at least 8 characters) and never prints it. The account is created in your Firebase project with its email already verified, so it signs in straight away with Continue with Email. Running it again for the same email sets a new password and turns the account back on. Email/Password must be turned on in the Firebase console (Authentication › Sign-in method). Put the email and password in Play Console (App content › App access) and in App Store Connect (App Review Information › Sign-in required).

The cron line starts these on their schedule (Cron & queues). You don't need to run them, but you can, to see their output: edrama:publish-episodes, edrama:send-scheduled-pushes, edrama:expire-bonuses, edrama:release-held-pushes, edrama:ai-recover, edrama:vip-renewal-reminders, edrama:rank-top-titles, edrama:roll-up-title-stats, edrama:roll-up-daily-metrics, edrama:roll-up-creator-stats, edrama:wallet-reconcile, edrama:store-voided-purchases, edrama:prune-exports, edrama:prune-job-runs, edrama:prune-video-uploads, edrama:prune-cache, edrama:prune-webhook-events, edrama:prune-failed-jobs, edrama:prune-ai-files, edrama:creator-revenue, edrama:creator-report and edrama:work-queues.

These exist for WRTeam's development, testing and demo server. They refuse to run in production, or would damage live data: Command Why not edrama:seed-demo Drops every table and rebuilds the database. Local and staging only. edrama:demo-data --fresh Drops every table before importing. Never in production. edrama:load-test-seed Creates load-test viewers with coins. Staging and local only. edrama:ad-verify Fakes an AdMob confirmation, for local testing. edrama:video-upload Uploads a local file to the video service, for manual checks. edrama:repair-encryption --force Empties saved secrets the current APP_KEY can't read, after a lost key. Without --force it only counts them. Keep a copy of APP_KEY with your backups so you never need it. Not comfortable with the command line? Our team can run these for you, or install and configure the whole server. Contact support →

eDrama does a lot of work in the background: releasing episodes at their time, processing videos, sending pushes and emails, counting the Dashboard's numbers and checking store refunds. Two things make that happen: The scheduler decides when each task runs. It is started by one cron line that runs every minute. Queue workers do the jobs that wait in line, such as processing a video or sending 10,000 pushes. Without these, eDrama stops moving If the cron line is missing, episodes never release, scheduled pushes never go out and videos never finish processing. Set this up straight after the installer.

Every server needs exactly one cron entry. The easiest way to get it right is to copy it from the panel: your-domain.com/admin/system 1234567 1Cron statusTurns into “Cron running” once the scheduler has run in the last few minutes. 2Setup stepsShow or hide the steps. 3Where you set it upThree tabs: SSH / crontab, Hosting panel (command), Hosting panel (PHP script). 4Crontab entryWith your server’s own PHP path and project folder. 5CopyCopies the line. 6PHP binary and folderUsed in the line. 7Queue workersWhen supervisor runs the workers, keep this command running. System’s Server setup card with the SSH / crontab steps and the crontab entry. Sign in and open Admin Panel›System›System. In Server setup, choose Setup steps, then the tab that matches your server. Copy the line and add it: SSH: run crontab -e as the user that owns the site (on a VPS, crontab -u www-data -e), paste the line on a new line, save. Hosting panel: open Cron Jobs, choose "every minute" and paste the command. Wait a minute or two and refresh System. Cron running turns green. The line looks like this (your folder and PHP path will differ): crontab * * * * * cd /var/www/edrama && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1 The five stars mean "every minute"; they are part of the line.

Shared hosting (no supervisor) VPS with supervisor (recommended) Nothing else to do. With EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=true in .env (the default), the same cron line also works through the queues every minute, in two pools. Each pool takes its queues in priority order and stops when they're empty or after 55 seconds, so the next minute's run can start. No long-running process is needed, which is why this works on shared hosting. Pool Queues, in priority order Longest one job may run urgent webhooks (store and video notifications), notifications (pushes), default (emails and the rest) 60 seconds slow video, reports 600 seconds Two pools, so a ten-minute export never holds up a store notification. The time limit needs the pcntl PHP extension. On a VPS, long-running workers react instantly instead of once a minute. eDrama ships a ready-made supervisor file at docs/deploy/supervisor.conf. Server cp /var/www/edrama/docs/deploy/supervisor.conf /etc/supervisor/conf.d/edrama.conf sed -i 's#%(ENV_APP_DIR)s#/var/www/edrama#g' /etc/supervisor/conf.d/edrama.conf supervisorctl reread && supervisorctl update && supervisorctl start edrama:* The file runs every program as user=www-data. If another user owns your project files, change each user= line before you start it. Check the workers with supervisorctl status. It starts four programs: two urgent workers (store and video notifications, then pushes), one default worker (emails and everything else), one slow worker (video processing and large exports) and the scheduler. Because supervisor now runs the scheduler and the workers, turn off the cron's own workers so they aren't doubled. In .env: .env EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=false Then run php artisan config:cache. With supervisor running the scheduler (schedule:work), you don't need the cron line: run exactly one of the two. To keep the cron line instead, remove the [program:edrama-scheduler] block and its name from the programs= line. After every update Run php artisan queue:restart so workers finish their current job and reload the new code.

All times are UTC. Task When What it does Publish episodes Every minute Releases episodes whose publish time has passed. Send scheduled pushes Every minute Sends pushes scheduled in the Push composer. Expire bonuses Every 5 minutes Removes bonus coins past their expiry date. Release held pushes Every 5 minutes Sends pushes held back by quiet hours or the daily limit. AI recovery Every 5 minutes Picks up AI Studio calls that were interrupted. Poll stuck videos Every 10 minutes Checks uploads that seem stuck and restarts stalled processing. VIP renewal reminders Every 15 minutes Reminds subscribers about 24 hours before each charge. Rank top titles Every 15 minutes Builds "Top 10 today" per region. Roll up stats Every 15 minutes Title stats, Dashboard figures and creators' 28-day stats. Wallet reconcile Daily 02:30 Checks every wallet's balance against its ledger. Reports, never changes. Voided purchases Daily 03:30 Reads Google Play's list of refunded and charged-back purchases. Clean-up tasks Daily 04:00–05:10 Expired exports, old run records, unfinished uploads, cache, webhook events, failed jobs, unused AI files. Creator revenue Daily 05:00 UTC Prepares the month's creator revenue on the import day you set. Creator report 1st of the month, 02:00 UTC The monthly creator report. Every task's last run and result is on Admin Panel›System›System, with any failed jobs, which you can Retry, Retry all or Delete there. A failure alerts the team by email, Slack and the bell (see System alerts).

The .env file in the project folder holds the settings that change only when you deploy: the database connection, the app's address, and a few switches. Almost everything else (branding, keys for Firebase or the stores, prices, features) is set in the Admin Panel instead, so you rarely need to touch this file. warning .env contains your database password and APP_KEY, the key that signs every session and encrypts stored secrets. Never share it, never let it be reachable from the web, and keep a copy of APP_KEY with your backups: if it is lost, saved keys in Settings can't be read back. After editing .env, apply the change: Server php artisan config:cache php artisan queue:restart Some settings are already in .env with a # in front: remove the # to use one. A setting that isn't in the file at all can be added on its own line, as NAME=value.

Setting Meaning APP_URL Your site's address, such as https://admin.your-domain.com. APP_ENV production on a live server. The System page warns you if it isn't. APP_DEBUG false on a live server, so error pages never show internals. DB_* The database connection. EDRAMA_INSTALLER false once installed. The installer only opens while this is true and no install marker exists. EDRAMA_LICENSE_ENFORCED true once installed: the purchase code is checked (see License & updates). SESSION_DRIVER, CACHE_STORE, QUEUE_CONNECTION All database: sessions, cache and the job queue live in MySQL, so no Redis is needed. APP_KEY Generated once. It signs sessions and encrypts the keys you save in Settings. If you move to another domain, change APP_URL too: the purchase code is registered to its domain (License & updates).

Setting Default When to change it EDRAMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES empty Behind Cloudflare's proxy set cloudflare; behind your host's CDN or a load balancer set * (only when the app can't be reached around it), or list addresses. The System page tells you when it's needed. EDRAMA_TRUST_APP_COUNTRY true Set false behind a CDN that always sends the country header, so a viewer's region can only come from the CDN. EDRAMA_COUNTRY_HEADER CF-IPCountry The header holding the viewer's country. EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED true Set false when supervisor runs the queue workers (Cron & queues). EDRAMA_CREATOR_PANEL_URL empty Only if the Creator Portal is on a different domain. EDRAMA_SUPPORT_EMAIL support@example.com The support address used until Admin Panel›Settings›App & support has one. Set one of the two, or the app's Help screen and creator emails show the example address. EDRAMA_DEFAULT_REGION GLOBAL The region code used when no region is marked default. EDRAMA_BONUS_EXPIRY_DAYS 7 A fallback for bonus-coin expiry. The real setting is per region: Monetization › Rewards › Bonus coins expire after. MAIL_* MAIL_MAILER=log The server's own email settings, used until Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP) is saved. With log, emails are only written to the log: nobody receives them. EDRAMA_CORS_ORIGINS empty Extra browser addresses allowed to call the API. EDRAMA_APP_CHECK off Firebase App Check on the viewer API: off, monitor (log only) or enforce. See Firebase. EDRAMA_APP_CHECK_APP_IDS empty Limit App Check to these Firebase app IDs. EDRAMA_FIREBASE_CLOCK_LEEWAY 60 Seconds of clock difference allowed when checking Firebase tokens. Keep the server's clock synced too. EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE empty Your Android app ID, so share links open the app (Deep links). EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 empty Your app's signing fingerprints (comma-separated), for the same. EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID empty TEAMID.bundle.id, for iOS share links. EDRAMA_PLAYBACK_URL_TTL_SECONDS 600 How long a signed playback link works. EDRAMA_UPDATE_MAX_MB 300 The largest update package accepted. EDRAMA_AI_CLIP_MAX_MB, EDRAMA_AI_CLIP_MAX_SECONDS, EDRAMA_AI_CLIPS_PER_SERIES 300, 1800, 200 Limits for videos imported into AI Studio. EDRAMA_SUPPORT_REPLY_HOURS 24 The reply time the app's Help screen promises. EDRAMA_SLOW_QUERY_MS 500 Log database queries slower than this. EDRAMA_API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE 300 The overall request limit per viewer per minute. EDRAMA_ALERT_EMAILS, EDRAMA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL empty Fallbacks for system alerts when Settings has none. FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS empty Path to a Firebase service-account file, when Settings has none. EDRAMA_OWNER_NAME, EDRAMA_OWNER_EMAIL, EDRAMA_OWNER_PASSWORD empty Read by php artisan edrama:create-owner in a deploy script (Server commands). Remove the password once the Owner exists. EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH, EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH empty See Video processing. Advanced: video encoding, rate limits and housekeeping You rarely need these. Change one only when a page or WRTeam support tells you to. Setting Default What it does EDRAMA_VIDEO_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS 900 The longest episode accepted, in seconds (15 minutes). EDRAMA_TRANSCODE_TIMEOUT 540 How long one ffmpeg run may take, in seconds. Raising it also needs the slow workers' --timeout and DB_QUEUE_RETRY_AFTER raised. EDRAMA_TRANSCODE_PRESET veryfast The x264 preset: faster presets use less CPU, slower ones make smaller files. EDRAMA_TRANSCODE_THREADS 2 Encoder threads per ffmpeg run. 0 lets ffmpeg decide; keep it low on shared hosting ("Error while opening encoder"). EDRAMA_UPLOAD_CHUNK_MB 8 The size of the pieces browsers upload videos in. Must stay below your web server's body limit. EDRAMA_KEEP_VIDEO_SOURCE true Keeps the uploaded original, for re-encoding and storage moves. EDRAMA_SUBTITLE_DISK files The storage subtitle files live on. EDRAMA_API_ANONYMOUS_IP_PER_MINUTE 1200 Requests per minute from one IP address before sign-in (many phones can share one carrier address). EDRAMA_API_SESSION_IP_PER_MINUTE 300 Requests per minute per IP address for signed-in sessions. EDRAMA_MEDIA_PER_MINUTE 3000 Requests per minute per IP address to signed media links (video playlists and segments). EDRAMA_TABLE_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS 50000 The most rows one table download holds. Filter for more. EDRAMA_IMPORT_MAX_ROWS 1000 The most rows one bulk-import file holds. EDRAMA_FAILED_JOB_DAYS 30 Failed jobs older than this are deleted daily. EDRAMA_WEBHOOK_EVENT_DAYS 90 Processed store and video notifications older than this are deleted daily (at least 7). EDRAMA_AD_LIMIT_MODE per_ad_unit The starting value for whether unlock ads and Rewards ads share one daily limit (shared). Change it per region in Monetization › Ads instead. EDRAMA_IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_HOURS, EDRAMA_IDEMPOTENCY_LOCK_SECONDS 24, 60 How long a purchase or unlock request is remembered, so a retried request never charges twice.

Setting Why EDRAMA_DEMO_MODE, EDRAMA_DEMO_* Only for WRTeam's public demo server: makes both panels read-only. Keep them off. EDRAMA_FAKE_FIREBASE_TOKENS Developer testing only. Never true in production. APP_KEY Changing it makes saved secrets unreadable. If you must replace it, put the old key in APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS. APP_DEBUG true shows error details, including secrets, to everyone. Keep it false. EDRAMA_LICENSE_VALIDATOR_URL, EDRAMA_LICENSE_ITEM_ID Where and how your purchase code is checked. Changing them stops the license check working. EDRAMA_APP_LANGUAGES, EDRAMA_VIDEO_PROVIDER Starting values the installer uses. Change languages and the video provider in Settings instead.
eDrama is licensed per domain. Your CodeCanyon purchase code is registered to the domain you install on, and both panels check it in the background.

The check runs when the panels are used, at most once every 7 days, with WRTeam's license server. Only a clear answer locks the panels: "invalid code" or "domain mismatch". If the license server can't be reached, nothing is locked; the app tries again 10 minutes later. When locked, every page of the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal sends people to /activate, where the Owner enters the purchase code again. The viewer app is never locked by the license. Your viewers, the creator application form, share pages and legal pages keep working. A local development address (such as localhost) is never checked. The Owner is alerted by email, Slack and the bell if a weekly check refuses the code.

Sign in as the Owner and open Admin Panel›System›License & updates (or follow the link to /activate when locked). Enter the purchase code. Leave the update package empty. Choose Check code and activate. Members whose role can open Settings can see this page; only the Owner can activate the license or install updates.

One purchase code is registered to one domain: the domain of APP_URL in .env, without www.. To move eDrama to a new domain: Ask WRTeam to free the code. Write to support with your purchase code, the old domain and the new one. The panel has no button for this: the license server releases it. Move the backend. Copy the project folder and the database to the new server, or point the new domain at the same folder (VPS, shared hosting). Change the address. In .env, set APP_URL to the new address, such as https://admin.new-domain.com, then run php artisan config:cache. Activate it there. Open the Admin Panel on the new domain. It shows Activate your purchase: enter the same purchase code and choose Activate. Update everything that names the old domain: the app's apiBaseUrl and shareBaseUrl (Connect to your server), the stores' notification URLs, AdMob's verification callback, the website's EDRAMA_API_URL, and Firebase's authorised domains (callback addresses). While the panels wait for activation, the app, the website and the API keep working.

Updates come from CodeCanyon as a zip named like update-1.0.0-to-1.1.0.zip, holding version_info.json and source_code.zip: upload the zip as it is, without unzipping it. The license server must be reachable, because the purchase code is checked before the package is opened. Each one moves you exactly one version forward: to go from 1.0.0 to 1.2.0, install the 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 update first, then 1.1.0 → 1.2.0. your-domain.com/admin/license 123456 1LicenseStatus, purchase code, domain, buyer and last check. 2VersionThe installed version and update history. 3Activate or updateOne form for both: the purchase code, and optionally an update package. 4Purchase codeChecked first, every time you submit. 5Update package (.zip)Optional. When added, you confirm you backed up the database and files. 6SubmitCheck code and activate, or Check code and install update. License & updates: the license and version cards and the activation form. Back up first. Download a copy of your database and the project folder (most hosting panels have a one-click backup). Pick a quiet time. The update doesn't switch the app into maintenance mode, so run it when few people are using it. Open Admin Panel›System›License & updates as the Owner. Enter your purchase code and choose the update zip. Tick I backed up the database and files. Choose Check code and install update. What happens next, in order: Step What it means Purchase code checked With the license server, for this domain. A refused code stops here. Package checked Its version must follow yours exactly, and every file inside is inspected for safety. Update installed Every file about to be replaced is first backed up to storage/app/private/updates/, then the new files are written and the database changes run. When it's done, the page shows the new Installed version and adds a line to Update history. Then restart the workers so they load the new code: Server php artisan queue:restart Why an update can be refused It's for a different version than the one installed (updates go one at a time). It's larger than the upload limit (300 MB by default, and also your PHP upload_max_filesize and post_max_size). It tries to write outside the allowed folders. Your .env and storage folder are never touched by an update.

The app's source code is updated separately: copy your changes (server address, name, package name, Firebase files, logos and colours) into the new version of the app project, then build and publish it. Keeping your changes to the files listed in Mobile app setup makes this quick.

The server software (the Admin Panel, the Creator Portal and the API) is installed once, on a server you control. The package already contains everything it needs to run: you do not need to install Composer or Node.js on the server, and you never run a build step.

A serverA VPS (recommended) or shared hosting with PHP 8.5, MySQL 8 and the ability to run ffmpeg.→A domain with HTTPSSuch as admin.your-domain.com, pointed at the server, with an SSL certificate.→Your purchase codeFrom your CodeCanyon downloads page. It is registered to your domain.→An empty MySQL databaseA database name, a user that can create and change tables, and its password.→

The web installer checks all of these and marks anything missing in red. Requirement Details PHP 8.5.0 or newer PHP extensions bcmath, ctype, curl, fileinfo, gd, intl, json, mbstring, openssl, pdo_mysql, sodium, tokenizer, xml, zip PHP function proc_open must be allowed (not in disable_functions): the cron line starts each task through it, and ffmpeg runs through it Recommended The pcntl extension, so a background job that hangs is stopped at its time limit Database MySQL 8 (an empty database) Writable by the web server storage, storage/app, storage/framework/cache, storage/framework/sessions, storage/framework/views, storage/logs, bootstrap/cache, and the .env file Video processing ffmpeg and ffprobe, unless you use Cloudflare Stream (details) Background work One cron entry every minute; supervisor is recommended on a VPS (details) Web server Apache or nginx, with the domain pointing at the package's public folder Upload size At least 16 MB for upload_max_filesize and post_max_size (videos upload in 8 MB pieces), and the same for the web server's body limit (nginx client_max_body_size is only 1 MB by default). Higher if you'll install update packages or import AI Studio clips from the browser (up to 300 MB). Outgoing HTTPS The server must reach WRTeam's license server (to check your purchase code), Firebase, the stores and your video service. HTTPS An SSL certificate on your domain: the app and the website only talk to https:// servers. Which server? A small VPS (2 CPU cores, 4 GB of memory) handles a launch comfortably. Video processing is the heaviest job: every upload is turned into four qualities on your server. If your hosting is small, choose Cloudflare Stream in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video and your server does no video work at all.

Every uploaded episode is turned into adaptive streaming video in four qualities (1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p). You choose who does that in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video, and can switch later. Option You need Good for This server (the default) ffmpeg on the server Getting started and small catalogues Amazon S3 (or S3-compatible) ffmpeg on the server, plus a bucket Growing catalogues: storage grows without filling your disk Cloudflare Stream A Cloudflare account with Stream. No ffmpeg. No video work on your server. Cloudflare bills for minutes stored and watched. The largest episode file is 20 GB by default (up to 200 GB, set in Admin Panel›Settings›Video pipeline), and the longest episode is 15 minutes.
documents.s: Video: choose who does the work

documents.t: Address What runs there admin.your-domain.com This package: the Admin Panel (/admin), the Creator Portal (/creator), the API (/api/v1), share pages (/s/…, /c/…) and legal pages (/legal/…) your-domain.com or www.your-domain.com The public website, hosted separately

Prepare the server. Install PHP, MySQL and ffmpeg, upload the package and point your domain at its public folder. Follow VPS server or Shared hosting. Run the web installer. Open your domain in a browser and complete four screens: requirements, purchase code, database and Owner account. See Web installer. Start the background work. Add the cron line, and on a VPS the queue workers. See Cron & queues. Check video processing. Make sure ffmpeg is found, or choose Cloudflare Stream. See Video processing. Finish the setup. Sign in, connect email and Firebase, set your branding and remove the demo data. See After installation.

Your CodeCanyon download holds one zip per part, each named with its version: Zip What it is Guide edrama-backend-<version>.zip The server: Admin Panel, Creator Portal, API and installer This section edrama-app-<version>.zip The Flutter app for Android and iOS Mobile app setup edrama-website-<version>.zip The public website (Next.js) Website Inside the backend zip: Folder or file What it is app, bootstrap, config, database, lang, resources, routes The application. vendor Every PHP library it uses, already included. public The only folder the internet should see. Your domain points here. public/build The panels' styles and scripts, already built. storage Logs, sessions, uploads (when files stay on this server). .env The settings file. The installer fills it in. Some computers hide files whose names start with a dot: make sure it is uploaded. .htaccess Used only when your domain can't point at public (see Shared hosting). docs/deploy/ A ready-made supervisor.conf (Cron & queues) and ffmpeg-shared-hosting.md (Video processing). artisan The command-line tool for the server commands. Want WRTeam to install it? Our team can prepare the server, run the installer and set up cron, queues and ffmpeg for you. Contact support →

Shared hosting (cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin, aaPanel and similar) works for eDrama, with two things to check first: that you can choose PHP 8.5, and that the host lets you run ffmpeg (or you use Cloudflare Stream for video instead). There's no supervisor on shared hosting, and you don't need it: one cron line runs both the schedule and the queues.

In cPanel, open MultiPHP Manager (or Select PHP Version), choose PHP 8.5 for your domain, and make sure these extensions are ticked: bcmath, ctype, curl, fileinfo, gd, intl, json, mbstring, openssl, pdo_mysql, sodium, tokenizer, xml, zip. Then, in Select PHP Version › Options (or MultiPHP INI Editor): remove proc_open from disable_functions (ffmpeg can't run without it), set upload_max_filesize and post_max_size to at least 16M (more to install updates from the browser: up to 320M).

Open MySQL Databases: create a database, create a user, and add the user to the database with All privileges. Write down the full names (cPanel adds your account name as a prefix, such as myacct_edrama) and the password.

Open File Manager, upload the eDrama server zip and Extract it. Most hosts ask you to put a site in public_html. You have two options: Best: point the domain at public If you can't change the document root Extract the package into its own folder, such as /home/myacct/edrama. Then, in Domains (or Addon Domains / Subdomains), set the domain's Document Root to /home/myacct/edrama/public. Nothing outside public can then be reached from the web. Extract everything into the folder your domain already uses (such as public_html), including the hidden .htaccess file at the top of the package. That file serves the app from public and keeps everything else (the .env file, logs and code) out of reach. File Manager hides files that start with a dot: turn on Settings › Show Hidden Files to check that .htaccess and .env are there. Check that .env is hidden Open https://your-domain.com/.env in your browser. You must see an error page, not a list of settings. If you see the settings, anyone can read your database password: fix the document root or upload the .htaccess file. The installer and the System page both run this check and warn you.

Shared hosts can't install system programs, but most let you run a ready-made ffmpeg from your home folder. Follow Video processing › Shared hosting. If your host refuses, choose Cloudflare Stream later in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video.
Open your domain in the browser and follow Web installer.

In cPanel, open Cron Jobs, choose Once Per Minute (* * * * *) and add the command shown on Admin Panel›System›System under Server setup after you sign in. It looks like this: Cron command /usr/local/bin/php /home/myacct/edrama/artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1 The System page shows your server's exact PHP path and folder, with a copy button. See Cron & queues.

Every episode you upload is turned into adaptive streams: copies at 1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p (never above the original's quality), plus a poster image, cut into small pieces so the app can switch quality as the connection changes. By default your own server does this with ffmpeg, a free video program. You have two choices: Choice Your server needs Cost This server (default) ffmpeg installed and allowed to run Nothing extra Cloudflare Stream Nothing for video Cloudflare bills for minutes stored and watched You switch between them in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video. Videos already uploaded keep playing from wherever they are.

One command: Server sudo apt install -y ffmpeg ffmpeg -version | head -1 Then open Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video and refresh: the This server card shows a green line such as ffmpeg 7.x on this server.

You can't install programs on shared hosting, but most hosts let you run a ready-made ffmpeg from your home folder. Run each block in cPanel › Terminal (or over SSH). Check the server allows it. php -v php -r 'var_dump(function_exists("proc_open"));' uname -m You need PHP 8.5, bool(true), and usually x86_64. If proc_open is false, remove it from disable_functions in Select PHP Version › Options (or ask your host). If uname -m prints aarch64, use arm64 instead of amd64 below. Download ffmpeg into your home folder. cd ~ && mkdir -p ffmpeg && cd ffmpeg wget https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/releases/ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz tar -xf ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz --strip-components=1 chmod +x ffmpeg ffprobe rm ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz No wget? Use curl -LO with the same address instead. Check that it runs. ~/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -version ~/ffmpeg/ffprobe -version Check your hosting is strong enough for video. This makes a 2-second 1080p test clip and deletes it: ~/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=1080x1920:rate=25 -t 2 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast ~/ffmpeg/test.mp4 && echo "ENCODE OK" rm -f ~/ffmpeg/test.mp4 ENCODE OK means you're fine. "Killed" or "Cannot allocate memory" means the hosting is too small: use Cloudflare Stream or a VPS. Tell eDrama where ffmpeg is. Go to your project folder (the one with the artisan file), then: grep -q '^EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH=' .env || echo "EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH=$HOME/ffmpeg/ffmpeg" >> .env grep -q '^EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH=' .env || echo "EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH=$HOME/ffmpeg/ffprobe" >> .env php artisan config:clear && php artisan optimize Check from the panel. Open Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video and refresh. The ffmpeg line should be green. If the terminal works but the page stays red, the website's PHP still blocks proc_open: fix it for the website's PHP version and wait a minute (the check is remembered for 60 seconds). Test a real upload. Upload one short episode on Admin Panel›Content›Upload & pipeline. It should go Uploading → Processing → Ready within a few minutes.

These lines in .env change how videos are processed. The defaults suit most servers. Setting Default Meaning EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH, EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH found automatically Where ffmpeg and ffprobe are, if not on the normal path. EDRAMA_VIDEO_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS 900 The longest episode accepted, in seconds (15 minutes). EDRAMA_TRANSCODE_TIMEOUT 540 How long one video may take to process, in seconds. EDRAMA_TRANSCODE_PRESET veryfast Slower presets make smaller files but take longer. EDRAMA_TRANSCODE_THREADS 2 in the example file CPU threads per video; keep it low on shared hosting. 0 lets ffmpeg decide. EDRAMA_UPLOAD_CHUNK_MB 8 The size of each upload piece. EDRAMA_KEEP_VIDEO_SOURCE true Keep the original upload after processing. AI Studio's episode editor needs it to merge new clips with an episode. Run php artisan config:cache after changing .env.

What you see Fix Upload stays Processing forever The background worker isn't running: check the cron line. Upload goes Processing, then Failed The host stopped the long job. Use Cloudflare Stream, or a VPS. "ffmpeg not found" on the Storage & video page Check EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH, then php artisan config:clear. "Permission denied" running ffmpeg The host blocks programs in your folder. Ask support, or use Cloudflare Stream. The easiest way out of any of these is Cloudflare Stream. See Storage & streaming.

A VPS (virtual private server) is a server where you have full control, usually reached over SSH (a secure command line). This page prepares a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 server. If your provider gives you a control panel such as cPanel instead, follow Shared hosting. note The commands below are a standard, tested way to prepare Ubuntu for a PHP application. Package names and versions can differ between providers and over time; if a command fails, the error message usually names the package to install instead. The parts specific to eDrama are marked eDrama.
Connect from your computer's terminal (replace the address with your server's): Your computer ssh root@203.0.113.10 Then bring the server up to date: Server apt update && apt upgrade -y

Server apt install -y software-properties-common add-apt-repository -y ppa:ondrej/php apt update apt install -y php8.5-fpm php8.5-cli php8.5-mysql php8.5-bcmath php8.5-curl php8.5-gd \ php8.5-intl php8.5-mbstring php8.5-xml php8.5-zip php8.5-sodium unzip php -v php -v should print a version starting with 8.5. Raise the upload limits (eDrama: videos upload in 8 MB pieces; update packages can be up to 300 MB): Server sed -i 's/^upload_max_filesize.*/upload_max_filesize = 320M/; s/^post_max_size.*/post_max_size = 320M/' /etc/php/8.5/fpm/php.ini systemctl restart php8.5-fpm

Server apt install -y mysql-server mysql_secure_installation Create an empty database and a user for eDrama. Choose your own strong password: Server mysql -u root -p MySQL CREATE DATABASE edrama CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci; CREATE USER 'edrama'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'choose-a-strong-password'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON edrama.* TO 'edrama'@'localhost'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES; EXIT; Write down the database name, user and password: the installer asks for them.
documents.s: 3. Install MySQL 8 and create the database

documents.t: Server apt install -y ffmpeg nginx supervisor ffmpeg -version | head -1 ffmpeg turns each uploaded episode into streams (eDrama). Supervisor keeps the queue workers running (Cron & queues).

Upload the eDrama server zip to /var/www/ (with an SFTP program such as FileZilla, or scp), then: Server cd /var/www unzip edrama-server.zip -d edrama chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/edrama find /var/www/edrama -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \; find /var/www/edrama -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \; chmod -R 775 /var/www/edrama/storage /var/www/edrama/bootstrap/cache Use the zip's real name. Check that the hidden .env file arrived: ls -la /var/www/edrama/.env.

Create the site file: Server nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/edrama Paste this, replacing admin.your-domain.com: /etc/nginx/sites-available/edrama server { listen 80; server_name admin.your-domain.com; # eDrama: the domain points at public/, never at the project folder. root /var/www/edrama/public; index index.php; # eDrama: videos upload in 8 MB pieces; update packages up to 300 MB. client_max_body_size 320M; location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string; } location ~ \.php$ { include snippets/fastcgi-php.conf; fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.5-fpm.sock; fastcgi_read_timeout 300; } location ~ /\.(?!well-known) { deny all; } } Turn it on and reload: Server ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/edrama /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx

At your domain provider, add an A record for admin.your-domain.com with your server's IP address. Once it resolves (usually minutes), add a free Let's Encrypt certificate: Server apt install -y certbot python3-certbot-nginx certbot --nginx -d admin.your-domain.com
documents.s: 7. Point your domain and add HTTPS

documents.t: Open https://admin.your-domain.com in your browser. The installer starts by itself: continue with Web installer. Behind Cloudflare or a load balancer? If visitors reach your server through Cloudflare's proxy or another CDN, tell eDrama to trust it, or every visitor will look like the same person (rate limits and sign-in lockouts would count them as one). Add EDRAMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES=cloudflare to .env. The System page warns you when this is needed. See Environment file.

The installer runs in your browser the first time you open your domain. It takes about five minutes and has four steps. When it finishes, it closes itself for good: /install then answers "not found". your-domain.com/install 12345678 1StepsRequirements, Purchase code, Database, Owner account. The current step is highlighted. 2Step headingStep 1 of 4, and what this step checks. 3SummaryOr how many items to fix, with Check again once they are fixed. 4PHPThe version eDrama needs, and the one this server runs. 5PHP extensionsEach extension eDrama needs, ticked when the server has it. 6Writable folders and filesThe web server must be able to write these. Folders 755 (or 775), files 644 (or 664). 7Hidden filesChecks that .env can’t be opened from the web. If it can, point the domain at the public folder. 8ContinueShows once every check passes. Otherwise fix the items marked Missing and choose Check again. The installer’s first step, Server requirements, on a server where every check is Ready, with Continue at the bottom.

The installer checks: PHP 8.5 or newer, and each required extension. Writable folders and files: storage and its subfolders, bootstrap/cache and .env. Hidden files: that https://your-domain.com/.env can't be opened from the web. Fix anything marked Missing, then choose Check again. If the installer can't even write its own files, it shows a Folder permissions page listing what to fix: give folders 755 (or 775) and files 644 (or 664), owned by the account the site runs as.

Enter the purchase code from your CodeCanyon downloads page. It is checked with WRTeam's license server and registered to this domain. Where is my purchase code? A code for another product, or one already used on another domain, is refused and the install stops here. If the license server can't be reached, the install continues and the code is checked again later.

Field What to enter Site address Your full address, such as https://admin.your-domain.com. Host Usually 127.0.0.1 or localhost. Port Usually 3306. Database name The empty database you created. Username / Password The database user. Continue tests the connection, creates all the tables (this can take a minute) and saves the settings to .env. warning The database user must be allowed to create and change tables. If you see "Connected, but the tables could not be created", give the user All privileges on that database and press Continue again.

The Owner is the Super Admin: the one account that can do everything, including managing the team. Field Notes Name Shown to your team across the panel. Work email You sign in with this. Password At least 8 characters. Use the eye to show what you typed. Later password changes inside the Admin Panel need 12 characters and a password that hasn't appeared in known data leaks, so you may as well choose one like that now. Password again The same password. Import demo data Optional. Adds sample dramas, creators, viewers and figures, with artwork drawn for you, so you can look around. You remove it all later with Clear demo data. Press Install. The installer: Creates the remaining tables and fills in the starting data: the Global (USD) and India (INR) regions, their coin packs and VIP plans, ad and reward settings, the starting categories, English and Hindi app languages, the four role templates and the first Home and website layouts. Creates your Owner account and records the license. Links the public storage folder. Switches the server to live settings: APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, sessions, cache and the queue in the database, the installer off and the license check on. From now on /install answers 404. Imports the demo data, if you ticked it.

You see Your studio is ready. Choose Go to sign-in and sign in with the Owner email and password you just chose. There are no default credentials. If the demo data couldn't be imported, the install itself still finished; the reason is in storage/logs, and you can import it later with: Server php artisan edrama:demo-data

Message What to do The .env file could not be written PHP must be able to write .env (and ideally the project folder, so it can save it safely). Fix the permissions as on Step 1, then try again. Could not connect to the database Check the host (often localhost on shared hosting), the port (3306), the database name, the user and the password, and that the user has all privileges on that database. The install could not finish The message says why. Fix it and press Install again: what was already set up is kept. The purchase code is refused Check you copied the whole code. If it's registered to another domain, ask support to free it (Move to another domain). The license server could not be reached Your server can't make outgoing HTTPS calls, or the license server is busy. Try again in a few minutes, or ask your host to allow outgoing connections. The demo data could not be imported The install itself finished. The reason is in storage/logs; import it later with php artisan edrama:demo-data. /install answers 404 The install already finished (sign in at /admin), or EDRAMA_INSTALLER isn't true in .env. To install again on an empty database, contact support. Next: Cron & queues.

eDrama uses AdMob rewarded ads in two places: to unlock an episode, and to earn bonus coins on the Rewards tab. AdMob is set up in three places: Where What The app project The AdMob app IDs (Ads setup). Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Ads The ad unit IDs per platform and region, and the limits. Admin Panel›Settings›Creator revenue The AdMob Reporting API, so unlock-ad earnings can be shared with creators.
In AdMob, for each app (Android and iOS), create two Rewarded ad units: one for unlocks, one for Rewards. Each ID looks like ca-app-pub-0000000000000000/0000000000.

For every ad unit: AdMob › Ad units › the unit › Server-side verification › enter the callback URL shown on the Ads tab in Monetization. Required An ad unlocks an episode or pays coins only once AdMob confirms it through this callback. Without server-side verification, ads play but reward nothing.

In Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Ads, for each region: Unlock ad unit ID (Android / iOS) and Rewards ad unit ID (Android / iOS), plus the daily limits and coins per Rewards ad. A platform without a unit shows no ads in that region.

So the monthly import can read your unlock ads' earnings by country and ad unit (read-only): In Google Cloud, enable the AdMob API. Set up APIs & Services › OAuth consent screen and publish it (in testing mode, Google ends the connection after 7 days). Credentials › Create credentials › OAuth client ID › Web application. Add the Authorised redirect URI shown on the AdMob Reporting API card. Paste the OAuth client ID and client secret on the card and Save. Choose Connect AdMob and sign in with the Google account that owns the AdMob account. The refresh token and publisher ID (pub-…) are filled in. Without it, creator revenue's ads pools stay at zero unless set by hand.
documents.s: 4. Connect the Reporting API (for creator revenue)

documents.t: One ad, one reward; 30 seconds at most; no playable or interactive ads in the unlock path; never shown to VIP; never auto-played. Use AdMob's Blocking controls to keep interactive formats out of your rewarded units.
Your server checks every iOS purchase with Apple and receives App Store Server Notifications (version 2) for renewals, refunds and cancellations.

App Store Connect › Users and Access › Integrations › In-App Purchase: generate a key. Copy its Key ID and download the .p8 file (Apple lets you download it once). Issuer ID: shown at the top of Users and Access › Integrations › App Store Connect API.

Admin Panel›Settings›Payments › App Store card: Field Value Bundle ID Your iOS app's ID, such as com.yourcompany.drama. Issuer ID From step 1. Key ID The 10-character ID. Private key (.p8) Open the file in a text editor and paste all of it, from the first line of dashes to the last. Environment Only decides where Test connection asks Apple for a test notification: Production (default) or Sandbox. Save, then Test connection: it asks Apple to send a test notification to the URL below. TestFlight and App Review purchases just work Every purchase is checked with the live App Store first, then the sandbox, whatever Environment says. So TestFlight, Sandbox testers and App Review can buy without you switching anything. Leave Environment on Production.

Copy the Server notifications URL (version 2) from the card and paste it in App Store Connect › your app › App Information › App Store Server Notifications, choosing Version 2, for both production and sandbox: https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/app-storeCopy Notifications are signed by Apple and checked before anything is stored.
Create the coin packs (consumable) and the three VIP subscriptions in one group, matching the IDs in Monetization. See In-app purchases.

Apple decides App Store refunds. In Transactions, the purchase drawer links to Apple's refund request page for the viewer, and Apple's notification updates the purchase when a refund (or a refund reversal) happens.

eDrama sends team invites, password resets, every creator email (invites, review decisions, suspensions…) and system alerts. Connect your provider in Admin Panel›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP) (full page). Provider Host Port / encryption Username Gmail / Google Workspace smtp.gmail.com 587 STARTTLS Your address; password = an app password Amazon SES email-smtp.<region>.amazonaws.com 587 STARTTLS SES SMTP credentials SendGrid smtp.sendgrid.net 587 STARTTLS apikey (password = your API key) Any other Your provider's SMTP host 587 STARTTLS or 465 SSL/TLS Your SMTP login The From address must be one your provider lets you send from (a verified sender or domain). Save, then Send test email. Land in the inbox, not spam Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for your sending domain, as your provider describes. It's the single biggest factor in deliverability.

When a background job or scheduled task fails, eDrama alerts the team within minutes. In Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications›System alerts: Field Value Alert emails One or more addresses, separated by commas. Members with Settings (Edit) also get a bell. Slack webhook URL Optional. api.slack.com/apps › Create New App › Incoming Webhooks › Add New Webhook to Workspace › pick the channel › copy the URL. Test connection sends a test alert. Alerts are throttled to one per job per 15 minutes, and the license check also alerts here if your purchase code is refused.

Firebase is Google's app platform. The app uses it to sign viewers in and receive pushes; your server uses the same project to check every viewer's sign-in token, send pushes, and sign creators in to the portal. App side: Mobile app setup › Firebase. This page covers the server side.

Open the Firebase console › your project › Project settings › General. Copy the Project ID. Under Your apps, open (or add) the Web app. Its config holds the Web API key (apiKey) and Auth domain (authDomain). Project settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key. A JSON file downloads. In the Admin Panel: Admin Panel›Settings›Notifications › Firebase card. Fill in Project ID, paste the whole Service account JSON, and the Web API key and Auth domain. Save, then Test connection.

Creators sign in from the browser at your domain, so it must be allowed: Authentication › Settings › Authorized domains › add your Admin Panel's domain. Otherwise creators see This site isn't allowed to sign in with Firebase yet. Enable the sign-in providers creators use (Google, Email/Password, Phone) under Authentication › Sign-in method; viewers also need Anonymous (guests) and Apple.

App Check proves requests come from your genuine app on a real device. In .env: EDRAMA_APP_CHECK Behaviour off (default) Not checked. monitor Checked and logged, nothing refused. Start here. enforce Requests without a valid token are refused. Limit it to your apps with EDRAMA_APP_CHECK_APP_IDS (comma-separated Firebase app IDs). An outage on your side is never held against viewers.

Without the keys, inbox notifications are still saved but pushes are skipped, and Push shows Pushes aren't set up yet. If viewers get signed out right after signing in, your server's clock may be off: keep it synced, and the allowance EDRAMA_FIREBASE_CLOCK_LEEWAY (60 seconds) covers small drift. Saved keys are encrypted and never shown again.

AI Studio makes images and video with Google's Gemini models. It needs a Gemini API key from a Google project with billing on: create one at Google AI Studio. Key Where Used for The platform's key Admin Panel›Settings›AI Studio›Keys and billing (Owner only) The team's AI Studio, and creators in Admin managed or Hybrid mode. A creator's own key The creator's Your account › AI Studio Their calls in Creator managed or Hybrid mode, billed to them. Google checks a key before it's saved; only its last 4 characters are shown afterwards. Default models: gemini-nano-banana-2.1 (images), gemini-3-pro-image (higher quality), gemini-omni-1.2-flash (video). Google retires models often; change the IDs in Settings when it does. Google's own limits apply to each key: a Tier 1 project allows about 40 videos a day and 8 requests a minute, which is why eDrama runs 2 calls at once by default. Prompts and images used in AI Studio are sent to Google, under the account that pays. Every frame Google makes carries its SynthID watermark. See AI Studio settings.

With Allow YouTube videos as episodes on (Admin Panel›Settings›Video pipeline, on by default), your team and creators can add a public YouTube video (Shorts suit it best) as an episode. Only the video's ID is stored; the server checks the video may be embedded, with no API key. Before you use it: Terms: the app must follow the YouTube API Services Terms of Service and the YouTube Terms of Service. Privacy policy: your policy must say the app uses YouTube API Services and link to the Google Privacy Policy. No paywall: YouTube episodes are always free: never sold with coins, an ad unlock, VIP or a Series Pass, and they earn creators nothing. Don't change this. Player: YouTube's own player and its ads stay as they are. Its quality and subtitles are YouTube's; the app's quality menu and subtitle files don't apply. Rights: add only videos you own or may show. Use the Credit field for attribution, such as Title by Creator, CC BY. Uploading a file to the same episode later replaces the YouTube video once it's processed; an episode holding an uploaded video refuses a YouTube link.

Your server talks to Google Play to verify every coin-pack purchase and VIP subscription, to refund from the Admin Panel, and to hear about refunds, renewals and cancellations through real-time developer notifications.

In the Google Cloud console, in the project linked to your Play account, enable the Google Play Android Developer API. IAM & Admin › Service accounts › Create service account, then its Keys › Add key › JSON. A file downloads. In Play Console › Users and permissions › Invite new users: invite the service account's email (it ends in iam.gserviceaccount.com), with View financial data, orders and cancellation survey responses and Manage orders and subscriptions, for your app. note New Play Console access can take up to a day to start working. If Test connection fails straight after, try again later.

Admin Panel›Settings›Payments › Google Play card: Field Value Package name Your app's ID, such as com.yourcompany.drama. Service account JSON The whole file. Pub/Sub push service account The account the push subscription signs with (step 3 below). Required for real-time notifications: without it, every Google Play notification is refused. Save, then Test connection.

In Google Cloud Pub/Sub, create a topic. On the topic's Permissions, give google-play-developer-notifications@system.gserviceaccount.com the Pub/Sub Publisher role, so Google Play can post to it. Create a push subscription on the topic. Set the endpoint to the Real-time notifications push URL shown on the card: https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/google-playCopy Turn on authentication, pick a service account, and set the audience to the same URL. Enter that service account's email in Pub/Sub push service account on the Google Play card and Save. In Play Console › Monetize with Play › Monetization setup › Real-time developer notifications, enter the topic's full name (projects/<project>/topics/<topic>) and choose Send test notification. Google Play notifications are refused without it. Each notification is checked, stored once, and processed in the background (up to 5 tries). Google's voided purchases list is also checked daily, so refunds and chargebacks are never missed.

Create the coin packs (consumable) and the vip subscription with base plans weekly, monthly and yearly, matching the IDs in Monetization. See In-app purchases. warning A purchase must be for the product the app names; the server refuses mismatches. VIP base plans must not carry a free-trial offer.

eDrama connects to a handful of outside services. Each one's keys go in a card in Admin Panel›Settings with a Where do I find these? guide, Save and Test connection. Service Used for Needed? Keys go in Guide Firebase Viewer sign-in, push, App Check, Creator Portal sign-in Yes Settings › Notifications Firebase Google Play Coin packs and VIP on Android; refunds and renewals For Android Settings › Payments Google Play App Store Coin packs and VIP on iOS; refunds and renewals For iOS Settings › Payments App Store AdMob Rewarded ads; earnings for creator revenue If you use ads Monetization › Ads; Settings › Creator revenue AdMob Amazon S3 / S3-compatible Storing files and videos Optional Settings › Storage & video Storage & streaming Cloudflare R2 Storing files and videos, no download fees Optional Settings › Storage & video Storage & streaming Cloudflare Stream Processing and streaming videos Optional Settings › Storage & video Storage & streaming ffmpeg Processing videos on your server Unless you use Stream Server Video processing SMTP email Invites, resets, creator emails, alerts Strongly recommended Settings › Email delivery Email & alerts Slack System alerts Optional Settings › Notifications Email & alerts Google Gemini AI Studio Optional Settings › AI Studio; creators' accounts Gemini & YouTube YouTube Free episodes from YouTube Optional Settings › Video pipeline (switch) Gemini & YouTube WRTeam license server Purchase code checks Yes Installer; System › License & updates License & updates

Several services call your server back. Each card in Settings shows its exact address with a Copy button. They're all listed here too: type your Admin Panel's domain once and every address fills in. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it, ready to copy. It never leaves this browser. Service Address Google Play real-time notifications The Pub/Sub push subscription's endpoint and its audience (Google Play) https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/google-playCopy App Store Server Notifications App Store Connect › your app › App Information, Version 2, for production and sandbox (App Store) https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/app-storeCopy AdMob server-side verification AdMob › each rewarded ad unit › Server-side verification (AdMob) https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/admob-ssvCopy Cloudflare Stream webhook Registered for you by php artisan edrama:video-webhook (Cloudflare Stream) https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/videoCopy AdMob OAuth redirect Google Cloud › your OAuth client › Authorised redirect URIs, for Connect AdMob (AdMob) https://admin.your-domain.com/admin/admob/callbackCopy Android app links Nothing to paste: open it to check it lists your app (Deep links) https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.jsonCopy iOS universal links Nothing to paste: open it to check it lists your app https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-associationCopy tip If you move to another domain, every one of these changes with it. Update each service, or notifications stop reaching your server.

By default, every file and video stays on your own server, processed with ffmpeg. As you grow, you can move files to a bucket (cloud storage) and/or let Cloudflare Stream process and stream videos. Switching is done in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video (how switching works).

AWS console › S3 › Create bucket. Pick the region nearest your viewers (ap-south-1 for India) and keep Block all public access on. IAM › Users › Create user (such as edrama-storage), without console access. Give the user a policy that allows listing, reading, writing and deleting in this bucket only. Open the user › Security credentials › Create access key › Application running outside AWS. Copy the access key ID and secret access key (shown once). On the Amazon S3 bucket card: the keys, the bucket's name and region. Save, then Test connection. Optional Public URL (such as a CloudFront domain) serves posters and banners publicly; without it they're served through secure links that last six days. Inside the bucket, public media goes under media/ and private files and videos under files/: a bucket policy that makes only media/* public is enough for a Public URL. Using the website? Add the bucket's host (or its Public URL's host) to the website's EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS, or posters won't show there (Connect the website).

DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, MinIO and others work through the same card (choose the Service): Endpoint: the provider's S3 address, such as https://sgp1.digitaloceanspaces.com, https://s3.ap-southeast-1.wasabisys.com or https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com. Region: the bucket's region there (sgp1, ap-southeast-1, us-west-004), or us-east-1 / auto when any works.

R2 has no download fees, which suits video streaming at scale. Cloudflare dashboard › R2 Object Storage › Create bucket (location Automatic, unless you need EU or FedRAMP). Copy your account ID from the R2 overview's Account details. Manage API tokens › Create API token, with Object Read & Write for this bucket only. Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key (shown once). Optional: connect a custom domain to the bucket for posters and banners, and put it in Public URL. On the Cloudflare R2 bucket card: account ID, jurisdiction, keys and bucket name. Save, then Test connection. Then pick Cloudflare R2 under Storage (files).

Cloudflare uploads, transcodes and streams the videos; your server does no video work, so ffmpeg isn't needed. Turn on Stream. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Stream and subscribe. Account ID: Cloudflare dashboard › Stream, or the address bar after dash.cloudflare.com/. API token: My Profile › API Tokens › Create Token › Custom token, with Account › Stream › Edit. Copy it (shown once). Signing key: signed playback stops anyone playing your videos outside the app. Create one with the API (below). The answer's id is the signing key ID and its pem the signing key (paste it as Cloudflare returns it). Customer subdomain: Stream › any video › its link starts with customer-….cloudflarestream.com. Fill in the Cloudflare Stream card and Save. Leave Webhook secret empty: the next step fills it in. Register the webhook, so Cloudflare can tell your server when a video is ready (below). Press Test connection. It fails until every key, the webhook secret included, is saved, and it checks the signing key belongs to your account. Then choose Cloudflare Stream under Video streaming. Create a signing key (step 4) curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/ACCOUNT_ID/stream/keys" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN"

With one command (recommended) With Cloudflare's API From the project folder on your server: Server php artisan edrama:video-webhook It registers this address with Cloudflare and saves the Webhook secret Cloudflare returns, straight into Settings: https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/videoCopy If your Admin Panel answers on a different address, pass it as an argument: php artisan edrama:video-webhook https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/video. Register the webhook curl -X PUT "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/ACCOUNT_ID/stream/webhook" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{"notificationUrl": "WEBHOOK_URL_FROM_THE_CARD"}' The answer's secret is the Webhook secret: paste it on the card and Save. Cloudflare's own guides: Stream webhooks and signed links. Stream's notifications are signed and checked (at most 5 minutes old) before they're stored. Missed ones are caught by a check every 10 minutes. To check one episode's video from the server: Server php artisan edrama:video-status <episode-id> --refresh

eDrama is a complete short-drama streaming business: a mobile app where viewers watch vertical episodes of 60 to 90 seconds, a back office where your team runs the catalogue and the money, and a portal where invited creators publish their own series. The first few episodes of every series are free. After that, viewers unlock an episode with coins, by watching one short ad, with a Series Pass, or with a VIP subscription. Fair, visible pricing is the product's promise, and it is built into the code so nobody can switch it off by accident. This documentation covers all of it, from installing the server to publishing the app in the stores, and every screen your team, your creators and your viewers will use.

Viewer appThe Android and iOS app your audience downloads. Built with Flutter.→Admin Panel (the “Studio”)Your team’s back office at /admin: titles, uploads, creators, users, money and settings.→Creator PortalA second panel at /creator where invited creators upload and manage only their own series.→Public website & APIShare pages, legal pages, the creator application form and the API the app talks to.→ The Admin Panel, the Creator Portal and the API all run on one server (a computer on the internet that you rent from a hosting company). The mobile app is a separate project that you build on your own computer and publish to Google Play and the App Store.

You are… Start with The owner of the platform, setting it up for the first time Launch checklist The person installing it on a server Server installation The person building the app for the stores Mobile app setup A team member running content, support or finance Admin Panel A creator publishing series Creator Portal Anyone who wants to know what viewers see Viewer App No technical background is needed for the Admin Panel, Creator Portal and Viewer App guides. The installation and app setup guides involve a server and a few commands; each command is given in full, with a copy button.

Follow the menu paths. A chip like Admin Panel›Settings›Branding tells you exactly where to click: open the panel shown in colour, then each part in turn. Creator Portal paths are gold, such as Creator Portal›My series›New series, and the app's are blue, such as App›Me›Settings. Use the numbered screens. Most pages show the screen they describe with numbered markers. Each number is explained right below it; point at a number (or tap it) to highlight its explanation. Watch for the coloured notes. A green Tip saves you time, a blue Note explains why something works the way it does, an amber Warning protects you from a mistake, and a red Danger is about something that can't be undone. Where a behaviour couldn't be confirmed These pages were written from eDrama's source code. Where the code leaves a question open, the page says so in a note titled To confirm instead of guessing.

This documentation describes Admin Panel & Creator Portal 1.0.0 Viewer app 1.0.0 (build 1) Server software Laravel 13 and Filament 5 on PHP 8.5, MySQL 8 App framework Flutter 3.47.7, Android 7+ and iOS 15+ Website Next.js 16 and React 19, on Node.js 20.9+
