WRTeam can install the Admin Panel on your server, connect Firebase, the stores and AdMob, and publish your branded app. Contact support →

Each series has a coin price per episode per region, set in the title editor. A region without its own price uses the default region's. Creators propose a price within the limits you set (30–90 coins by default), and a reviewer confirms it. What a particular viewer pays is decided on the server, never on the phone: Take the series' price in the viewer's region (or the default region's). Cap it by the viewer's price lock for that series, if they have one. Show it in coins and in the region's money in the unlock quote, and charge exactly that.

The first time a viewer unlocks an episode of a series with coins, the price they paid is locked for them: If you later raise the price, it doesn't reach them. If you lower it, the lower price applies to them too. The title editor's Change prices dialog tells you how many viewers have a lock on that series. This is one of the fair-play rules: a viewer halfway through a story is never squeezed.

Every series page shows What it costs before anything is paid: the free range (E1–E5), what it costs to catch up or finish, the Series Pass, and the rule 60 coins (≈ $0.59) an episode, never more. Or 1 ad ≤ 30 s per episode. You can preview it per region in the title editor's Monetization tab.

When a viewer unlocks with coins: Bonus coins first, earliest expiry first. Then paid coins. The unlock sheet says which: Uses 20 bonus first, then 40 paid. Bonus coins can't be used for tips or creator payouts; a creator's share comes from paid coins.

Every unlock and purchase is idempotent: if a viewer double-taps or the connection retries, they're charged once. Every coin in and out is a new row in the viewer's append-only ledger, which they can see in their wallet and your team sees on their user page.
One title: Change prices in the title editor (with a reason). Many titles: Import › Prices on the Titles list (Bulk imports). Creators are emailed when their series' prices change.
Creators earn a share (50% by default, set per creator) of what their series bring in. Three streams make up a creator's month.

Stream How the creator's part is worked out Coins Paid coins spent on their episodes and Series Passes (less refunds) × the region's paid coin value × (1 − store fee) × their share. The share saved with each unlock is used, so a later share change never rewrites the past. Worked example below. Ads The region's ads pool (unlock-ad earnings from AdMob × the ads pool percent) × their verified ad unlocks ÷ all verified ad unlocks in the region × their share. VIP The region's VIP pool (VIP charges less refunds and store fees × the VIP pool percent) × their VIP minutes on locked episodes ÷ all VIP minutes in the region × their share. Not counted: bonus coins, the creator's own viewing and unlocks, accounts under a day old (for ads), free and YouTube episodes, and granted episodes. Your own and licensed titles count in each region's totals, so their part of the pools stays with the platform. Licensed titles have their own licensor share.

Only paid coins earn money. Bonus coins (the welcome bonus, coin-pack bonuses, the spin, streak titles, Rewards ads) are given away, so they earn nobody anything. For each series, each region and each month: The coins part of a statement paid coins = paid coins spent on its episodes and Series Passes − paid coins taken back by refunds gross money = paid coins × paid coin value net money = gross money × (1 − store fee ÷ 100) creator money = net money × the creator's share ÷ 100 your money = net money − creator money Term What it means Coin value What one coin is worth in the region's currency (0.0099 USD in Global and 0.29 INR in India to start), set in Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Regions. Paid coin value What one paid coin really brought in that month in the region: the store money of completed purchases divided by every paid coin added (team adjustments included). It's never above the coin value, so discounted packs, test purchases or coins your team added never pay out more than you received. When every purchase paid full price, it equals the coin value. Store fee Google Play's and the App Store's cut (15% each to start, in Admin Panel›Settings›Payments). The fees saved on that month's purchases in the region are used, weighted by amount. Saved at the time Each unlock saves the share in force when it happened; each purchase saves its store fee. Changing a setting never rewrites past money. Refunds When a store refund or chargeback arrives after the coins were spent, what those coins earned is taken back in the month of the refund. Example. A creator series priced at 60 coins in the Global region. In one month, viewers unlock 1,000 episodes with paid coins, all from full-price packs: Paid coins 1,000 × 60 = 60,000 Gross money 60,000 × 0.0099 = 594.00 USD Store fees (15%) 89.10 USD Net money 504.90 USD Creator (50%) 252.45 USD You 252.45 USD

Move the sliders or type a number. It uses the same formula as the monthly statements, with eDrama's starting values filled in. Global · USDIndia · INRYour own Coin price per episodecoinsCreators choose 30 to 90 coins by default.Paid unlocks this monthEpisodes unlocked with paid coins. Bonus coins earn nothing.Series Pass paid coinscoinsOptional: paid coins spent on this series' Series Pass.Store fee%Google Play and App Store: 15% by default (Settings › Payments).Creator share%Default creator share is 50%. A licensed title uses its licensor share. Paid coins this month60,000 coins× 0.0099 USD per coin = 594.00 USD gross Store fees (15%)89.10 USD Net money504.90 USD Creator (50%)252.45 USD You keep252.45 USD Assumes full-price packs and no refunds. Ads and VIP are shared separately, from monthly pools. What the calculator leaves out Refunds, discounted packs (which lower the paid coin value), and the ads and VIP pools, which are shared separately (above). It also leaves out your own running costs: hosting, video storage and streaming, taxes and payout fees.

Month ends StatementCoins share, closed on the 1st Creator revenueAds & VIP, imported on the 5th Approve PayRecorded as a payout On the 1st, the month before is closed: each creator's statement gets their coin share (minus refunds). The monthly creator report is also built. On the import day (the 5th by default), Creator revenue imports AdMob's earnings and calculates the ads and VIP pools and each creator's part. Your team reviews, sets a pool by hand or adjusts a creator if needed, and approves. The ads, VIP and adjustments go onto the statements. Finance pays each creator outside the app and records the payout (amount, method, reference, date) on the creator's page. Creators follow the same figures on their Earnings page: earned, paid, waiting to be paid, and this month so far.

Transactions › Monthly creator report (also built automatically each month) gives one row per series and region: paid coins spent, Series Pass coins, ad unlocks and VIP minutes, with the settings used. Useful for licensors and auditing. To confirm Earlier project notes said the Creator Portal shows no money figures and payouts are manual. The current code adds the Earnings page and Creator revenue workflow described here; payouts are still made outside the app and recorded by hand.

Short-drama apps are often criticised for surprise charges, endless ads and prices that rise mid-story. eDrama's answer is a set of fair-play rules that are part of the product. They're shown, locked, on Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›Fair-play rules, so a pricing change can't quietly undo them. Rule What it means for viewers Price shown in coins and money, before every unlock The full cost, in their own currency, before they spend anything. Price lock per viewer Once they start a series, their per-episode price can't rise. Cost to finish on every series page What the rest of the story costs, before they start. Auto-unlock off by default, always capped The next episode is never charged without them choosing it. Daily spend cap (300 coins by default) Screen-time-style control over spending. Append-only ledger the viewer can see Every coin in and out stays on record; paid coins are always accounted for. Unlocks tied to the account, restorable anywhere What they unlocked survives a restart or a new phone. VIP: reminder before renewal, cancel in two taps, no ads A renewal never comes as a surprise. Bonus coins are spent first, earliest expiry first Paid coins never expire, so bonus coins go before they can. Never charged twice Every unlock and purchase is idempotent: a retry or a double tap can't take coins again. One ad, one reward A rewarded ad unlocks or rewards once, verified by the ad network. 45-second floor No paid episode is shorter than 45 seconds, so a coin always buys a real scene. (Your team can allow a single short episode, such as an epilogue, with a reason in the audit log.)

Ads are at most 30 seconds, never playable or interactive in the unlock path, and never auto-play an unlock. VIP never sees an ad. No free trial that turns into a charge; a reminder 24 hours before every renewal.

Not from the Admin Panel. Some have settings around them (the spend cap's choices, the floor's length, ad lengths up to 30 seconds), but the rule itself stays on. Changing one means changing the code, which WRTeam advises against: these rules are what make viewers trust the price. The daily spend limit is the one fair-play protection you can switch off entirely from the Features switches.
eDrama earns the way short-drama apps do, with one difference: fair, visible pricing is built in and locked, because viewers who trust the price keep coming back.

Source How it earns Configure it Coin packs Viewers buy coins in Google Play or the App Store. The server checks every receipt before coins land. Coin packs Coin unlocks Viewers spend coins to unlock an episode, at the series' price. Title editor › Prices Series Pass Viewers spend coins once to unlock every episode of a series, including future ones. Title editor › Prices VIP A weekly, monthly or yearly store subscription: every episode, no ads. Never a free trial. VIP plans Rewarded ads A viewer watches one ad (30 seconds at most) to unlock an episode or earn coins. AdMob pays you. Ads Free episodes The first episodes of every series. They earn nothing directly, but they're the hook. Title editor › Paywall

Money inA coin pack from the store CoinsPaid + bonus in the wallet Coins outUnlocks and Series Passes SharesCreators and licensors Paid coins come from purchases and never expire. Bonus coins come from pack bonuses, the welcome bonus, the daily spin, streak titles, ads and goodwill credits. They expire (7 days by default) and are always spent first, earliest expiry first. A coin's money value is set per region (for example $0.0099 in the Global region), so prices are fair in every currency. See Regions & currencies.

Each unlock and purchase records the share in force at that moment (creator or licensor share, store fee), so later changes never rewrite the past. Creators are paid monthly: their coin share, plus their part of the ad and VIP pools. See Creator earnings.
Coins & pricingPrice per episode, price lock, the cost card.→Unlock methodsCoins, ads, Series Pass, VIP, free and grants.→Fair-play rulesThe promises that can’t be switched off.→

Source How it arrives Admin Panel A member refunds a Google Play purchase from Transactions. Store notification Google or Apple tells your server about a refund or chargeback. Google Play voided purchases A daily check of Google's list of refunded and charged-back purchases, which always appear there. App Store refunds are always decided by Apple: the viewer requests them from Apple, and Apple's notification updates the purchase.

A refund can take the coins back (the default for store refunds; optional from the panel): Coins still in the wallet are taken back as a new reversal row in the ledger. Coins already spent can't be taken back: the balance never goes below zero. The part already spent is recorded on the refund as the shortfall. If the store later reverses a refund, the coins come back. From the panel, you can also refund the money and let the viewer keep the coins (for example, a goodwill refund).

Each role has a refund limit in the reporting currency (Admin 100.00, Finance & Support 20.00 by default; other roles none). Over the limit, someone with a higher limit must do it. The Owner can refund any amount. The panel asks Google first and writes nothing if Google refuses.

The Dashboard's revenue and Transactions' totals subtract refunds for the days they affect; the daily counts are redone for those days. A creator's statement subtracts refunds of coins that were spent on their series; if a refund takes back more than a later month earned, it comes off the next statements.

Without Google Play's real-time notifications and App Store Server Notifications, refunds made in the stores reach your server late (Google's daily check) or not at all (Apple). Set them up as described in Google Play and App Store. If a notification can't be processed after 5 tries, members with Transactions (Edit) get a bell, and the job can be retried from Admin Panel›System›System.
documents.s: Store notifications must be set up

documents.t: A price that's fair in the United States is too high in India. Regions let each market have its own currency, coin value, coin packs, VIP plans, title prices, ad limits and rewards, while one server runs them all. Region setting Example (India) Currency INR (₹ before the amount) Coin value 1 coin = ₹0.29 Time zone Asia/Kolkata Countries India Coin packs 300 + 300 for ₹99 … VIP Weekly ₹49, Monthly ₹149, Yearly ₹999 Ads 20 unlock ads a day The default region (Global, USD) serves every country no other active region lists.

The country the app store reports at sign-in. Otherwise the country your CDN reports (Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry header, from a proxy you trust). Otherwise the default region. Viewers can't pick their region. Your team can move one (Users › Change region). Purchases, unlocks and price locks always keep the region they were made in. Behind Cloudflare? Set EDRAMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES=cloudflare so the country header is believed. Without a trusted header, the app's reported country is used (EDRAMA_TRUST_APP_COUNTRY), which a determined viewer could change. Monetization › Regions says which source is in use.
documents.s: How a viewer's region is decided

documents.t: A new region starts as a copy of the default region's packs, plans, prices, ads and rewards, with money prices converted between the two coin values. Review, then turn it on (Regions).

The Dashboard, Transactions totals, refund limits and creator payouts use one reporting currency (USD by default). Each currency needs an exchange rate into it, dated from when it applies (Regions & languages). Rows on days without a rate are left out and named, never guessed. Amounts are stored in each currency's smallest unit (cents, paise), with each currency's own decimals (0 for JPY, 3 for KWD).
Free coins bring viewers back and let them sample paid episodes. They're all bonus coins: they expire (7 days by default) and are spent first, so they never pile up.

Source Default Set in Welcome bonus 100 coins for 7 days, once per device Monetization › Rewards Coin pack bonus +50 to +2,000 per pack Monetization › Coin packs Daily spin 10–200 coins, average about 20 (19.7) Monetization › Rewards Streak titles 0–500 coins, paid once per title Monetization › Rewards Ads for coins 15 coins per ad, up to 6 a day (20 in India) Monetization › Ads Goodwill credit Any amount, with a reason Users › Adjust balance

Every spin pays. The server picks the prize by weight (viewers can see the odds), so the outcome can't be tampered with. VIP members win their prize × the VIP multiplier (2 by default); title bonuses are never multiplied. The Rewards tab in the Admin Panel shows the average spin and about how many coins a daily viewer earns a month (and roughly how many episodes that is), so you can balance generosity against sales.

A streak counts days in a row with a spin. Shields (one every 7 days, up to 2 held) cover a missed day automatically. Titles are earned at a viewer's best streak and kept for good; each pays its bonus once.

Two kinds of rewarded ad, each with its own AdMob unit and daily limit (or one shared limit): Ad Reward Unlock ad One episode. Rewards ad Bonus coins (15 by default). Either pays only once AdMob's server-side verification confirms the ad was watched to the end, 30 seconds at most, never a playable or interactive ad, never shown to VIP. See AdMob.

A background task removes expired bonus coins every 5 minutes; the ledger shows a bonus expiry row. The wallet always tells viewers when their next bonus coins expire. Balancing tips If viewers rarely buy, the spin may be too generous: lower the big prizes' weights. A first top-up offer with double coins converts guests well: keep one per region. Keep the welcome bonus close to the price of one or two episodes so it's a real taste of the paywall.

An episode a viewer can watch was unlocked one of six ways. Each is recorded, so reports, the Dashboard's donut and creator earnings all add up. Method How Earns Counts toward Free Within the series' free episodes. Nothing directly. Views Coins The series' price, bonus coins first. The paid coins' value. Creator coin share Series Pass One coin price for every episode, including future ones. The paid coins' value. Creator coin share Ad One rewarded ad, up to 30 seconds, verified by AdMob. AdMob's payment to you. Creator ad pool, by verified ad unlocks VIP An active VIP subscription. The subscription. Creator VIP pool, by VIP minutes watched Grant Your team, from Users › Grant episode. Nothing; no coins move. No revenue share

Set per region in the title editor (optional). Unlocks every episode, including future drops. The unlock sheet shows the saving against paying per episode. It isn't held to the viewer's daily spend limit. Switch it off for everyone in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Features. To confirm The project notes record that the Series Pass ignoring the daily spend limit is a deliberate choice (a pass usually costs more than the highest limit) still awaiting the product owner's confirmation.

Only on series with Ads can unlock on (title editor › Paywall). One ad, one episode. The viewer always taps to watch; ads never auto-play an unlock. Unlocks only once AdMob's server-side verification confirms the ad was watched to the end. A failed or unconfirmed ad unlocks nothing, but still counts toward the day's limit. Never shown to VIP members. See Rewarded ads and AdMob.
Episodes added from YouTube can't be sold, gated or rewarded under YouTube's rules. They're always free, never part of VIP minutes or creator earnings.
Unlocks belong to the account, not the phone. A viewer who signs in on a new phone gets them all back.
VIP is an auto-renewing store subscription (Weekly, Monthly or Yearly) that unlocks every episode with no ads. Plans are set per region in VIP plans.
Every episode of every series with Included in VIP on (the default). No ads, anywhere. 1080p playback. The daily spin's prize multiplied (×2 by default). The perks text your team writes per plan.

Rule Why No free trial that turns into a charge The price must be above zero, and no store ID or perk may name a trial. The server refuses a subscription the store started with a free trial, and leaves a Google Play one unacknowledged so Google refunds it. Renewal reminder 24 hours before every charge A notification and an inbox message, always sent. Cancel in two taps The app opens the store's subscription page. VIP never sees an ad Not between episodes, not on the paywall, nowhere.

The viewer subscribes in the store from the app's VIP page. The app sends the receipt to your server, which verifies it with Google or Apple before turning VIP on. Afterwards, the stores' notifications keep it up to date: renewals, cancellations, grace periods, refunds. They arrive at the URLs on the store cards in Admin Panel›Settings›Payments.

Status Meaning Active Paid and current. Grace period A renewal payment failed; the store is retrying. On hold Payment failed; access paused until fixed. Canceled Won't renew; VIP lasts until the end of the paid period. Expired Ended. Revoked Refunded or taken back by the store. Each viewer's subscriptions are on their user page's VIP tab.

Every charge is recorded with the store's amount (or the plan's price), the store fee in force, and whether it was refunded. VIP revenue appears on the Dashboard, and the minutes VIP members watch creators' locked episodes decide each creator's part of the VIP pool (Creator earnings).

Every viewer starts as a guest: they can watch, follow, save series and earn bonus coins straight away, and they get the welcome bonus (100 bonus coins for 7 days by default, once per device). Their progress is saved on that phone. A guest must sign in to buy coins or VIP, so purchases are tied to an account and follow them to a new phone. 1234567 1Guest“Your progress is saved on this phone.” A signed-in viewer sees their name, photo and how they signed in. 2Sign inOpens the sign-in sheet. 3Reminder“Sign in to keep your coins and unlocks safe on any phone.” 4Coins · Day streak · TitlesEach opens its page. 5Your activityMy List, Wallet and Spend guard. 6MoreBecome a creator, Invite friends, Restore purchases, Help & refunds and Settings. 7SettingsAlso at the top, beside the notifications bell. The Me tab for a guest: Guest with Sign in, the reminder to sign in, coins, day streak and titles, Your activity, More, and Settings.

The app asks the viewer to sign in when it matters (before a purchase, for example), or they choose Sign in on the Me tab. 1234567 1Sign in to keep what you buy“So your coins and unlocks follow you to a new phone.” 2Continue with GoogleThe phone’s own provider comes first, marked Recommended: Google on Android, Apple on iPhone. 3Continue with AppleOne tap with the Apple account. Each provider can be turned off in the app’s config. 4Continue with EmailSign in or create an account with an email address. 5Continue with PhoneA 6-digit code by SMS. 6Carry-over note“Your guest history and welcome bonus move into the account.” 7Keep browsingCloses the sheet; they stay a guest. The sign-in sheet on Android: Sign in to keep what you buy, with Continue with Google (Recommended), Apple, Email and Phone, the carry-over note and Keep browsing. The phone's own provider is listed first and marked Recommended: Google on Android, Apple on iPhone. Email and Phone follow. Method How it works Google The phone's Google account. Apple Sign in with Apple, on iPhone and Android alike. Keep it on if you offer Google: Apple requires Sign in with Apple on iOS whenever Google is offered. Email Enter email and password (6+ characters) to sign in, or create an account. A new address is confirmed with a link: Check your email waits and carries on by itself once the link is tapped. Forgot password? emails a reset link. Phone Pick the country code, enter the number, then the 6-digit code sent by SMS (can be resent after a short wait). Can be switched off from the Admin Panel. Which methods appear is set in the app (Defaults & limits) and, for phone, in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›Features.

When a guest signs in, their coins, unlocks, progress and welcome bonus move into the account: Your history and bonus moved to your account. If they sign in to an account that already exists, the guest's history is merged into it.
documents.s: What happens to the guest's history

documents.t: App›Me›Edit profile: Name: others see it on their comments and reviews (at least 2 characters). Photo: choose from photos, take a photo, or remove it. The Me tab shows how they signed in ("Signed in with Google") and that your coins and unlocks are kept in your account.
App›Me›Settings›Sign out. Coins, unlocks and history stay in the account; signing in again brings them back. The app continues as a guest.

App›Me›Settings›Delete account removes the account, history, coins and unlocks for good. For security the viewer may be asked to sign in again first. VIP keeps billing until it's cancelled in the store Deleting the account doesn't cancel a VIP subscription: the store bills it. The app says so: Your VIP subscription is still active: cancel it in your app store so it stops billing.
If your team bans an account, the viewer sees This account has been suspended. Contact support if you think this is a mistake. and continues as a new guest; they can't sign in to the banned account.

The coin packs appear on the Rewards tab (under Top up) and in the coin store an unlock opens. On a pack Meaning 1,000 coins · +200 bonus The coins and the bonus on top. Popular / Best value Flags your team sets. ≈ 16 episodes About how many episodes it unlocks at the region's prices. First top-up: double coins A one-time offer: 300 + 300 bonus for $1.99 · once per account. Under the packs: Prices in INR · India, Paid coins never expire. Bonus coins expire after 7 days and are spent first. and Prices include tax. You confirm with Google Play next. Tap a pack. A guest is asked to sign in first. Confirm in Google Play or the App Store. The server checks the receipt, then: +1,200 coins added · 1,000 paid · 200 bonus, with the new balance. Coins fly to the balance. If the app closes mid-purchase, the purchase is picked up at the next start. Restore purchases (App›Me›Restore purchases or the wallet) checks the store for anything already bought: All set: 3 purchases checked, nothing missing.

App›Rewards›Wallet (or App›Me›Wallet). 123456789 1BalanceTotal coins. 2Paid coins“Never expire.” 3Bonus coins“Spent first · 100 expire Dec 1.” 4Top upOpens the coin packs. 5RestoreGets back purchases already made with this store account. 6Spend guard“0 of 300 coins today · 300 left.” Edit changes the daily limit. 7FilterAll, Coins in, Coins out. 8HistoryEvery coin in and out, with what it was for and the balance after. 9Append-onlyNothing is edited or deleted; refunds and corrections appear as new rows with a reason. The wallet: the balance with paid and bonus coins, Top up and Restore, the Spend guard card, the All / Coins in / Coins out filter and the history. The history is append-only: nothing is edited or deleted. Refunds and corrections appear as new rows with a reason you can see. Tap a row for its details: the change, paid and bonus coins, balance after, the episode, and a reference to copy when contacting support.

Spend guard is a daily limit on coins, like screen time, for spending. Pick Coins a day from the choices your team sets (the default is marked). Unlocks past the limit pause and ask first; auto-unlock never goes past it. If you switch the daily limit off in the Admin Panel, it disappears from the app.

Tap Comments in the player. Comments belong to an episode, and each can be tied to a moment in it: E7 · tap a time to jump there. Sort: Top, By moment, Newest. Write: Add a comment at 0:42…. Mark it as a Spoiler to hide it until tapped (Spoiler from E7 · tap to show). Reply, Like, Report, view more replies. Replies from the series' creator carry a Creator badge; replies from your team are marked Team. A Pinned comment stays on top. A comment with a blocked word, a link or a phone number waits for a quick check: Waiting for a quick check before others see it. (Only its author sees it meanwhile.)

On the series page, Rate once the viewer has reached episode 3: stars, and optional words. The score shown is weighted, so a few 5-star ratings can't outrank a series with thousands. The Reviews page lists them with helpful votes, the reviewer's episodes watched, and the creator's or team's reply. Viewers can mark a review helpful or report it. Reports and held posts go to your team on Comments & reviews. Comments and reviews can each be switched off in the Admin Panel.

The app opens on the splash screen: your logo draws itself, with the tagline Stories that hook you. Prices that don't. and, at the bottom, "Made by" your company. Meanwhile the app signs the viewer in as a guest (no account needed) and reads its configuration from your server.

Two short steps, then Home. No account is needed. 12345 1Step 1 of 2The bar on top shows how far along they are. 2SkipGoes straight on without picking. 3What hooks you?Pick three or more categories. Home is shaped around them, no account needed yet. 4A picked categoryYour categories, with their artwork, in the order set in the Admin Panel. 5Continue · 3 pickedShows “Pick 3 more” until enough are chosen. Onboarding step 1 of 2: What hooks you? with category tiles, three of them picked, and the Continue button. What hooks you? The viewer picks three or more categories. They feed Home's "Because you like…" rows. Watch in your language. They pick the app language from the languages you offer, and can turn on Data saver (start every episode at 360p, then sharpen; good on slow networks). Start watching. Home opens. You can change all of this in Settings. 12345 1Step 2 of 2Skip is still there, top right. 2Watch in your language“Pick the language eDrama speaks. You can switch any time.” 3The picked languageEach language in its own name and in English, with a tick on the one picked. 4Your languagesThe app languages you offer, from Settings › Regions & languages. 5Start watchingOpens Home. “You can change all of this in Settings.” Onboarding step 2 of 2: Watch in your language, with the languages you offer (English picked) and Start watching.

Screen When Back soon Maintenance mode is on. Shows your message. Your coins, unlocks and progress are safe. Update required The app's version is below the minimum supported version. The viewer must update; an Update now button opens the store. A new version is ready A newer version than theirs is marked latest. They can update or carry on. Set the versions in Admin Panel›Settings›App & support›App versions.
documents.s: Screens your server can show instead

documents.t: Home is built by your team in the Home builder, so what viewers see depends on your layout and on who they are (guest, signed in, VIP) and where they are (their region). Section What the viewer does Featured series (hero) Swipe through big cards; tap Play E1 (or Continue E7) or Details. Shows First 5 free or Complete · 24 eps. Continue watching Pick up where they stopped: E2 · 0:03 in, E3 ready to watch, E8 · 60 coins, or E9 drops soon. Rows and grids Tap a poster to open the series; See all opens the full list. Top 10 rows show Number 1, Number 2… Banners and promo cards Open a series, a category, the store, VIP, Rewards or a web page. Category chips Open a category's page. Notes Short lines from your team, such as the fair-pricing promise. Pull down to refresh. If nothing is published yet: Nothing to watch yet.

Tap the search button on Home. 123456 1Search box“Titles, categories, creators”. Results update as you type. 2ClearEmpties the box and goes back to Browse by category. 3CategoriesMatching categories. Tap one to browse it. 4A resultA series with its categories, episode count and rating. 5Complete / next drop“Complete”, or when new episodes come out, such as “New episodes every Thursday”. 6OpenOpens the series page. Search with “love” typed: matching categories, then series with their categories, episode count, rating, and Complete or the next drop. Before typing, Search shows Browse by category. Before typing: Recent searches (with Clear all), Browse by category and Trending. Results cover titles, categories and creators (creators only while creator pages are on). No results: Try a category, a title or a creator's name.

A category, or See all on a row, opens Browse: Filter: All, Complete, Ongoing. Sort by: Most popular, Newest, Top rated. The count of titles, then a grid of posters. Every genre (See all on a category row) shows all categories as tiles; tapping one flies its picture into the category's page.

Tap Created by on a series to open the creator's page: photo, Verified creator tick, followers, series count, bio, and their series. Follow to be told when they publish a new series. Share sends a link to their page. Creator pages can be switched off in the Admin Panel.
Links viewers share (…/s/12 for a series, …/c/name for a creator) open straight in the app on phones that have it, and on the website's share page otherwise. See Deep links.

The Library tab has three shelves: 123456 1SearchFinds a series in the Library. 2Watching · My List · UnlockedThe three shelves. 3A series in progress“E1 of 5 · Today”: the episode reached, when it was watched, and how far. 4ResumeBack where they stopped. 5Next episode lockedIts price shows instead. Tap to unlock it. 6Library tab The Library on Watching: series in progress with their poster, the episode reached and when, a progress bar, and Resume, or the price when the next episode is locked. Shelf What's there Watching Series in progress, newest first: E7 of 24, today/yesterday/days ago, Resume, the Next drop, or Episode 8 is locked. Empty: Start something from Home and it shows up here, right where you stopped. My List Series saved with the bookmark. Remove from My List to take one off. Unlocked Episodes unlocked and Series Passes bought: Series Pass · all 24 episodes, 5 episodes unlocked. Unlocks belong to your account, not this phone. They come back on any device you sign in to.

The bell on Home (and App›Me›Notifications) opens the inbox: new episodes of followed series, replies to the viewer's comments, new series from followed creators, offers, and VIP renewal reminders. Unread ones are marked; Mark all as read clears them. Tapping one opens what it's about (a reply opens the comments). You get at most 3 alerts a day. Pushes are held during quiet hours (23:00–08:00 by default) and arrive when they end.

In App›Me›Settings›Notifications: Switch Default Meaning Drop alerts On New episodes of series they follow, at most a few a day. Replies On When someone replies to their comment. Offers On Bonus coins and win-back offers, at most weekly. VIP renewal reminders Always on So a renewal never surprises you. To confirm The defaults for these switches are set by the server when an account is created; check them in the app after installing if they matter to you.

The viewer app is what your audience downloads from Google Play and the App Store. It's built for vertical episodes of 60 to 90 seconds: open a series, swipe up for the next episode, and unlock more when the free ones run out. It runs on Android 7+ and iOS 15+, on phones and tablets, in light and dark themes, and in every language you offer (including right-to-left ones). 12345678910 1Your logoFrom the app’s brand files. 2CoinsThe viewer’s balance (here the welcome bonus). Tap for the wallet. 3SearchTitles, categories and creators. 4NotificationsNew drops and replies, with an unread dot. 5Featured seriesThe hero slider from the Home builder. Swipe to browse; the dots show where you are. 6Schedule, kicker, categoriesThe series’ schedule line, its kicker and its categories, set on the title. 7Play E1 / ContinueStarts or resumes the series. 8My List · DetailsSave it to the Library, or open the series page. 9Rows of seriesBrowse by mood, Trending this week, Top 10 and more, in the order set in the Home builder. 10Tab barHome, Library, Rewards and Me. Rewards becomes Wallet when your team switches Rewards off. The Home tab: the logo, coin balance, search and notifications on top, the featured series slider with Play E1, My List and Details, the Browse by mood row, and the tab bar.

Tab What's there Home The sections your team built: featured series, Continue watching, rows, banners, categories. See Home & discovery. Library Watching (series in progress), My List (saved for later) and Unlocked (episodes and Series Passes you own). See Library & notifications. Rewards The daily spin, the streak, titles, ads for coins, the coin store and the wallet. When Rewards is switched off, this tab becomes Wallet. See Rewards. Me The profile, VIP, settings, help and account. See Settings & help. Swipe between tabs or tap them. Tapping the tab you're on scrolls it back to the top. Pressing back on any tab other than Home goes Home.

WatchThe vertical player, speed, quality, subtitles.→UnlockCoins, one ad, Series Pass or VIP.→EarnThe daily spin, streaks and ads for coins.→SubscribeVIP: everything unlocked, no ads.→TalkComments, ratings and reviews.→Get helpHelp & refunds, legal pages, settings.→

What's already loaded keeps working offline; a banner says You're offline. What's loaded still plays. Every list the app loads is saved on the phone and shown when the server can't be reached. Data saver (in onboarding and Settings) starts every episode at 360p, then sharpens, and loads the next episode later.

At each start, the app reads its configuration from your server: the app name and theme colour, which features are on, the viewer's region with its prices, and the languages. So most changes you make in the Admin Panel reach viewers without a new app release. If your server is in maintenance mode, viewers see a "Back soon" screen instead of the catalogue.

documents.t: The player shows one episode at a time, full screen, in portrait. Swipe up for the next episode, down for the previous. On a tablet or a wide window, the episode plays in a 9:16 column. 12345678910 1BackReturns to where the viewer came from. 2SubtitlesShown over the video in the viewer’s language when the episode has them. 3LikeDouble-tapping the video works too. 4CommentsComments on this episode, with the count. 5Episodes“1/3”: the episode list, with what is watched, locked or coming soon. 6ShareShares a link to this episode. 7MoreSpeed, quality, subtitles and Report a problem. 8Clean viewHides the buttons to watch the video alone. 9Series and episode“E1 · The Wedding That Wasn’t”. Tap for the series page. 10ProgressDrag to seek. Elapsed and total time on each side. The player during episode 1: Back, the subtitles over the video, the buttons on the right (Like, Comments, Episodes, Share, More, Clean view), the series and episode at the bottom, and the progress bar.

Control What it does Tap Play or pause. Double-tap Like the episode. Press and hold Plays at 2× speed while held. Clean view Hides the buttons; the way out fades after 2 seconds and comes back with a tap. More › Speed 0.75×, Normal, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2×. More › Quality Auto (adaptive, up to 720p without VIP), or a fixed quality the video has: 1080p (VIP only), 720p, 480p, 360p. With data saver on, Auto starts at 360p. More › Subtitles The languages the episode has, or Off. By default, subtitles follow the app language. More › Report a problem Video won't play, Sound or sync is off, Subtitles are wrong, Inappropriate content, Something else. Thanks. The team will take a look. Reports reach the Review queue.

When an episode ends, an Up next card counts down 3 seconds and plays the next one (Play now to skip the wait, or dismiss it). Autoplay can be turned off in App›Me›Settings›Autoplay next episode. If the next episode is locked, the card says Unlock for 60 coins or See unlock options. If it isn't out yet: E9 drops 12 Dec with Remind me (follows the series).

A locked episode shows Unlock for 60 coins (≈ $0.59), one short ad, VIP or the Series Pass. and See unlock options. See Unlocking episodes. With auto-unlock on, the next episode unlocks with coins as it starts, never past the daily limit.

Episodes your team added from YouTube play in YouTube's own player with nothing drawn over it, and are always free. A line says Plays from YouTube. By watching you agree to YouTube's Terms of Service. with Watch on YouTube.

The player can't be captured: Android blocks screenshots and recordings, and iOS hides the video while the screen is recorded or mirrored (Screen recording is on. Episodes can't be recorded.). This is on by default (Defaults & limits). The screenshot on this page was taken from a documentation build with it switched off.

The app reports progress as the viewer watches. It drives Continue watching, views and stats, and VIP minutes for creators' earnings. An episode counts as watched at 90%. The screen stays awake while playing.

The Rewards tab brings viewers back every day: a free daily spin that always pays, a streak that grows with each day, titles to earn, and ads for coins. All coins earned here are bonus coins. 12345678 1Your coinsPaid and bonus coins, and when bonus coins expire. 2Top upOpens the coin packs. 3StreakA dot for each day of the week; today is ringed. “Spin today to start your streak.” 4Streak flameLit while the streak is alive. 5Next title“1 more day to Extra”: the next streak title, set in the Admin Panel. 6Prize wheelHere 8 prizes from 10 to 200 coins. Every spin pays. 7Spin for freeOnce a day. See the odds sits under it. 8Watch an ad · +15 coins“6 of 6 left today · 30 s at most · never a playable ad.” The Rewards tab for a new viewer: the coin balance with Top up, the streak card with its flame, the daily spin with the prize wheel, and Earn more with Watch an ad.

Tap Spin for free. The wheel lifts above the page and spins; tap the wheel to skip ahead. It lands on a prize, such as +50, about 1 episode. VIP members see VIP ×2 and win double. Collect: the coins fly to the balance. See the odds shows every prize's chance. Your team sets the prizes and chances per region (Ads & rewards).

Each day's spin adds a day to the streak. Today isn't counted yet. Spin the wheel to keep your 7-day streak. Miss a day and the streak restarts, unless a shield saves it. Streak shields: earned every 7 days of streak (default), up to 2 held. A shield covers one missed day by itself: Your shield saved your 12-day streak. Shields are never sold. Titles: names earned at the viewer's best streak and kept for good (Extra, Understudy, Scene Stealer, Plot Twister, Drama Champion, Drama Royalty, Drama Legend, Hall of Famer), each paying its bonus coins once. A new title appears with a celebration; Titles lists them all with the days to go. The top title shows You've reached the very top. Share the streak as a card: 12 days in a row on eDrama 🔥 Plot Twister.
Watch an ad pays bonus coins (15 by default) per ad, up to the daily limit, 30 seconds at most, never a playable ad. Coins arrive once AdMob confirms the ad (Your coins are on the way).
After a reward, a Keep watching card offers the next locked episode the new coins can unlock.

If your team switches Rewards off, the tab becomes Wallet, with the balance, coin packs and history. note Bonus coins expire (7 days by default) and are always spent before paid coins. Spin once a day for free. Every spin pays bonus coins, which are spent first and expire soon after you earn them.

Tapping a series opens its page. The poster flies into place, so it feels instant even while the rest loads. 123456789 1Title and detailsKicker, name and subtitle, then the rating, age rating, episode count and when new episodes come out. 2RatingsOpens the reviews. 3My ListSaves it in the Library. 4Follow“We’ll tell you when new episodes drop.” 5ShareShares a link to the series. 6What it costsBefore anything is paid: the free episodes, the coins to catch up on the rest, and the Series Pass. 7Series PassAll episodes plus future drops, in one purchase. 8The price, plainlyCoins per episode with the money it comes to, “never more”, or one short ad per episode. 9Play E1 / ContinueStarts or resumes in the player. The episode list is further down the page. A series page: the poster with the kicker, title, rating, age rating, episode count and schedule line; My List, Follow and Share; the What it costs card; the synopsis; and Play E1.

The cost card shows the full price before the viewer spends anything, in coins and in their own money: Part Example Free E1–E5, no ads to start Catch up / Finish The coins to unlock the released episodes they haven't unlocked yet Series Pass ≈ $1.49 · all 24, when the series has one The rule 60 coins (≈ $0.59) an episode, never more. Or 1 ad ≤ 30 s per episode, watched to the end. Price locked Shown once they've started: their price can't rise. The card changes for VIP members (Included with VIP · No ads · Every released episode is unlocked for you), for viewers with a Series Pass (Series Pass active · Paid in full), and when every released episode is free.
Each tile shows the episode's state: Free, Unlocked, Locked · 60 coins, Watched, Now (where they are), or Not yet released. Tapping a locked one opens the unlock sheet.

About: the synopsis (More / Less) and Created by, with the creator's followers. Ratings & reviews: the score, reviews, and Rate once they've reached episode 3 (Comments & reviews). More like this: similar series. A series limited to some regions isn't shown to viewers elsewhere; a link to it says it isn't available in their region.

Prices From the country you're in: their region and currency. Invite friends Shares the app: I'm watching short dramas on eDrama. When a viewer reaches a locked episode, the Keep watching sheet opens with every way to unlock it, the price in coins and in money, and their balance, before anything is charged. 123456789 1Keep watching“E2 · Five Years Gone · The Heiress Returns”. 2Unlock with coinsThe price in coins and money. Bonus coins are spent first. 3Watch 1 ad“Unlocks when it ends · up to 30 s · 6 of 6 left today.” Free: 1 ad = 1 episode. 4Series Pass“All 3 episodes + future drops”, with what it saves. 5VIP“Everything unlocked · no ads · cancel any time”, with the price per period. 6BalancePaid and bonus coins, and when bonus coins expire. 7Top upOpens the coin packs without leaving the sheet. 8Auto-unlockUnlocks the next episodes as they start, only up to the daily spend limit. 9Unlock E2 · 60 coinsThe button changes with the option picked. The Keep watching sheet for episode 2: Unlock with coins (selected), Watch 1 ad, Series Pass and VIP, the balance with paid and bonus coins, Auto-unlock, and the Unlock button.

Option How it works Coins Pays the series' price per episode. Bonus coins are spent first, earliest expiry first, then paid coins. The viewer is charged exactly the price shown. Watch 1 ad One rewarded ad, 30 seconds at most, unlocks one episode once it's watched to the end and AdMob confirms it. Each region has a daily limit (Today's ad unlocks are used up. Back tomorrow.). Only on series that allow ads. Series Pass One price in coins for every episode, including future drops, with the saving shown. VIP Opens the VIP page: every series unlocked, no ads. Free and already-unlocked episodes simply play. Unlocks belong to the account, so they come back on any phone the viewer signs in to.
E8 unlocked · 60 coins · 20 bonus, 40 paid, the coins fly to the balance, and the episode plays. A Series Pass shows Every episode of Heiress Returns is yours.

You need 15 more coins for E8. Top up and it unlocks straight after. Top up to unlock opens the coin store on You need 15 more coins for this episode; once the coins land, the unlock finishes by itself.

We couldn't confirm the ad yet. The episode unlocks by itself once AdMob confirms it. AdMob is slow; nothing more to do. The ad didn't finish, so this episode is still locked. AdMob didn't confirm it.

With Auto-unlock next episodes on, the next locked episode is unlocked with coins as it starts: Auto-unlocked E9 · 60 coins. It's off by default, and it never goes past the daily spend limit. Change it in the sheet or in App›Me›Settings›Auto-unlock.

Viewers choose how many coins they may spend a day (100, 300, 600 or 1,000 by default; 300 to start). When an unlock would go past it: You've hit today's limit. You set 300 coins a day. You've used 280. This unlock costs 60 coins. Spend guard paused it, so nothing is charged without you deciding. They can Raise today to 360 and unlock, or Watch 1 ad instead. Set the limit in App›Rewards›Wallet›Spend guard. The Series Pass isn't held to the daily limit.

The website and the Admin Panel need to know about each other: the website needs your server's address, to read its content; the Admin Panel needs the website's address, to show previews and to tell it about changes. The two share a refresh secret, so only your Admin Panel can ask the website to refresh.
documents.s: Connect the website to the Admin Panel

documents.t: They go in .env.local on your computer, or in your host's environment variables (on Vercel: Settings › Environment Variables). Variable Needed What it is EDRAMA_API_URL Yes Your server's address without /api, such as https://admin.your-domain.com. Must be https:// (plain http:// only works for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and *.test). REVALIDATE_SECRET Recommended The refresh secret from the Admin Panel (below). Without it, a publish shows within 5 minutes instead of at once. At least 32 characters, which the Admin Panel's secret always is. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL No The website's own address, used only while the Admin Panel has none set. EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS No Extra hosts images may come from, comma-separated, when your files live on S3 or a CDN, such as my-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com,cdn.your-domain.com. Your server's host is always allowed. EDRAMA_SCRIPT_HOSTS No Extra https:// origins allowed to serve analytics scripts, for self-hosted Plausible or Umami. Plausible, Umami Cloud and Google Analytics are allowed already. EDRAMA_FRAME_ORIGINS No Other addresses your Admin Panel opens at, comma-separated, that may show the website's live preview. Your server's own address always may. APP_ADS_TXT No The lines of /app-ads.txt, which AdMob checks on the developer website listed in your store pages. Copy them from AdMob › Apps › app-ads.txt, one per line (or separated by \n). Without it, /app-ads.txt isn't served. Rebuild after changing them EDRAMA_API_URL, EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS, EDRAMA_SCRIPT_HOSTS and EDRAMA_FRAME_ORIGINS are built into the site's security headers and image settings. After changing any of them, build and deploy the website again. Files on Amazon S3? If you moved files to S3 or another S3-compatible bucket in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video, add the bucket's host (or its Public URL host) to EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS, or posters won't show on the website.

Open the Connection tab. Go to Admin Panel›Content›Website and open Connection & history. It shows This server's address for the website (EDRAMA_API_URL): that's the value for EDRAMA_API_URL. Set the Website address. Enter where visitors open the website, such as https://www.your-domain.com, and choose Save address. It's used for previews, canonical links, the sitemap, share pictures, and to tell the website about changes. Make the refresh secret. Choose Make a secret (once one exists, the button reads Make a new secret, and the old one stops working). The secret is shown once: copy it into the website's REVALIDATE_SECRET, then redeploy (or restart) the website so it reads the new value. Permission area: Website View Open the page Edit Change the content Changing the Website address or making a secret needs a role with Settings › Edit (Roles & access).

Change a heading on the Sections tab and choose Publish. Open the website: the new heading shows within a minute. If it only shows after about 5 minutes: the secret doesn't match: make a new one, paste it again and redeploy; the server's queue isn't running: the refresh is sent as a background job (Cron & queues); or the website runs on localhost or a private network address, which never receives the call.

Each time you publish, or switch the website on or off, your server sends POST <Website address>/api/revalidate with a small JSON body, signed with the refresh secret (an HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Edrama-Signature header). The website refuses calls that aren't signed with its REVALIDATE_SECRET or are more than 5 minutes old. The call is only sent to a public address, never to localhost or a private network, and if it fails nothing breaks: pages rebuild by themselves every 5 minutes.

The website is a standard Next.js app. Pick where it runs: VercelThe easiest: no server to manage, every push deploys, and the free Hobby plan is enough to start (check Vercel’s terms for commercial use).→Your own Node.js serverA VPS, a cloud VM or a host with Node.js app support, behind your own web server and certificate.→ It can't be a static export The website needs a running Node.js process: it rebuilds pages in the background, answers the refresh call and serves the /.well-known files. Uploading the build folder to plain shared hosting won't work.

Pick where the website runs: Vercel Your own Node.js server Before you start​ A Vercel account. The website's code (edrama-website-<version>.zip, unzipped) in a Git repository you own (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket), or the Vercel CLI on your computer. Your Admin Panel installed and reachable over https://. Steps​ Create the project. In Vercel, choose Add New › Project and import the website's repository. Vercel detects Next.js by itself (the repository's vercel.json says so too); no build settings need changing. Add the settings. Before the first deploy, open Environment Variables and add the variables from Connect to the Admin Panel: at least EDRAMA_API_URL and REVALIDATE_SECRET, for Production and Preview. Deploy. From now on, every push to your production branch (usually main) deploys the live site, and every other branch gets its own preview address. After changing an environment variable, redeploy (Deployments › Redeploy) so the site picks it up. Add your domain. In the project, open Settings › Domains, add your domain (for example your-domain.com and www.your-domain.com) and point its DNS records at Vercel exactly as that screen shows. Tell the Admin Panel. Set the same address in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Connection & history › Website address. Deploying from your computer instead​ The website includes scripts/deploy.sh, a Bash script (macOS, Linux, or WSL on Windows) that uses the Vercel CLI. It runs npm ci, npm run lint and npm run build before deploying. Terminal, in the website folder npm install --global vercel vercel link # once: link the folder to your Vercel project scripts/deploy.sh # a preview deployment, with its own address scripts/deploy.sh --prod # the live site Any server with Node.js 20.9 or newer works. Set the settings from Connect to the Admin Panel in .env.local or the server's environment. They're read when the site builds and when it runs, so after changing one, build and restart again. Build it. Server, in the website folder npm ci npm run build Start it. It listens on port 3000; use PORT=8080 npm run start for another port. Server npm run start Keep it running. Use a process manager such as PM2 or a systemd service, so it restarts after a crash or a reboot: Server npm install --global pm2 pm2 start npm --name edrama-website -- run start pm2 save && pm2 startup Put it behind HTTPS. Point your web server at the Node.js port as a reverse proxy, with an SSL certificate for your domain (Let's Encrypt's certbot --nginx -d your-domain.com -d www.your-domain.com adds one to nginx). /etc/nginx/sites-available/edrama-website server { server_name your-domain.com www.your-domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; } } Tell the Admin Panel. Set the Website address in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Connection & history.

Open your domain: the home page shows your sections. Open https://your-domain.com/sitemap.xml and https://your-domain.com/robots.txt: the files search engines read. Publish a small change in the Admin Panel: it shows within a minute (Check the refresh).

eDrama comes with a public website: a landing page, a page for every series, category and creator, plus a sitemap, robots.txt and llms.txt. It helps people find your series on Google and leads every visitor to the app. Admin PanelContent › Website Publish Website API/api/v1/website… Your websiteNext.js You edit and publish in the Admin Panel; the website reads it from your server.

The website is a Next.js app, hosted separately from the Admin Panel: on Vercel, or any server that runs Node.js. It has no database of its own. It reads your server's public website API (/api/v1/website…), which holds no viewer data and needs no keys. Everything it shows is edited in Admin Panel›Content›Website: sections, layouts, texts, header and footer, theme, languages, search text and social links (Website). The name, logos and theme colour come from Admin Panel›Settings›Branding, so the app, the panels and the website always match. Series are shown, never played: every poster and button leads to the app. Pages are built once, shared by every visitor and rebuilt in the background every 5 minutes. When you Publish in the Admin Panel, your server tells the website to refresh at once. If your server can't be reached, the website keeps showing its last good copy.

Install the Admin Panel first. The website needs a running server (Server installation). Run it on your computer (below), to check it works. Connect it to your Admin Panel: the server's address, the website's address and the refresh secret. Deploy it to Vercel or your own Node.js server. Fill in the content in Admin Panel›Content›Website, then Publish. Address What runs there your-domain.com (or www.) This website admin.your-domain.com The server: Admin Panel, Creator Portal and API

Open the folder. Unzip edrama-website-<version>.zip from your download and open the folder in a terminal or an editor such as VS Code. Install the packages. Terminal, in the website folder npm install Create your settings file and set at least EDRAMA_API_URL (every setting): Terminal cp .env.example .env.local .env.local EDRAMA_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 Start it. Terminal npm run dev Open http://localhost:3000. The home page shows your app name and the sections from Admin Panel›Content›Website. For the Admin Panel's live preview, set Admin Panel›Content›Website › Connection & history › Website address to http://localhost:3000. On your computer, a publish shows within 5 minutes: the instant refresh is only sent to a public address.
Terminal npm run lint npm run build Both should finish without errors.

Address Page / Home, built from your sections in Admin Panel›Content›Website /series All series, with category chips /series/<slug> One series: banner, poster, synopsis, creator, an Open in app button and the store buttons /categories and /categories/<slug> All categories, and the series in one /creators/<slug> A creator's profile and series /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt For search engines /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt For AI assistants, only when you allow AI crawlers and llms.txt (Admin Panel›Content›Website › Search & statistics) /app-ads.txt For AdMob, only when APP_ADS_TXT is set (Connect) /s/<id>, /c/<handle> The app's own share links: they redirect to the series or creator page The website shows what viewers in your default region see. A series limited to other regions isn't on it, so include the default region if a series should appear on the website.

The default language is at plain addresses: /series/…, /categories/…. Every other language turned on in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Look & languages lives under its code: /hi/series/…, /ar/series/…. Only languages already offered in the app (Admin Panel›Settings›Regions & languages) can be picked. Right-to-left languages such as Arabic are laid out right to left. Visitors switch language from the header when Show a language menu in the header is on, and light or dark when Let visitors switch between light and dark is on. Website texts are translated on the Translations tab. Series and category names use the translations already entered for the app. The sitemap lists every page in every language, with links between the language versions.

The website serves the two files phones read to open links in your app instead of the browser: /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android) /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS) Both are filled from your server's app settings, so they stay empty until the server knows your app: set EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE, EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 and EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID in the server's .env. Your app must list the website's domain too, as websiteHost on Android and an applinks: entry on iOS (Deep links).
